title: Sean McVay laughs as he says he's tempted to ask assistant coach Robert Woods to suit up
summary: He didn't sound completely serious, but Rams coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that he talked to assistant wide receivers coach Robert Woods about whether he could suit up and play while receivers Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all out with injuries.
full_text: He didn't sound completely serious, but Rams coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that he talked to assistant wide receivers coach Robert Woods about whether he could suit up and play while receivers Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all out with injuries. McVay was asked during his press conference whether he has talked to the 34-year-old Woods, who was a receiver for the Rams for five years, about potentially playing again. “I have, yes," McVay answered with a laugh. McVay acknowledged that there are Collective Bargaining Agreement rules against a coach becoming a player, but he said Woods is still in great shape and it would be fun to give it a try. "I've looked at him, and the way he looks out there, I've definitely been tempted," McVay said. "I think that’d be a violation of the CBA. I don’t know what he’d have to do, but he looks damn good and still is smooth out there. Very tempting." Woods was cut by the Steelers before the 2025 season and hasn't played since, and he announced his retirement and signed a one-day contract with the Rams in February of 2026. Realistically, even with his intimate knowledge of the Rams' offense, he probably wouldn't be able to contribute as much on the field as whatever receiver the Rams could add off waivers or another team's practice squad. If Woods and the Rams actually wanted him to become an active player, it wouldn't be as simple as signing him to the active roster, as the league has rules preventing that. Players on the reserve-retired list have to pass through waivers before they can join a team. And the NFL generally doesn't allow coaches to become players: In 2020, when the Broncos lost all their quarterbacks to covid, they asked the league office if they could activate one of their assistant coaches and were told no. In 2009, Eagles coach Andy Reid wanted to play coaching intern Matt Nagy at quarterback in a preseason game and was also told by the league that he couldn't. So the idea of Woods playing receiver for the Rams is probably not going to get any kind of serious consideration. Even if, with all the Rams' injuries, it's tempting.
author: Michael David Smith

title: For Week 9, Next Gen Stats outpaced the McAfee alt cast again
summary: The ESPN announcement of the viewership for a given Monday night game always requires a careful look for any information about the viewership of the multiple weekly alt casts on the Disney-owned networks.
full_text: ''' The ESPN announcement of the viewership for a given Monday night game always requires a careful look for any information about the viewership of the multiple weekly alt casts on the Disney-owned networks. This week, the release presented only the total viewership for all platforms, at 21.7 million. Nothing was said about the total or individual numbers for the McAfee alt cast on ESPN2 or the Next Gen Stats version on NFL Network. Andrew Marchand of The Athletic has gotten the numbers . For the Next Gen Stats alt cast, 499,000 tuned in. For the McAfee ensemble, the number was 406,000. The final tally gives Next Gen Stats a 2-0 lead over the McAfee option. The gap was more narrow this time around; when they first squared off for the Week 6 Commanders-49ers game, NFLN attracted 469,000 and ESPN2 got 351,000 . (ESPN2 is in roughly 70 million homes; NFL Network's distribution is at or below 50 million.) The total viewership for that game was 17.9 million. With Bills-Vikings beating that figure by 21.2 percent, Next Gen Stats was up 6.3 percent over Week 6 and the McAfee cast increased by 15.6 percent. Of the total audience for the game, 2.2 percent watched NFL Network and 1.87 percent watched ESPN2. Which raises, once again, a one-word question: Why? The Monday night alt casts don't draw in new viewers. It's added expense, with no extra revenue for the broader operation. (Unless there's a tangible benefit to siphoning viewers from ABC/ESPN for the other channels.) Ultimately, it's a zero-sum game. With alt casts, Bills-Vikings viewership was 21.7 million. Without alt casts, Bills-Vikings viewership undoubtedly would have been 21.7 million. And that's why the various ABC affiliates are upset that Disney will have a full slate of alt casts for Super Bowl LXI. The total number will be the total number, if the game is on one network or twenty. The alt casts will rob the Peter of ABC to pay the Paul of the various other platforms.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay optimistic that Trent McDuffie will play Sunday vs. Cardinals
summary: Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie has missed three games this season and was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice with a back injury, but the outlook for his ability to play Sunday against the Cardinals is good.
full_text: Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie has missed three games this season and was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice with a back injury, but the outlook for his ability to play Sunday against the Cardinals is good. Coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that McDuffie wants to go and the only question for the Rams is whether he'll be able to do everything he needs to do in a game, which can't always be simulated on the practice field. "He's feeling good. We're optimistic this week he will be able to go," McVay said. "He's so damn tough, but you want to make sure that you're putting him in a position to have a successful outcome, and he is making really good progress. It's really just being able to deal with the functional movements and some of the unpredictability." Injuries have taken a major toll on the Rams this season, and McDuffie is one of the big-name players in Los Angeles who hasn't made the impact the team was hoping to see, in large part because he hasn't been fully healthy. But when asked about McDuffie on Wednesday, McVay answered, "Hopefully this is the week."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Packers-Patriots on Fox leads Week 9 with 25.7 million
summary: As NFL games go, the 4:25 p.m.
full_text: As NFL games go, the 4:25 p.m. ET window routinely has the biggest audience of the week — larger than any prime-time game. That was true on Sunday, when 25.7 million on average tuned in for the window headlined by the Packers shredding the Patriots, 45-27. It was the most-watched telecast of the week on any network, besting the Bills-Vikings game on Monday night by 4.0 million. As the NFL is looks for more windows, and potentially heads toward more Wednesday night (and possibly Tuesday night) games, 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday continues to be the best slot. Currently, that window is shared by CBS and Fox, with one or the other having the game in most weeks. (A few times per year, they both have 4:25 p.m. ET games on the same day.) With all windows (except for Monday night, which is available a year later) opening up in 2030, it will be interesting to see whether the NFL decides to stop splitting all of Sunday afternoon between two networks and selling 4:25 p.m. ET as a weekly package. Given the audiences generated by that window, it would easily generate the biggest rights fee of any of them.
author: Mike Florio

title: Broncos, Chargers announce Daiyan Henley will not be traded after all
summary: More than 24 hours after the NFL trade deadline, the trade of Henley from the Charges to the Broncos was canceled.
full_text: '' Just before Tuesday afternoon's trade deadline, the Chargers agreed to trade linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos. Late on Wednesday night, the trade was canceled. Both the Chargers and the Broncos have announced that Henley will remain with the Chargers. Neither team explained why, but typically that would happen after the trade deadline only if the player failed his physical. "The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized," the Broncos said in a statement. "We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward." The Chargers posted " Welcome back, Daiyan " on social media, about 30 hours after posting, "Thank you, Daiyan" to officially announce the trade. According to ESPN, Henley was at the Broncos' facility on Wednesday and took a physical, so presumably the Broncos' medical staff decided to nix the trade. Henley did suffer a shoulder injury in Week 8 against the Rams, but he was a full participant in practice the next week and played well in Week 9 against the Texans. There have been no indications that he has had any other health concerns. The Broncos had agreed to send a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chargers for Henley, who is in the final year of his rookie contract and is slated to become an unrestricted free agent in March.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Keenan Allen says his beef with Mike Evans is in the past
summary: Keenan Allen says his beef with Mike Evans is in the past.
full_text: Keenan Allen says his beef with Mike Evans is in the past. Allen joined Evans in the 49ers' wide receivers room this week after a trade from the Colts. "We squashed it a long time ago," Allen said Wednesday, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "Everybody wants to bring it back up, obviously. But no, Mike's a hell of a player. He’s probably better than me at this point." In a memorable 2020 back-and-forth on social media , Allen and Evans engaged in a spirited debate about who was the better wide receiver. Allen was ranked 77th on the NFL Top 100 that season. Tyreek Hill ranked 22nd, Evans 30th and Chris Godwin 38th. Allen argued that he was better than Hill, Evans and Godwin. "Ok I’m tired of biten my tongue...@cheetah @MikeEvans13_ @chrisgoodwin... ( and the list goes on) ARE NOT a better receiver than me! Faster than me...every day of the week but separation..CHILD PLEASE!" Allen wrote in his post. Evans responded, "You tagged the wrong Chris Godwin lol and don’t be mad at us we ain’t make the rankings or care about em. I like the confidence but be realistic you not on my level bro." Allen, who is in his 14th season, has 1,095 catches for 12,402 yards and 71 touchdowns and is a six-time Pro Bowler. Evans, who is in his 13th season, has 893 catches for 13,472 yards and 111 touchdowns and is a six-time Pro Bowler.
author: Charean Williams

title: Dianna Russini's return includes no specifics about multiple controversies
summary: As expected, Dianna Russini made her return to sports media on Wednesday, with a one-hour show platformed by an illegal offshore sports book.
full_text: ' As expected, Dianna Russini made her return to sports media on Wednesday, with a one-hour show platformed by an illegal offshore sports book . It's hardly a prime gig, but her " crisis publicist " managed to create plenty of hype — and to finagle a puff piece with People.com that included no questions about the circumstances that prompted Russini's resignation from The Athletic . In September, the New York Post reported that Russini would " share her side of the scandal upon taking her next job." She hasn't, and she didn't in the debut episode of her new show. Technical difficulties delayed the release of the first episode, which was supposed to be live but seemed to be entirely pre-recorded. (The company blamed the glitch on a "record-breaking audience." Comparable to what?) Once the episode finally appeared, it featured three guests (none of whom are current players or coaches), preceded by a segment in which she addressed the future of Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Which, from an editorial standpoint, is hardly the top story in the NFL on the day after the trade deadline. There was nothing new or particularly insightful about Jackson. It was a summary of the facts that anyone who has been paying attention to the situation already knew, with a not-groundbreaking assertion that the Ravens want to keep him beyond 2026. More significantly, the wooly mammoth in the mud room was not addressed. The overriding message was that she went away for a while, she went through some things, and now she's back. For anyone who doesn't know the story, she said nothing that would even begin to shed light on it. If it's going to be an opinions-and-interviews show, that's fine. If she's going to include the reporting of facts about the NFL, the credibility question can't be ignored. And this isn't about the relationship (or whatever it was) with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. It's about how she responded to it. She issued a strident denial when the Post published the photos of the two of them at a resort in Arizona. One week later, she abruptly resigned from her position at The Athletic , complaining that "commentators in various media have engaged in self-feeding speculation that is simply unmoored from the facts ." In the months since making that assertion, she hasn't shared her own version of the facts. In her kid-gloves interview with People.com, Russini said that the “lies became so out of control.” Without identifying even one of the alleged lies. Her nothing-to-see-here position was undermined by Vrabel himself, who abandoned his initial position that the initial photos "show a completely innocent interaction and any suggestion otherwise is laughable ." Then came another group of photos , from March 2020, which had a distinct know-it-when-you-see-it vibe as to the specific nature of the relationship. That prompted Vrabel to step away from the team for the all-important third day of the draft, in order to attend counseling with his family. So, to date, Russini's official position is that it was all a big nothing. Vrabel’s words and actions make it clear that it was something, whatever it was. (That boat-trip video didn't help much, either.) Beyond the fact that The Athletic concluded, following an internal investigation, that "Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic ’s standards," the situation creates clear questions of credibility. Put simply, and bluntly, can the audience believe what she says? That leads to the other issue, which has been largely overlooked in connection with her return to sports media — if a one-hour show hosted by an illegal offshore sports book even counts as that. In February, she told the story of being pulled over for texting while driving. She claimed that she FaceTimed a current head coach to get her out of the ticket. And, based on the bodycam footage released by the local authorities, that contention was flat-out false . Forget the relationship with Vrabel. All insiders have compromised their journalistic integrity, in one way or another. The interests of the audience often take a back seat to the broader chess match of getting and staying in position to get "scoops" (which usually come in the form of a five-minute heads-up before a transaction is announced). Punches are pulled. Relevant stories are overlooked or downplayed. Favors are done for sources. It's one thing to be compromised. It's another thing to have real issues when it comes to telling the truth. Because the fundamental premise of anyone who is engaged in reporting of any kind is that they are at all times telling the truth . Even in post-truth America, it's a standard that should never be relaxed. Russini's credibility has been damaged by her denials regarding the relationship (whatever it was) with Vrabel, and by Vrabel's actions that undercut her denials. Moreover, the casual, nonchalant spinning of a phony yarn about FaceTiming a coach to get out of a ticket makes it even harder to believe anything she says. That's why I said last Saturday on #PFTPM that we'll be ignoring any of her reports until her credibility is somehow restored, if that's even possible at this point. In this business, it would be very easy to make assertions and couch them as news from an unnamed source. When someone has not one but two concrete instances of clear issues when it comes to telling the truth, it would be irresponsible for us to blindly accept any reports from that reporter and to use them here. It's that simple. People may not like some of the things we report, but the goal at all times is to be fully and completely honest with the audience. Part of that duty of honesty includes being brutally honest that the word of someone who has, in multiple ways, damaged her own credibility simply can't be trusted here.
author: Mike Florio

title: NC State moves even closer to hiring Philip Rivers
summary: Rivers, who played for the Wolfpack from 1999 through 2003, is now poised to coach them.
full_text: ' Don't expect Philip Rivers to come out of retirement again this season. He'll be busy. Via ESPN, the NC State board of trustees is expected to finalize a contract that will make Rivers the next head coach of the Wolfpack. Rivers played for NC State from 1999 through 2003. He was the fourth overall pick in the 2004 draft, technically of the Giants. He was traded to the Chargers (with Eli Manning going to New York), and Rivers played for the Chargers through 2019. He spent 2020 with the Colts, and he unexpectedly returned late in the 2025 season to play for the Colts again. Rivers became a high-school coach in Alabama in 2021. He has never coached at the college or pro level, but he interviewed for the Bills' head-coaching job. It's not known whether he still aspires to coach at the NFL level. As he gets experience at NC State — and if he does well — buzz could build for a shot with an NFL team. For now, he'll be returning to the place where he played college football. His name surfaced almost immediately after long-time coach Dave Doeren was fired last month. Along the way, NC State interviewed fellow former NC State quarterback (and NFL quarterback and current CBS analyst) Russell Wilson.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vikings are in the four-quarterback club, for now
summary: The Vikings' addition of quarterback Kirk Cousins comes with a surprising decision on the back end.
full_text: The Vikings' addition of quarterback Kirk Cousins comes with a surprising decision on the back end. Minnesota has not released any of its other quarterbacks. Giving the Vikings four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. With Cousins on the team, Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer remain. It's amazing, frankly, that Wentz hasn't been cut; Monday night's performance shows that he should no longer be playing in the NFL. Or the UFL. Or the CFL. Or any organization that ends with "FL." It's hard to imagine Wentz sticking around for long. The Vikings possibly have decided to keep Wentz for now, given that Murray still has a hamstring injury. Regardless, the soft benching of Murray has now become a hard benching. And the hard benching of Wentz inevitably will become a pink slip. They're all in with Cousins. The longer he plays, the better chance the Vikings have to make it to the playoffs. It starts on Sunday, despite coach Kevin O'Connell being coy about it. Cousins undoubtedly will play. That's why he's there. Even if he's not 100-percent ready, a less-than-prepared Cousins is better than the other options they have.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kamario Taylor lands $7.5 million deal to return to Mississippi State
summary: One man's chaos is another man's ca-ching.
full_text: One man's chaos is another man's ca-ching. After years of being stuck in a system that prevented them from getting fair (or any) value for their skills, efforts, and/or sacrifices, college football players are finally getting paid. And one of them is setting a new bar. Via On3.com, Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is finalizing a $7.5 million deal to return in 2027. With incentives, it could yield as much as $9 million. With Taylor under center, the Bulldogs started 4-0. Taylor has since suffered a season-ending injury. Before the injury, Taylor was regarded as one of the favorites to win the Heisman Trophy. While the development will prompt the pearl-clutchers to try to parlay the situation into more political momentum for the Protect College Sports Act, it's a reflection of the free market at work. Which is fine for those in positions of wealth and power, when it comes to their own financial position. When someone else is reaping the benefits of capitalism in a way that complicates the lives of those who have to balance the books (and to pry cash from boosters who support the NIL funds), it becomes a problem. And so they'll do whatever they have to do to roll back the gains players have made. Because free enterprise is desirable only when the people in control practice it. When the workers start getting paid according to their worth, it becomes a crisis.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bills-Vikings racks up 21.7 million for Monday Night Football
summary: The game itself was not much fun to watch, except for Bills fans.
full_text: The game itself was not much fun to watch, except for Bills fans. That didn't impact the viewership. Via ESPN, 21.7 million watched the Week 9 game between the Bills and Vikings on ABC, ESPN, ESPN2, NFL Network, and ESPN Deportes. The announcement doesn't mention the audience for any of the two alt casts — the McAfee gathering on ESPN2 or the Next Gen Stats edition on NFL Network — either individually or collectively. Next Monday night's game features the Chargers at the Ravens. It won't do 21.7 million viewers, primarily since the 0-8 Chargers have become entirely unwatchable. After that, it's Bengals-Commanders, Panthers-Buccaneers, Cowboys-Seahawks, Steelers-Jaguars, Patriots-Chiefs, Giants-Lions, and Texans-Packers. And, yes, the season is already slipping away. Enjoy it while it lasts. Except when it's Chargers-Ravens.
author: Mike Florio

title: Matthew Stafford a full participant Wednesday; Myles Garrett limited
summary: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (right elbow) had full participation on Wednesday.
full_text: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (right elbow) had full participation on Wednesday. Stafford went on the injury report with his injury a week ago, but he played all 75 offensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Commanders. Outside linebacker Myles Garrett (knee) was limited after playing 37 of 62 defensive snaps in his return Sunday, when he had three sacks. He had not played since Week 1 after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his knee the following week. Offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring), wide receiver Puka Nacua (knee/toe), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), safety Kam Curl (toe) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not practice. Tight end Davis Allen (oblique), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) and long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) were limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Daniel Jones is "not happy" with Colts' roster purge
summary: The Colts had a mini-fire sale in recent weeks, trading away four starters for future assets.
full_text: The Colts had a mini-fire sale in recent weeks, trading away four starters for future assets. Quarterback Daniel Jones, not surprisingly, isn't thrilled by the decision to send guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, receiver Keenan Allen, and receiver Josh Downs to other teams. "I mean, honestly, you’re not you’re not happy to see it, right? " Jones said. "You're a player and you're going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So you're not happy to see a lot of those decisions, and — but like I said, it's outside of our control, and our job is to play, be prepared, and play well. So, like I said, we got a lot of trust in the guys coming in to those spots, and we'll be ready to go." It's a bad situation for the players who remain, since it will be harder for them to win with backups thrust into the lineup. But that's how it works whenever a non-contender admits its situation and trades players. Those who remain have to keep going, trying to win games even if they get the impression that the front office doesn't really care. And even though the Jets hold the Colts' first-round pick, a bad season for Indianapolis will result in a higher spot in every round. As the Colts embark on a rebuild, it's not crazy to think the front office hopes to sink as low in the standings as possible, since that will enhance the priority of the picks they have. The Jets will welcome that, since they have the Colts' first-round pick. Thanks to the failed trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sam Darnold did not practice Wednesday; Drew Lock was limited
summary: The Seahawks have already ruled out Sam Darnold for Week 10, with the starting quarterback's return potentially coming in Week 12 after the bye.
full_text: The Seahawks have already ruled out Sam Darnold for Week 10, with the starting quarterback's return potentially coming in Week 12 after the bye. He did not practice on Wednesday, with ribs and quad injuries. Drew Lock will start against the Raiders. Lock was limited in practice as he navigates right elbow and quadriceps injuries. Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards with a touchdown in the 17-3 victory over the Cardinals. He also rushed five times for 16 yards while playing every offensive snap. Offensive tackle Charles Cross (ankle), offensive guard Quenton Nelson (knee), defensive tackle Brandon Pili (back), defensive tackle Jarran Reed (personal), wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (rest) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) were the others who did not practice. Offensive guard Anthony Bradford (knee), linebacker Derick Hall (back), linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and linebacker Patrick O'Connell (toe), linebacker Connor O'Toole (foot) were the others who were limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Ravens to sign K Riley Patterson
summary: The Ravens have reportedly settled on their next kicker.
full_text: The Ravens have reportedly settled on their next kicker. Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that the Ravens will sign Riley Patterson. Patterson worked out for the team on Wednesday. The Ravens found themselves in need of a new kicker because Jake Moody opted to sign with the Falcons after being elevated from Baltimore's practice squad in Week 9. Moody became the choice because Tyler Loop is on the team's injured reserve list. Patterson opened the season as the Dolphins' kicker, but was released in October after going 7-of-9 on field goals and 5-of-6 on extra points. He is 97-of-112 on field goals and 148-of-154 on extra points over his entire career.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bucs-Bears generates 21.5 million on Sunday night
summary: The Bears have become a significant draw — and it helps when they're in a close game.
full_text: '' The Bears have become a significant draw — and it helps when they're in a close game. Sunday night's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers generated an audience of 21.5 million for NBC and Peacock. It was the biggest Week 9 Sunday night audience since 2019, and the seventh 2026 audience for the Sunday night franchise that exceeded 20 million viewers. The Week 10 game between the 6-2 Steelers and the 6-2 Bengals should also crack 20 million, as should the Week 11 game between the 6-2 Vikings and 7-1 49ers in Mexico City. For Week 12? When the Patriots visit the Chargers? Well, they can’t all be winners , can they?
author: Mike Florio

title: Deebo Samuel limited in his return to practice
summary: 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel was limited in his return to practice on Wednesday.
full_text: 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel was limited in his return to practice on Wednesday. Samuel missed the past three games with a hamstring injury. He had not practiced since Oct. 9. Samuel has 16 catches for 206 yards and three touchdowns in five games. The 49ers practiced without wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles), cornerback Renardo Green (back), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (rest), cornerback Deommodore Lenoir (foot), running back Christian McCaffrey (rest) and left tackle Trent Williams (rest). Safety Siran Neal (knee/foot), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) and defensive tackle C.J. West (knee) were limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bills S Amani Hooker: "Amazing" to be on a team that's winning
summary: Safety Amani Hooker was catapulted up the standings this week.
full_text: Safety Amani Hooker was catapulted up the standings this week. Hooker was traded from Tennessee to Buffalo on Tuesday and the move took him from a 1-7 team to a 7-1 club that has designs on making a long postseason run. Acquiring Hooker to shore up the back end of their defense should help their chances and Hooker said on Wednesday that he was thrilled by the change in circumstances. "It's amazing ," Hooker said, via Nick Suss of ESPN.com. "That's literally all I can say. Because I've been on a team that hasn't been winning. So I'm obviously very grateful for the Titans and what they did for me. But in the past, we haven't been winning. And to be on a team that's putting up points with a quarterback and offensive guys that are on fire, and a great defense, I'm just excited to be here." Hooker said he's confident he will pick up the Bills defense well enough to play against the Jets on Sunday and the process of getting him up to speed will continue over the next couple of days.
author: Josh Alper

title: Browns WR Denzel Boston is expected back at practice Thursday
summary: The Browns practiced without wide receiver Denzel Boston on Wednesday, but they don't expect his absence to be an extended one.
full_text: The Browns practiced without wide receiver Denzel Boston on Wednesday, but they don't expect his absence to be an extended one. Boston is listed with a toe injury and head coach Todd Monken said at his pre-practice press conference that the second-round pick is expected to be back on the field on Thursday. “I wouldn’t say it’s a concern," Monken said, via a transcript from the team. "Obviously, I anticipate him being out today. He’s got a little toe issue, but we anticipate him being back tomorrow.” Fullback Michael Burton (calf), safety Ronnie Hickman (concussion), and center Elgton Jenkins (knee) were also out of practice. Offensive tackle Austin Barber (calf), defensive tackle Maliek Collins (elbow), tight end Harold Fannin (groin), right tackle Tytus Howard (knee), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (wrist, ankle), cornerback Denzel Ward (quad), and linebacker Quincy Williams (hamstring) were the team's limited participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: A.J. Brown limited in return to practice, Patriots rule out three
summary: The Patriots ruled three players out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich on Wednesday, but there was some encouraging news about wide receiver A.J.
full_text: The Patriots ruled three players out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich on Wednesday, but there was some encouraging news about wide receiver A.J. Brown. Brown was a limited participant in practice after missing the last two games with a knee injury. Brown was also listed as out on the team's last five practice reports. Safety Kevin Byard (chest), fullback Reggie Gilliam (knee), tight end Hunter Henry (foot), right tackle Morgan Moses (foot), guard Greg Van Roten (hamstring), and cornerback Charles Woods (hamstring) joined Brown as limited participants. Quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder) was a full participant.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons DE James Pearce did not practice Wednesday
summary: Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. made his season debut on Sunday after serving an eight-game suspension.
full_text: Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. made his season debut on Sunday after serving an eight-game suspension. Pearce played only 15 snaps in the loss to the Bengals, though, after back tightness late last week. He had no stats. Pearce rehabbed Wednesday, sitting out practice. The Falcons also practiced without wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring), linebacker Josh Woods (ankle) and defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. (illness). Linebacker Divine Deablo, who played with his arm wrapped against Cincinnati, was limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Blake Cashman, T.J. Hockenson miss practice for Vikings
summary: Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman may not be available for Sunday's showdown with the Packers.
full_text: Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman may not be available for Sunday's showdown with the Packers. Cashman would have missed practice on Wednesday because he is in the league's concussion protocol. The Vikings issued an estimated injury report because they played on Monday night. Cashman will have to progress through that protocol quickly if he's going to have a shot of getting on the field in Green Bay this weekend. Tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist, chest) also would have missed practice on Wednesday. Hockenson played 39 of the team's 48 offensive snaps in Monday night's loss to Buffalo. Defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), wide receiver Jauan Jennings (calf), quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring), and linebacker Kyle Van Noy (calf) were the other Vikings listed as out of practice. Safety Jay Ward (knee) and quarterback Carson Wentz (ankle) were listed as limited participants.

title: Christian Mahogany: I need to grow up and stop breaking team rules
summary: Christian Mahogany will return as the Lions' starting left guard on Sunday, a week after his benching for a violation of team rules.
full_text: ''' Christian Mahogany will return as the Lions' starting left guard on Sunday, a week after his benching for a violation of team rules. Mahogany apologized to the team Wednesday morning and was back with the first-team offense in the afternoon. Coach Dan Campbell has said only that Mahogany broke a team rule "multiple times," but did not elaborate. Mahogany wouldn't either when he spoke Wednesday. "I’m not going to [say what the rule was] either. I’m not going to disobey him," Mahogany said, via Will Burchfield of 97.1 The Ticket. "It sucks what happened, but I have to grow up , and I have to stop breaking team rules. It is what it is. I let my teammates down. I let my organization down, and it won’t ever happen again." Campbell's four team rules are: Don’t be late; keep your weight in check; don’t disrespect your teammates, and don’t disrespect the game. Mahogany first landed in trouble in training camp when he was briefly placed on the non-football injury list. His absence in Sunday's win over the Dolphins was noticeable as his replacement, Miles Frazier, had a rough afternoon. "You just gotta eat it on the chin," Mahogany said of his benching. "That’s who I am. I’m not a person that’s gonna sulk. It sucked not being out there, because I let my teammates down. I don’t want to do that. I did, and that’s on me."
author: Charean Williams

title: 3-5 Panthers face 3-5 Saints for first place in NFC South
summary: It's not often that a matchup of two 3-5 teams carries major playoff implications.
full_text: It's not often that a matchup of two 3-5 teams carries major playoff implications. But it's also not often that there's a division as bad as this year's NFC South. On Sunday in New Orleans, the 3-5 Panthers will take on the 3-5 Saints, and the winner will have sole possession of first place in the NFC South. The Panthers and Saints are currently tied, with the Panthers in first place thanks to a better division record. Sunday's winner will be 4-5, a game ahead of the loser and also a game ahead of the 3-6 Buccaneers, who have their bye this week. The 3-6 Falcons face the Chiefs, and the betting odds say Atlanta is likely to fall to 3-7 after that game. All four teams in the NFC South are bad, but someone has to win the division, and whoever that "someone" is will host a playoff game.

title: Patrick Mahomes practiced in full on Wednesday: "I'm in a great spot"
summary: While it looked at first on Sunday like Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes had suffered a significant elbow injury, it turns out he hasn't even missed any practice time.
full_text: While it looked at first on Sunday like Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes had suffered a significant elbow injury, it turns out he hasn't even missed any practice time. Kansas City listed Mahomes as a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Mahomes said in his press conference that he's in a better spot now, particularly after going through an MRI that did not reveal anything too serious. "[A]nytime you get in there, you never know what it’s going to show on the machine after," Mahomes said. "And so, you can feel as optimistic as you do, but then you get in there, and something happens. And so, obviously after talking to the doctors and stuff like that, I feel like I’m in a great spot . Now it’s just about pain and pain management and stuff like that, which I’ll try to do whatever I can to be in the best place possible." Mahomes noted he'll have to do a lot of work in the building and at home to ensure he's in a good spot for Sunday. But he's prepared to do so. "I’ll be able to be out on the practice field, throw the football, and do all that different type of stuff," Mahomes said. "We’ll continue this process throughout the entire week so I can be 100 percent on Sunday whenever we get to Atlanta. So, it’s a process — a lot more time in the building. But that’s something that I’m willing to do." Also on the injury report, right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and defense lineman Peter Woods (neck) did not practice. title: Kirk Cousins plans to talk to Jakobe Thomas about No. 8
summary: Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins made his official return to the team on Wednesday.
full_text: Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins made his official return to the team on Wednesday. He still doesn't officially have a number. title: Kevin O'Connell on Kyler Murray: I want him to get healthy, you never know what could happen
summary: The Vikings made Kyler Murray their quarterback choice to open the 2026 season, but it didn't take long for their plans to go awry.
full_text: The Vikings made Kyler Murray their quarterback choice to open the 2026 season, but it didn't take long for their plans to go awry. Murray was concussed early in the season opener, missed Week 2 and then led an underwhelming offense to a 4-1 record before suffering a hamstring injury in Week 8. The Vikings offense got even worse with Carson Wentz in Monday night's loss to the Bills, which led the team to trade for Kirk Cousins on Tuesday. Head coach Kevin O'Connell hasn’t committed to starting Cousins against the Packers this weekend, but it's why the deal was made and Murray isn't currently an option because he remained out of practice with a hamstring injury on Wednesday. Once Murray is healthy, he'll be slated for a backup role as O'Connell said he doesn't believe "you can have a competition during the season" and that his hope is that Murray is available if and when the Vikings have to pivot again. “The reality is what it is ," O'Connell said. "It’s one of those things where I think he appreciated hearing about it before the transaction took place, but at the same time, he knows I believe in him. I believe in Kyler, just like I believe in Carson and I believe in Max [Brosmer]. I want him to get healthy and get back to work because you just never know. We do not hold the cards in how this will go from a health standpoint or anything like that with anybody on our team.” O'Connell said that he told Murray that he knows it has been a "less than ideal" series of events, but that underscores the possibility that the Vikings will have to turn back to him with an important game on the line at some point later this year.

title: Bengals nearly made a costly trade-deadline blunder, and Zac Taylor had to explain it
summary: The Bengals agreed to acquire Ebiketie from the Eagles before discovering the deal could cost them way more than they thought
full_text:
There were six trades on trade deadline day Tuesday, but a trade that didn't happen provided one of the more entertaining moments of what was already a wild day.
The Bengals agreed to send a sixth-round pick to the Eagles for edge defender Arnold Ebiketie , a fairly run-of-the-mill deal on the surface: Ebiketie figured to join the Bengals' pass-rush rotation with Cashius Howell (wrist) on IR. But it seemed the Bengals failed to realize or understand that the trade would have meant also forfeiting the compensatory 2027 third-round pick they are due after losing Trey Hendrickson in free agency.
The trade fell through after the Bengals, it seems, learned about that part of the equation. Wednesday, Bengals coach Zac Taylor addressed the near-trade.
"I feel good (about the EDGE depth)," Taylor said. "Obviously we tried something yesterday, and [director of personnel] Duke [Tobin] was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me of how he wanted this portrayed, and I'm not comfortable doing it, but I'm going to do what he asked.
"We did make an effort to kind of put some depth in there in place of Cashius. As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. He's really apologetic about it and wants to make clear Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our, and that's just the way things go, but certainly have a ton of confidence in our front office and how they do things, and they've given us the players that have allowed us to be 6-2 right now and playing at such a high level. So, we'll put that behind us and move forward ..."
Nick Korte, who contributes to the contract source site OverTheCap, was first to point the potential snafu out . The Eagles signed Ebiketie as a compensatory free agent this offseason, meaning he counted against the compensatory pick formula. That status carries over if he is traded in-season, per the Collective Bargaining Agreement. Here's the full chart:
Oh that's brutal on the 3rd round comp pick! as noted by @nickkorte pic.twitter.com/OwwyNB71PA
The Bengals may have believed Cordell Volson counted as a CFA lost, but he has not played this year, rendering his departure moot in the compensatory picks balance.
To his credit, Taylor said the failed trade didn't interrupt his Tuesday preparation, aside from the very brief conversation he had with Tobin, and that it would not impact the team's preparation for a crucial Week 10 "Sunday Night Football" matchup with the Steelers . Cincinnati and Pittsburgh are tied for the AFC North lead at 6-2.
The Bengals ended up not making any in-season trades this year, even while most other top AFC teams, including the Jaguars , Chiefs and Broncos , did. Taylor had a lot of confidence in the group he has, which has won four straight.
"I really like where we're at," Taylor said. "I think Duke really likes where we're at. So this is a team with a lot of confidence right now. I know it's a fun period of time, the weeks leading up to the trade deadline, for fans and people to generate a lot of media attention of of it, but the truth is we really do like where we're at."
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Cardinals name Carson Beck starting QB: Rookie faces Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett in NFL debut
summary: Gardner Minshew's season-ending injury opens the door for Beck, whose first assignment comes against one of the NFL's most accomplished pass-rushing duos
full_text:
If the 2026 NFL season feels like an unprecedented year for unheralded rookie quarterbacks, that's because it is.
With the Arizona Cardinals (3-6) announcing Carson Beck as their starting quarterback for Week 10 against the Los Angeles Rams (5-4), he will now be the third rookie quarterback drafted outside of the first two rounds to start a game this season. The other two were undrafted rookies -- Jalon Daniels of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Joe Fagnano of the Baltimore Ravens . That hasn't happened since 1987.
"You never really know until you get to the live bullets on Sunday, but just the way he goes about his business, whether it's been from OTAs through training camp before he got hurt, seeing him operate in that first half," coach Mike LaFleur said. "Plus, the one possession there in the second half, so obviously we'll know more come next Sunday, but we have all the confidence he's ready to roll."
In the Hall of Fame game that kicked off the 2026 preseason, Beck completed 15 of his 19 throws for 188 yards and a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers . Beck will also become the fifth quarterback to make his first career start against a duo of pass rushers with 100-plus sacks each when he faces the Rams' duo of Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett .
"Who do they got?" LaFleur said jokingly. "I got no expectations for him except to go out and play his game one play at a time. Go let it rip, go have some fun. Have some fun with your guys."
A depleted group represents Beck's supporting cast, with Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) out for the season and Marvin Harrison Jr . traded to the Houston Texans . Fifth-round rookie Reggie Virgil , undrafted veteran Simi Fehoko and Pro Bowl return man Devin Duvernay are the projected starters.
Fortunately, Beck also has the 2025 first-team All-Pro tight end at his disposal in Trey McBride . McBride leads the NFL with 73 catches through Week 9, and he has 11 consecutive games with at least seven catches. Beck also knows a thing or two about feeding his superstar tight end after his years teaming with Brock Bowers at Georgia.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Agent's Take: Three NFL trade deadline deals teams will regret not making
summary: The Giants needed a workhorse, the Rams needed a receiver and the Packers needed a running game, making these three missed deals natural fits
full_text:
The 2026 trade deadline day didn't produce fireworks like last year, when the New York Jets dealt their best two defensive players in cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . The most consequential deadline day move was the Minnesota Vikings ' reunion with Kirk Cousins , who was the team's quarterback from 2018 through 2023. The Vikings addressed a glaring need at quarterback by acquiring Cousins for a 2027 third-round pick.
The Jacksonville Jaguars , who have a 6-2 record, went all in to win Super Bowl LXI by making aggressive moves a day earlier. Safety Jessie Bates III was acquired from the Atlanta Falcons for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Defensive tackle Jordan Davis was obtained from the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. The Jaguars also traded a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to the New Orleans Saints for defensive tackle Davon Godchaux .
Here are three more trades that should have been made before the deadline that may have improved teams' chances of making the postseason or going on a deep playoff run. The financial ramifications of the moves are highlighted. Salary cap space is based on NFLPA data.
An acquiring team would have needed enough salary cap room to absorb the remainder of the player's current salary. Since the trades would have occurred after Week 9's games, the acquiring team would have been responsible for half of a player's 2026 base salary (9 of 18 total weeks) and any other applicable salary components in his contract.
Trades can't be executed again until the 2027 league year begins on next March 11.
Giants get: Jonathan Taylor , 2028 sixth-round pick Colts get: 2027 second-round pick, 2028 third-round pick
Taylor Remaining 2026 Salary: $ 3.97 million Colts 2026 Salary Cap Savings: $4.60 million Giants 2026 Salary Cap Room: $6.18 million Colts 2027 Dead Money: $10 million ($11.02 million 2027 Salary Cap Savings)
The Colts went into fire sale mode after firing general manager Chris Ballard six games into the season. Criticism about the return when dealing perennial All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner may have contributed to the Colts holding firm on a steep asking price for Taylor. The Colts reportedly wanted a first-round pick or something comparable to the 2023 second, third, and fourth-round picks and the 2024 fifth-round pick the Carolina Panthers received from the San Francisco 49ers for All-Pro running back Christian McCaffrey during the 2022 season to part with Taylor.
That type of haul wasn't realistic. McCaffrey was 26 when he was dealt, while Taylor turns 28 in January. There's also a big discrepancy in mileage. Taylor's 1,712 career carries are almost double the 866 carries McCaffrey had with the Panthers prior to his trade.
Taylor joined the exclusive $20-million-per-running-back club in August. He signed a two-year, $44 million contract extension (worth up to $47 million through incentives) with $39.02 million in guarantees and $23 million fully guaranteed at signing. Taylor's remaining 2026 compensation consists of $3.49 million in base salary and $480,000 of per-game active roster bonuses. Additionally, $625,000 of Taylor's $1 million in 2026 incentives is a salary cap charge because it is classified as likely to be earned, making a $4.595 million 2026 cap hit with him for the acquiring team. Taylor has two years worth $34 million remaining on his contract after this season. He is scheduled to make $16.02 million in 2027 and $17.98 million in 2028.
The Colts could revisit a trade for Taylor during the offseason. It's likely that Taylor's trade value won't be any higher in the future.
The Giants reportedly were willing to give the Colts a second-round pick, a fifth-round pick, and an unnamed player for Taylor before pulling the offer. According to ESPN's Jordan Ranaan, the Giants called multiple teams about finding a workhorse running back as the trade deadline approached.
Rams get: Brian Thomas Jr. Jaguars get: 2027 second-round pick
Remaining 2026 Salary: $537,500 Jaguars 2026 Salary Cap Savings: $537,500 Rams 2026 Salary Cap Room: $248,672 Jaguars 2027 Dead Money: $1.8M ($2.8M Salary Cap Savings)
After his stellar 2024 rookie season in which he had 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns, Thomas has struggled ever since Liam Coen took over as Jaguars head coach. The 2024 first-round pick has become an afterthought in Jacksonville's passing game. Week 9's game against the Baltimore Ravens was the first time in Thomas' NFL career he wasn't targeted at least once. Thomas has 10 receptions, 117 receiving yards, and two touchdowns in eight games this season. Josh Cameron , a 2026 sixth-round pick, has more offensive snaps than Thomas since Week 4.
The Jaguars, who are in win-now mode, rebuffed trade interest in Thomas despite his dwindling role. Moving Thomas would have allowed the Jaguars to recoup some of the draft capital from Monday's trades. Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.'s trade in October could have served as a blueprint. The Arizona Cardinals received a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick from the Houston Texans in exchange for Harrison—2024's fourth overall pick—and a 2027 sixth-round pick.
A 5-4 record didn't seem imaginable when the Rams were the heavy favorites to win Super Bowl LXI before the season started. Injuries have decimated the Rams receiving corps. Davante Adams was put on injured reserve after rupturing a hamstring tendon in Week 6's game against the Cardinals. His estimated recovery time is six to 10 weeks, likely putting his likely return in early December. Puka Nacua suffered a sprained MCL, sprained PCL, and turf toe in his right leg at the end of Week 9's win over the Washington Commanders . He is expected to miss at least a month but has not been put on IR.
Out of the 26 targets to wide receivers against the Commanders, 19 went to Nacua. The remaining wide receivers on the Rams' 53-man roster have caught 18 passes for 261 yards with one touchdown this season.
Thomas would have been a major short-term upgrade with Adams and Nacua out. He also could have been a younger, lower-cost potential replacement for a soon-to-be 33-year-old Adams, who has an expiring contract. Thomas, who is 24, is under contract in 2027 for a fully guaranteed $2,794,089. A fifth-year option for 2028 could be picked up by May 1 next offseason for around $19.5 million.
The big problem is that the Rams wouldn't have had any picks in the first two days of the 2027 NFL Draft if they had acquired Thomas. The 2027 first-round pick was part of the acquisition cost to get reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in June. The 2027 third-round pick was one of four draft choices the Kansas City Chiefs received for cornerback Trent McDuffie in March.
Restructuring a contract would have been necessary given the Rams' tight salary cap situation to handle Thomas' remaining $537,500 2026 base salary. Quarterback Matthew Stafford would have been a prime candidate since he has 2026's largest cap number at $48,267,348.

title: NFL trade deadline: Jonathan Taylor leads candidates for offseason moves after staying put
summary: Just because these players were not dealt at the deadline, that does not mean they will suit up for their current team in 2027
full_text:
The deals that got across the finish line at the 2026 NFL trade deadline included a couple of blockbusters that shook up the balance of power at the front of the Super Bowl race. But just as meaningful were the moves that never materialized. For instance, the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles called off an agreed-upon transaction that would have bolstered the former's defense. Even more significant than the nixed Arnold Ebiketie deal were the offers for Jonathan Taylor and other stars that never resulted in trades, either.
Taylor was supposed to be the belle of the ball at the deadline, but the Indianapolis Colts turned down interest from other teams when they did not receive the first-round pick they sought in a return package. Stars like George Pickens and other players like Will McDonald IV who would have been plug-and-play starters on other teams remained in place on their present rosters.
The players teams made and entertained calls on but did not switch at the deadline immediately became names to monitor ahead of the next trade window, which opens in the spring at the start of the 2027 league year.
Here are the 10 biggest names that did not change teams at the trade deadline but who could be on the move in the offseason.
The Indianapolis Colts were the most aggressive sellers at the trade deadline, but Jonathan Taylor was not among the four players they shipped out of town. The three-time Pro Bowler is a gargantuan asset because he is an elite-tier running back with no guaranteed money on his contract in 2027 or 2028, so he can remain an affordable and prolific foundational piece of the Colts' rebuild. Those same factors make him tremendously valuable on the trade market, though, and for a team that is going nowhere fast, it would behoove the Colts to take the right deal if it came to them in the offseason. They reportedly turned down offers that included second-round picks and more , so it will probably take at least a first-rounder to pry him away next spring or summer.
Unless the Dallas Cowboys re-sign George Pickens, they may regret not trading him. They likely could have garnered a sizable return package for their No. 2 wide receiver -- who would be a No. 1 on most teams -- and that would have arguably been the more prudent move than keeping him on a squad that is on the outside looking in on the playoff picture. Jerry Jones declined to sign Pickens to a long-term extension last offseason and could again use the franchise tag on the standout pass-catcher, but Pickens is worthy of a lucrative multi-year deal and may seek one elsewhere if Jones is hesitant again.
Will McDonald IV requested a trade from the New York Jets on the eve of the trade deadline, citing frustration with his playing time. He played 50% or more of the team's defensive snaps just three times over the first nine weeks and most recently saw only 24 snaps of work in Week 9. Darren Mougey did not heed his request, though, and retained him despite reported interest from other teams, including the Jacksonville Jaguars . New York has myriad options at edge rusher and will feature David Bailey most prominently in the years to come, so a clear path to a larger role may not manifest for McDonald. In that case, he could amplify his search for a trade in the offseason.
A reunion between Khalil Mack and the Chicago Bears would have made all the sense in the world, but the Los Angeles Chargers showed no interest in moving him , and the Bears used their draft capital on Jeffery Simmons instead. That the Chargers held onto all but one player despite their putrid 0-8 record was a major surprise. There were draft picks to be had for Mack, Ladd McConkey and even Justin Herbert , but the Chargers elected to keep their core intact even as it looks unsalvageable in a miserable campaign. Mack is a prime candidate to walk in free agency since he is in the latter stages of his career and would thus be more likely to seek a home on a contending squad rather than a bottom-dweller like Los Angeles.
Teams inquired about Tony Pollard , but none constructed a trade package strong enough for the Tennessee Titans to move on from him. The 29-year-old's value has never been higher on the heels of back-to-back 100-yard performances in which he totaled five touchdowns, and that could have played a role in the Titans driving a hard bargain. Retaining him is a short-term play that will allow Tennessee to continue to evaluate second-year quarterback Cam Ward but may not be much more than that since Pollard can leave in free agency if he pleases. At 29, he is not on the same career timeline as the rest of the team's offensive building blocks, anyway.
It makes ample sense for the Jacksonville Jaguars to hold onto anyone and everyone as they prepare for a potential Super Bowl run. If it ain't broke, don't fix it. But Brian Thomas Jr . is only a marginal part of their stellar passing attack and lost ground to Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the pecking order for targets. His Pro Bowl-caliber rookie season looks more and more like a flash in the pan. Unless the Jaguars truly believe they can maximize the former first-round pick's talent in the final year of his contract, his situation will be one to revisit in the next trade window that opens in March. This is not dissimilar to the situation that led to Marvin Harrison Jr . being traded to the Houston Texans for a second-round pick and sixth-rounder, but the Jaguars are a contender and would reasonably prefer not to toy with their lineup until after the season.
Budda Baker is an Arizona Cardinals legend. If the 2026 trade deadline—when the Cardinals are projected as potential sellers amid on-field struggles —was not the time to move him, they may just let him play out his career in the desert. As the Cardinals' roster continues to shift in a younger direction, though, a split could make sense. Baker will be 31 when the 2027 league year begins, and the Cardinals are poised to take a quarterback in the first round of the draft, restarting the clock on their contention timeline. As an eight-time Pro Bowler still in his prime, Baker would garner the kind of return that would help Arizona load up on draft picks and build around that incoming quarterback.
As with the other trade candidates on expiring deals, Riq Woolen's potential exit in free agency could net the Philadelphia Eagles a valuable compensatory draft pick. That is probably the justification for keeping him, because Howie Roseman was willing to move on from some foundational pieces in the weeks leading up to the deadline, and Woolen seemed as tradeable as any of them. Woolen has been solid for the Eagles in pass defense but regressed from the standout level he performed at with the Seattle Seahawks -- his 103.3 passer rating allowed is by far a career-worst -- so Philadelphia may not aim to retain him on a multi-year deal regardless.
There have been rumblings of a possible Josh Sweat trade since the spring. Nothing came to fruition in the offseason, and the Arizona Cardinals stood pat at the trade deadline, too. But as the team remains mired in the early stages of a deep rebuild, any tensions between Sweat and the front office may grow louder in advance of his next opportunity to seek a way out. Sweat reportedly requested a trade last spring amid frustration with his contract, but both he and the team worked to quell that narrative over the last handful of months. It is clear that moving him is not a top priority for the Cardinals, but the standout pass rusher will be one to keep monitoring at the start of the new league year in 2027 in case that changes.
The Tennessee Titans have phased Calvin Ridley out of their receiving corps, with Carnell Tate , Wan'Dale Robinson , Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike outproducing him in catches. Two tight ends and two running backs also have more targets than him this season. If he is no longer part of their plans, it makes little sense to retain him for…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Renner's post-deadline 2027 NFL mock draft: How the trade deadline affected the first three rounds
summary: The Eagles and Titans rebuild after the deadline, while the Chargers land a new weapon for Justin Herbert in Jeremiah Smith
full_text:
Dante Moore, Julian Sayin, CJ Carr, LaNorris Sellers -- what do all four of those quarterbacks have in common? Well none of them appear in this mock draft because all of them have more years of eligibility. With Sayin and Carr I think physical development and mastery are needed for them to get drafted where they want to. For Moore it's a full healthy season after his scary head injury last weekend. And for Sellers, well, there's a lot that needs to change.
While those four returning to school makes this "loaded" quarterback class far less exciting, the draft is still loaded at other positions -- especially the ones that get paid the big bucks. Three receivers, two offensive tackles, and two edge rushers go within the top 10 of what's shaping up to be a blue-chip-heavy draft class.
That certainly bodes well for teams like the Philadelphia Eagles and Tennessee Titans, who picked up some top-end draft capital in the weeks leading up to the NFL trade deadline. They now join the New York Jets and Cleveland Browns as teams with multiple first-round picks in the 2027 draft. Tennessee, the Atlanta Falcons, and the Arizona Cardinals also picked up second-round picks over the last few weeks. With the dust settled after the deadline , let's take a look at how those new picks are being spent.
One last thing, and this is important: The draft order was determined using the reverse Super Bowl odds at DraftKings Sportsbook. The Jets have three first-round picks: their own, the Cowboys' from the Quinnen Williams trade and the Colts' from the Sauce Gardner trade. The Cowboys have the Packers' selection from the Micah Parsons trade. The Browns have the Rams' first from the Myles Garrett trade. There have also been a total of 18 trades made before the deadline , nine of which involved picks in the first three rounds of this draft.

title: Former NFL head coach Rex Ryan arrested by Nashville police for allegedly striking two pedestrians with truck
summary: The incident occurred before midnight on Thursday, Nov. 5
full_text:
Rex Ryan surrendered for booking to Nashville police on Wednesday morning after an incident in which the former NFL head coach allegedly struck two pedestrians with his pickup truck on Thursday, Nov. 5. The two pedestrians suffered minor injuries, according to the police report .
The incident occurred before midnight that Thursday as the pedestrians were crossing Broadway and 4th Avenue with a walk sign on. Ryan, 63, allegedly turned right from 4th Avenue and ran over both victims' feet. Ryan's truck also made contact with one of the individuals' legs.
According to the pedestrians, the vehicle kept driving after striking them, but stopped at a red light at Broadway and Representative John Lewis Way.  That's when they waved Ryan down, and the former coach is said to have stepped out of his truck to argue with them before getting back in and driving away. They took pictures of the drive and the truck's license plate, which was registered to Ryan.
After surrendering for booking on Wednesday morning, Ryan was charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information/render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control device. Ryan's bond was set by a judicial commissioner at $6,000.
Ryan last coached in the NFL back in 2016 when he was head coach of the Buffalo Bills . Before that, he broke into the league as a defensive line and linebackers coach for the Arizona Cardinals back in 1994. From there, he went on to become a decorated defensive-minded coach. He spent the bulk of his career in Baltimore, beginning as a defensive line coach in 1999 before ascending to defensive coordinator in 2005 and holding that position until 2008, before being hired as the head coach of the New York Jets .
Ryan was on staff during Baltimore's Super Bowl XXXV championship and is 65-68 in his head coaching career (4-2 in the playoffs).
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Kirk Cousins traded to Vikings: Raiders gave QB option to stay or leave franchise, per report
summary: Minnesota gave up a third round pick to bring back Cousins
full_text:
Maybe the most consequential trade of deadline day in the NFL wasn't actually made by a front office executive. Instead, the lone player in the deal gave it the final go-ahead.
In the final hours before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline, the Minnesota Vikings pulled off a trade for Kirk Cousins , sending the Las Vegas Raiders a 2027 third-round pick to reunite with their former quarterback. Before ultimately agreeing to the deal, however, the Raiders put the ball in Cousins' court, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . Las Vegas gave Cousins the chance to decide whether he'd like to leave the organization and head back to Minnesota or stay with the club he had started the first nine games of the 2026 season for.
After talking with his family, agent Mike McCartney, and Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell, Cousins made up his mind by midday Tuesday and ultimately informed Raiders GM John Spytek that he wanted to return to Minnesota. Thus, the trade was made.
"So much respect for John Spytek and the Raiders organization," McCartney told The Ringer's Tom Pelissero about how the team handled this trade. "There aren't many leaders in this league who would've done that. Very appreciative of Spy."
Part of the calculus in Cousins' decision to opt for a return to the Vikings was the presence of Fernando Mendoza . The report indicates Cousins knew it was only a matter of time before the Raiders turned the keys to the franchise over to the 2026 No. 1 overall pick, so his status as QB1 was fleeting.
With an opportunity to go back and help a Vikings team he spent six years with and won the NFC North with in 2022, the proper pieces fell into place to give the deal the green light. This is also a pretty unprecedented move, as Cousins has the most single-season passing touchdowns (20) -- as well as career passing touchdowns (318) -- by any quarterback changing teams midseason in NFL history.
During his first six-season stint with the Vikings, Cousins was second in the league in completiion percentage (67.9%), fourth in passing yards (23,265), and third in passing touchdowns (171) among all quarterbacks over that span with at least 50 starts. He also reunites with wide receiver Justin Jefferson , who averaged 98.9 receiving yards per game with Cousins -- an NFL record for most receiving yards by a quarterback-receiver duo over at least 50 games. While the 15-year veteran is now returning at 38, the hope is that he can come close to that production and give an offense tied for the fewest offensive touchdowns (11) in the NFL this season a boost.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Why Packers' Jordan Love is the 2026 midseason MVP: Green Bay QB dominating with no help
summary: Love is doing more with less and doing it better than every other quarterback in the NFL through nine weeks of the 2026 season
full_text:
There is no quarterback in the NFL doing more with less in 2026 than Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love . That's why he is the 2026 midseason NFL MVP through the first nine weeks of the season.
Green Bay has a 6-3 record with wins in five of their last six games, which would have them making the postseason if the season ended today. That is an absolute miracle. The Packers are dead last in the NFL in rushing offense, averaging 68.2 rushing yards per game. That is the fewest rushing yards per game for a team with a winning record through the first nine games of a season in NFL history, and bell cow running back Josh Jacobs is sidelined after undergoing finger surgery.
The Packers have also dropped the most passes, 23, which is seven more than the next closest team. Green Bay's 39 accepted offensive penalties are the third most in the entire league, and the Packers' offensive line is allowing an average time to pressure of 2.48 seconds, the second-fastest in the league, better than only the Carolina Panthers (2.46 seconds). That's because the Packers' best offensive lineman, right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, went down with a season-ending injury in Week 2, and Green Bay is currently starting their third-string center. Love has also been hit 57 times this season, the fifth most in the league.
All of this is to say Love is doing a lot with not much help around him. He's earned the Packers' winning record.
Despite all those disadvantages and NFL defenses knowing he has to throw it because the Packers can't run it, Love is dominating. On Sunday, he rolled into Gillette Stadium and threw for 372 yards passing and three passing touchdowns while completing 23 of his 29 throws, in addition to adding a 13-yard rushing touchdown. When Packers coach Matt LaFleur subbed in his second-team offense into the game with eight minutes left in the fourth quarter, Green Bay led 45-21. Those 45 points are the most the Patriots have allowed in a home game since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.
Love is playing quarterback like Ethan Hunt in a "Mission: Impossible" movie. His adversaries know he is coming, and despite the odds stacked against him, Love is still coming out on top. He leads the NFL in passing yards (2,618) and completions of 20-plus yards (40) and is third in the league in passing touchdowns (19). Love is also up to three games with five-plus completions of 30-plus yards this season, which already ranks as the most in any season in the last 35 years.
On Sunday against the Patriots, he also completed six of his eight deep passes, throws of 20-plus air yards, for 235 yards and a touchdown. That was Love's second game with at least six completions of 20-plus air yards in 2026, and no other quarterback in the NFL has done that in any other game this season, per the league's Next Gen Stats.
"I can't say enough about the play of Jordan Love. He makes my job a hell of a lot easier," LaFleur said postgame on Sunday . "He is standing in there, he's taking hits and still dealing the ball. ... Those are low-percentage throws, in theory, but he's making them look high-percentage. They're right on the money."
When you turn on the tape, Love is doing things physically that no other quarterback is doing. In the clip from Sunday below, he is fading off of his back foot with pressure in his face, and he calmly hit wide receiver Christian Watson for a 28-yard gain. This throw isn't an isolated incident for Love either. He makes this pass multiple times a game, week after week.
JORDAN LOVE OFF HIS BACK FOOT FINDS CHRISTIAN WATSON LOVE IS UNSTOPPABLE RIGHT NOW pic.twitter.com/0FNSefZlWc
Buffalo Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen , a player some regard as the NFL's best quarterback this season, attempted a similar throw a day later on "Monday Night Football" against the Minnesota Vikings . However, he underthrew the pass for an interception. Even one of the league's most physically gifted passers couldn't execute what Love is doing.
BYRON MURPHY PICKS IT OFF IN THE END ZONE BUFvsMIN on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pJikc7Dtdj
Speaking of the Vikings and their No. 1 defense, no quarterback has thrown for more passing yards (387), yards per pass attempt (9.2), passing touchdowns (2) or a better passer rating (88.1) than Love has against Minnesota's blitzkrieg unit this season.
It's understandable for football fans and media alike to feel fatigued by hearing "the Green Bay Packers have an MVP-caliber quarterback" after Love's predecessors, Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers , each won at least three league MVP awards. However, Love learned well from Rodgers and Favre. The end result is the Packers quarterback factory cranked out another one. The Packers fans who made the trip out to New England know it. They serenaded him with "MVP" chants as he jogged into the tunnel after Green Bay's 45-27 victory on Sunday.
"It's a really cool feeling, and I really appreciate all the fans," Love said postgame on Sunday .
Making this all the most impressive: The Packers' defense remains without All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons , the unit's best player, who is still rehabbing his knee from a torn ACL and meniscus suffered in December of 2025. Most quarterbacks would crumble into a pile of dust if dropped into these circumstances. Instead, Love has soared and powered the Packers into playoff position. That's why he is the NFL's 2026 midseason MVP.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Week 10 QB Power Rankings: There's a new No. 1, while Caleb Williams drops out of top 10
summary: Joe Burrow swipes the top spot, Jordan Love climbs into the top five, C.J. Stroud cracks the top 10 and Caleb Williams falls
full_text:
Quarterbacks are the most vital position in football. After all, they're the highest-paid players, and the past 13 NFL MVP award winners are, that's right, quarterbacks.
