title: Giants attempted to trade for Falcons star RB Bijan Robinson at trade deadline, per report
summary: After missing out on Jeffery Simmons and Jonathan Taylor, New York took a huge swing on the league's leading rusher before standing pat
full_text:
The 5-2-1 New York Giants did not have a surprise for fans at the 2026 NFL trade deadline. After acquiring former No. 10 overall pick J.J. McCarthy to be their new quarterback in the wake of Jaxson Dart's injury, it looked like the Giants were going to be aggressive in acquiring a new star to help them secure the lackluster NFC East.
Head coach John Harbaugh made it clear that the team was interested in Jeffery Simmons of the Tennessee Titans before the defensive tackle was sent to the Chicago Bears in a deal that included two first-round picks. Reports also indicated the Giants were interested in Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor before ultimately pulling their offer, which reportedly was a package of picks headlined by a second-rounder.
The Giants were trying to be big-game hunters. In fact, ESPN's Jordan Raanan revealed that the Giants made a call to the Atlanta Falcons about star running back Bijan Robinson . Yes, the Bijan Robinson who currently leads the NFL with 880 yards rushing in nine games played. The Bijan Robinson who has recorded the fifth-most career scrimmage yards (6,778) before age 25 in NFL history.
New York swinging a deal for Robinson would have been the story of the trade deadline, but those talks probably didn't go very far. Atlanta views Robinson as a pillar of its franchise and rewarded him with a three-year extension worth up to $75 million this offseason after he recorded a franchise-record 2,298 scrimmage yards in 2025.
Plus, the Falcons are right in the mix for the lowly NFC South, which features four teams each with just three wins. Atlanta wasn't looking to sell pieces despite picking up a second-round pick and future fifth-round pick for Jessie Bates III . And if the Falcons were going to part ways with arguably the best running back in the NFL, they would require a massive, massive package that featured much more than a first-round pick. The question is what were the Giants willing to offer for Robinson? Or did the conversation with Matt Ryan even get that far?
With no additions at the trade deadline, the Giants will move forward with Cam Skattebo at running back. He's rushed for 418 yards and two touchdowns in seven games played this season, and he did rush for a career-high 124 yards and a touchdown his last time out against the Houston Texans in Week 7.
"You've seen what I can do," Skattebo said Tuesday, per NJ.com . "When I come out, and I'm ready to play football, I can be one of the most dangerous backs in the league. Simple as that."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Browns to start Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders in Week 10 vs. Texans, per report
summary: Watson missed last week's overtime loss vs. New Orleans due to a concussion
full_text:
After a one-game absence due to a concussion, Deshaun Watson will be back as the Cleveland Browns starter in Week 10. As reported by ESPN , the veteran signal caller will start the club's matchup against the Houston Texans on Sunday, a decision that was made despite an encouraging start from second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders in Week 9.
Sanders completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the overtime loss to the Saints in New Orleans. That showing from Sanders appeared to give head coach Todd Monken some pause about who would start going forward, after he declined to name a starter earlier this week. In the days that followed, however, Monken has reportedly decided to go back to his Week 1 starter and send Sanders back to his role as the top backup.
Watson, who has been sacked an NFL-high 33 times this season, was placed in concussion protocol last Tuesday before Week 9 after reporting concussion symptoms to the medical staff. He was eventually able to clear the protocol before the matchup against New Orleans, but the Browns decided to keep him inactive for the contest, thrusting Sanders into the starting role.
In his first start of the season, Sanders got into a rhythm down the stretch for Cleveland as it tried to pull off the overtime win. Over the span of the fourth quarter and overtime, the Colorado product completed 12-of-19 for 197 yards and two touchdowns.
That wasn't enough, however, to push Monken over the edge and keep him as the starter. Watson, who beat out Sanders for the Week 1 job this summer, has been a key factor in Cleveland jumping out to five wins over the first nine games. The Browns are 5-3 with him as the starter, and he's completed 65.5% of his passes with a 91.2 passer rating. Both of those figures are on pace to set new highs over his tenure with the Browns.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Fernando Mendoza new favorite to win Offensive Rookie of the Year ahead of his first NFL start
summary: A wide-open race puts the No. 1 overall pick atop the odds board before his first career start, though a brutal schedule against top defenses looms
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings beat the buzzer at Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, as they sent the Las Vegas Raiders a third-round pick for quarterback Kirk Cousins . There were plenty of winners in this trade.
The Vikings get better at the most important position in football, the Raiders got nice compensation, and Cousins upgrades his own situation — going from 4-5 to 6-2 with Justin Jefferson. And then, there's Fernando Mendoza .
The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft is now the Raiders' new starter, and because he's been promoted to first-string, Mendoza is now your new favorite to win Offensive Rookie of the Year over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza
It's pretty shocking to see a player making his first career start in Week 10 be favored to win Offensive Rookie of the Year, but that just spotlights the fact that no one else in the class has really been able to separate.
Boston and Concepcion in Cleveland are the first teammate duo to rank 1-2 in rookie receiving yards through Week 9 in NFL history, but neither are inside the top 20 of receiving when it comes to the entire league. Coleman appears to be the new RB1 in Denver, but he hasn't crossed 60 yards rushing in a single game this season. Then there's Tate in Tennessee, who had a nine-catch, 145-yard explosion against the Baltimore Ravens last month, but his production has been inconsistent.
It's possible one of those players steps up and ends the regular season on a tear, but the door is open for Mendoza to win rookie of the year despite the fact that he's completed just 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards halfway through the season.
"This is something that he's worked very hard for since the moment he's walked into this building," Raiders general manager John Spytek said of Mendoza. "He passed every test. ... He put us in a position where we had to make a very hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback."
Mendoza has to be ready to roll immediately, because the Raiders have a few tough defenses coming up on their schedule. Mendoza will become the first No. 1 overall pick quarterback in NFL history to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champions, per CBS Sports Research, as Vegas hosts the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. Mendoza also becomes the first No. 1 overall pick quarterback to make his first career start against the NFL's No. 1 defense since Vinny Testaverde in 1987.
In Week 11, Mendoza makes his first road start against the Broncos, who rank top five in sacks and are currently on a five-game win streak. In Week 12 come the Browns, who have gone 54 straight games without allowing a 300-yard passer. That's tied for the longest streak in the NFL over the past 40 seasons.
Still, the Raiders feel as though the rookie is prepared for the moment. Sportsbooks seem to think so, too.
"He's prepared," Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said. "He practices extremely well, and his work habits also allowed us to make this trade because we feel that he's ready to go. And we're excited for him to take the ball for the game here this Sunday."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Kirk Cousins' reunion with Vikings headlines NFL trade deadline; Georgia tops CFP Top 25 rankings
summary: Plus winners and losers from the first Celtics vs. 76ers showdown since their blockbuster trade
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
The trade deadline is all about the deals that actually get done, but what about the ones that never cross the finish line? The Bengals learned a hard lesson about the compensatory pick formula on Tuesday and called off a trade because of it. They were in agreement with the Eagles on a swap that would send Arnold Ebiketie to Cincinnati in return for a 2027 sixth-round pick but backed out when they realized the ramifications. Our Jordan Dajani explained the bizarre situation when he labeled the Bengals as the deadline's biggest losers .
That's an example of what not to do if you're inside an NFL front office. But as we shift our focus back to the trades that did come to fruition, we have to recognize the masterclass the 49ers put on. They landed Keenan Allen on Tuesday to add to a haul that already included DeForest Buckner . In securing much-needed wide receiver help, they became one of four teams to receive an "A" grade on our trade deadline report card . For context, here's a look at the rest of the NFC West:
Defensive players are important, too! In fact, many of the splashiest moves included defensive linemen and defensive backs. Take Amani Hooker , for instance. The Bills gave up a second-round pick to land the NFL's interception leader in one of the top five deals of the deadline .
It's hard to say that any team got better than the Jaguars (they made three splashes and boosted an already prolific defense), but the Chiefs also upgraded significantly. Josh Downs is the newest member of their wide receiver group by way of a win-win trade with the Colts .
Pete Prisco finalized his latest set of NFL Power Rankings before the last-minute hustle of trade deadline moves, so the dip the Vikings took ahead of Week 10 emphasizes just how important it was for them to add Kirk Cousins . Minnesota was the biggest faller of the week, down five spots to No. 11. Most teams' trades (or lack thereof) were already factored into the equation, though, so it should not come as a surprise to see the deadline's most active franchises check in at the top of the pecking order. Each of the top six teams made at least one trade.
A little further down, the Packers jumped into the top 10 without adding to their roster. A certain superstar edge rusher should return to action by the end of the month, though.

title: NFL Week 10 picks, best bets: Steelers cool off Joe Burrow's Bengals, Chiefs roll in Atlanta
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 10 schedule, including five locks against the spread
full_text:
There's only one way to describe last week in the NFL : Chalk.
Favorites dominated the Week 9 slate as just one upset occurred while every other favorite took care of business. That was music to our ears because we saw the week playing out that exact way, dialing up a perfect 15-0 record on the moneyline. The only underdog we liked last week was Green Bay, and they proved us right as they rolled into Foxborough and steamrolled the Patriots . That not only helped me notch a pristine moneyline record but also cashed one of my five Locks of the Week.
There, I was 3-2 ATS, which jived with my more modest 8-7 ATS record for the week overall. That's not as stellar as the straight-up mark, but we were above .500, so we made money. And that's what we're after at the end of the day.
I'll try to keep the momentum rolling into Week 10 where, unlike last week, I do have a fair share of underdogs pulling off the upsets. That includes the Pittsburgh Steelers , who land inside my five Locks of the Week.
Note : Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia, and Tampa Bay are on the bye in Week 10.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
There's arguably no offense hotter right now than the Bengals . Over their four-game winning streak, they've averaged over 35 points per game, and Joe Burrow has been playing at an MVP level. The Cincinnati QB has 18 total touchdowns over this stretch and a 132.0 passer rating. Simply put, they've been a bulldozer. However, I do think it's worth pointing out who they've played over the course of the winning streak: at Dolphins , at Ravens (no Lamar Jackson ), vs. Titans and vs. Falcons . Not exactly a murderer's row.
Pittsburgh, who beat these Bengals back in Week 3, should provide much more resistance than what they've faced recently. The Steelers defense is tied for the fifth-lowest yards per play average (5.0), tied for the fourth-lowest points per game allowed (18.0), and tied for the eighth-lowest passer rating allowed (83.3). Meanwhile, Cincinnati's defense is tied for the most yards per rush attempt allowed so far this season (5.0), which sets up Jaylen Warren to continue his ascent as one of the true breakout players of the season.
On top of this being a potential mismatch for the Bengals going up against this stout Steelers team, their scheduling surrounding this game does them no favors either. While they'll be at home in Week 10, Cincinnati is coming off an international game in Madrid last week. As for the Steelers, they're fresh off their bye week, creating a sizable rest discrepancy. All of this is a recipe for an upset.
Projected score : Steelers 27, Bengals 24 The pick : Steelers +3.5
While their 3-5 records don't exactly scream playoff contenders, first place in the NFC South is on the line in this game. Bryce Young doesn't have the best history going up against the Saints , as the Panthers quarterback is just 1-5 against his division foe in his career. That said, I think there's a window here for him to get a rare victory against New Orleans on Sunday.
While his numbers have come down since his stellar start to begin the season, Young started to look more like himself in the loss to Denver, completing 71.7% of his passes to go along with three touchdowns. The Saints secondary is allowing 7.3 yards per attempt so far this season, which is tied for the fifth-highest in the league. Their 99.5 passer rating allowed is also the seventh-highest in the NFL. This isn't as daunting a matchup for Young, who had to face Tampa Bay, Green Bay, and Denver over Carolina's recent three-game losing streak. I like him to rebound here.
Meanwhile, New Orleans is 1-4 straight-up and 0-5 ATS at home this season, so the Superdome hasn't been too friendly thus far.
Projected score : Panthers 24, Saints 21 The pick : Panthers +1.5
Similar to what we discussed with Cincinnati, the Falcons do have to deal with immediately playing the following week after an international game in Madrid last Sunday. That may only put them further behind the eight ball against a Chiefs team that cruised to a 35-12 win over the Jets last week. Patrick Mahomes did give us all a scare in the midst of that game after injuring his elbow, but it doesn't appear serious enough to keep him out of this matchup.
Mahomes has thrown five touchdowns and no interceptions over his past two games, but his lack of a downfield threat has been noticeable. He's averaging an NFL-low 5.6 air yards per attempt this season as the Chiefs have really looked for pass catches to put up yards after the catch. Well, they just acquired some help in that regard in Josh Downs , whom they brought in before the deadline in a trade with the Colts . The wideout has a knack for creating separation and now has a capable quarterback to deliver the football to him, so Kansas City could see quick dividends from this addition. That's especially true against a Falcons secondary that was just lit up by the Bengals last week and just traded away star safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars .
Atlanta is also 0-4 straight-up and ATS in its last four games against the AFC.
Projected score : Chiefs 26, Falcons 20 The pick : Chiefs -3.5
Jacksonville went all-in at the deadline, making trades to acquire Jessie Bates III, Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux to bolster its defense for a potential Super Bowl run. On the flip side, Tennessee traded away pieces, including standout safety Amani Hooker and, going back a couple of weeks, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . That's a lot of talent being drained from the defense, which doesn't bode well against Trevor Lawrence , who is making a sneaky MVP push. Entering Week 10, his 111.7 passer rating ranks second among quarterbacks who have started at least eight games, only looking up to Burrow.
As this double-digit spread suggests, this is a David vs. Goliath matchup, and it's hard to imagine the underdog keeping this thing close. Even before making these trades, Jacksonville's defense was allowing 15.1 points per game (second-best in the NFL) and has also allowed 20 or fewer points in six straight road games. Tony Pollard , who remained with the team through the deadline, has been a bright spot in Tennessee's offense in recent weeks, but could be negated here. The Jaguars are allowing 3.7 yards per carry this season, along with an 89.3 rushing yards per game allowed average that ranks fifth-lowest in the NFL.
A blowout is brewing in this matchup in favor of Jacksonville, who is 13-3 ATS over its last 16 games with a +16.3 points per game differential.
Projected score : Jaguars 34, Titans 16 The pick : Jaguars -10.5
Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The No. 1 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft is set to make his first career start in the aftermath of the Raiders trading Kirk Cousins , who started the first nine games of the year, to Minnesota before the deadline. This will be a baptism by fire for the Indiana product as he'll face off against a Seattle defense that is among the very best in the NFL. The Seahawks are allowing a league-low 244.2 total yards per game entering Week 10, along with an average of 18.0 points per game allowed that is tied for fourth-fewest. That just feels like too tall a mountain to climb for Mendoza right out of the gate.
Meanwhile, the Raiders defense won't do their young quarterback any favors. They're currently on a six-game streak of allowing 30-plus points, which is tied for the longest streak within a season all-time. So, even with Sam Darnold (quad) sidelined and backup Drew Lock set to play through an oblique injury, the Seattle offense should find plenty of scoring opportunities. This could be a breakout game for Zach Charbonnet after leading the team with 16 carries last week for 77 yards, as the Raiders are allowing an NFL-high 5.0 yards per carry.
Given that Mendoza is getting the start, it's also worth pointing out that No. 1 overall quarterbacks are 1-15-1 straight up and 3-14 ATS in their first career starts since 2003.
Projected score :…

title: Prisco's Week 10 NFL picks: Giants over Commanders on 'TNF,' Lions top Patriots in Munich
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 10 picks, including the Packers to spoil Kirk Cousins' return with the Vikings
full_text:
A perfect week. Can you believe it? I went 15-0 with my straight-up picks last week. I guess it was an easy week, like some said.
As for my picks against the spread, it wasn't quite as good, but it was better than it's been. I went 9-6 for the week, which I will take.
The season marks are now 59-74-3 ATS and 87-48-1 straight up. Let's see if we can get perfect against the spread this week.
Yeah, right. I will take three games above. 500 again as I make the climb to respectability.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Giants are back home after beating the Eagles and now face a Commanders team that probably has to win this to have any chance at the playoffs. The Giants' defense has been dominant up front as of late, and that will continue here as they contain Jayden Daniels . Giants keep winning.
Pick: Giants 23, Commanders 14
This is a big game for both teams, but especially so for the Patriots after they got blown out by the Packers at home last week. The Lions won at Miami and didn't play great, but they will get it going on offense here. New England is struggling on defense, so look for the Lions to win it with a strong offensive showing.
Pick: Lions 30, Patriots 24
The Chiefs snapped a two-game losing streak last week in beating the Jets , while the Falcons were blown out in Madrid by the Bengals . The defense had some major issues in that game. That will be the same here after the trade of safety Jessie Bates. Chiefs stack another victory.
Pick: Chiefs 23, Falcons 17
This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns . But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it.
Pick: Texans 21, Browns 20
The Packers are coming off an impressive road victory over the Patriots and Jordan Love has been on fire. But the Minnesota defense is special and now they have Kirk Cousins to play quarterback. Even so, look for the Packers to win another one as their defense limits Cousins and the offense.
Pick: Packers 27, Vikings 17
The Titans are coming off a bye, while the Jaguars are coming off a victory last Thursday at Baltimore. They will be rested too. Jacksonville is riding high as one of the top teams in the league and made some moves at the trade deadline to get even better. Though this is a rivalry, with some unpredictable games, this won't be. Jaguars big.
Pick: Jaguars 31, Titans 17
This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late.
Pick: Colts 23, Dolphins 22
This is an enormous game in the division, even though both teams have just three victories. The winner will be in first place. The Saints beat the Browns last week, while the Panthers have lost three straight. The Saints make it four in a row as Tyler Shough has a big day.
Pick: Saints 24, Panthers 21
The Bills are coming off a hard-fought road victory at Minnesota. The turnaround will be tough, but they are playing at a high level. The defense is improving. Look for Josh Allen to carve up the Jets' defense.
The Seahawks will start Drew Lock at quarterback again in this one. He was just OK last week against Arizona. But the Raiders have big-time defensive issues. For the Raiders, it's Fernando Mendoza time after they traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota. This is a tough defense for a first NFL start. Look for Lock to win it as the Seahawks' defense does the rest.
Pick: Seahawks 24, Raiders 16
The Rams lost at home to the Cardinals a few weeks ago and now must play without Puka Nacua . How will they move the ball? The Cardinals will start rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Going against Myles Garrett and company can be a problem. Rams win it, but it's low-scoring.
Pick: Rams 19, Cardinals 16
The Cowboys can't afford another loss in their division race, so this is a huge game for them. The 49ers are riding high and that offense will challenge the Dallas defense. But I think the Dallas offense will be even better. Upset special. Dak Prescott has a bigger day than Brock Purdy .
Pick: Cowboys 30, 49ers 28
This is for first place in the division. The Bengals are riding high behind their passing game and Joe Burrow . But the defense can't stop the run. The Steelers will run it here to keep Burrow off the field. It doesn't work. The Bengals will once again win it behind Burrow and the passing game.
Pick: Bengals 27, Steelers 21
This game had promise before the season, but the Ravens are without Lamar Jackson and the Chargers are 0-8. Jacoby Brissett will start for the Ravens, which should help the offense some. The Chargers have struggled on offense, but I think their defense will keep them in this. It's close.
Pick: Ravens 20, Chargers 17

title: Ranking NFL's greatest in-season trades of all-time: Where Kirk Cousins to Vikings ranks among top 10
summary: Tuesday's trade is already among the most notable in-season deals in league history
full_text:
While it was quiet for a while, there were plenty of fireworks during the final hours of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. The biggest trade was the one that sent quarterback Kirk Cousins back to Minnesota.
As it currently stands, that is already one of the most notable in-season trades in NFL history. Quarterbacks of Cousins' stature are almost never traded during a season, especially not to a team that is in position to possibly win a division title. Making this trade even more notable is that the Raiders, who received a third-round pick in exchange for Cousins, will now give the keys to the offense to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza .
Here's where the Cousins trade already ranks among the biggest in-season deals of all time.
The 1981 Chargers were involved in seismic trades, two of which included receivers. The first sent All-Pro John Jefferson to the Packers in a blockbuster trade that included a 1983 first-round pick and second-round picks in 1982 and 1984.
Two weeks after trading Jefferson, the Chargers traded for then-Saints receiver Wes Chandler, who provided an immediate spark for the "Air Coryell" offense. Chandler helped the Chargers advance to that year's AFC title game. He had 12 catches in two playoff games along with a big punt return for a score in the Chargers' overtime win over the Dolphins in the divisional round.
Chandler led the NFL in receiving yards and touchdown catches the following season and was named to the Pro Bowl three times during his first four seasons in San Diego. Jefferson, however, never again matched the level of success he had with the Chargers.
Wes Chandler 8️⃣9️⃣ pic.twitter.com/bYEvNBFbN9
Tuesday's trade has a chance to be one of the most consequential in NFL history. The trade officially signaled the beginning of the Mendoza era in Las Vegas, and it also infused life into a 6-2 Vikings team that desperately needed help at quarterback.
Tuesday's trade represented a full-circle moment for Cousins, who never wanted to leave Minnesota in the first place. After a two-plus year hiatus, Cousins will get another chance to lead the Vikings on a possible playoff run.
Rams GM Les Snead's "F them picks" philosophy eventually led to a Super Bowl win for the Rams. The trade for Ramsey two years earlier helped make that championship possible.
The Rams gave the Jaguars a first-round selection in the 2020 NFL Draft in addition to first- and fourth- round picks in the 2021 draft for Ramsey, who in 2017 had led the Jaguars within a game of the Super Bowl. Ramsey was named to the Pro Bowl during his first four seasons with the Rams. He had four picks, 16 pass breakups, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery during the Rams' Super Bowl-winning season.
After a 6-10 outfit in 1980, the 49ers were off to a 3-2 start in 1981 when they sent first- and second-round picks in the 1983 NFL Draft to the Chargers in exchange for Dean. Dean was a Pro Bowler each of the previous two years and also mired in a contract dispute.
Just days after coming to San Francisco, Dean had a pair of sacks while helping the 49ers record a 45-14 win over the Cowboys, the same team the 49ers would later defeat in the NFC title game. With the 49ers, Dean recorded 12 sacks in 11 games that season while helping San Francisco win their first Super Bowl. Dean helped San Francisco win another Super Bowl in 1984 before being inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2008.
#49ers greats Randy Cross and Ronnie Lott discuss the legend of Fred Dean. 🚬 "James Dean wasn't cooler than Fred Dean." Dean made his #FTTB debut, 43 years ago today — arguably the greatest mid-season acquisition in NFL history. October 11, 1981 pic.twitter.com/jYXDDsTYaK
Bobby Layne was Detroit royalty ... until he wasn't. Five years after leading the Lions to back-to-back NFL titles, Layne was traded to the Steelers just two weeks into the 1958 season. A year earlier, the Lions won their third title with Tobin Rote at quarterback after Layne broke his leg during the second-to-last game of the regular season.
At the time of the trade, Layne allegedly said that the Lions would not win for another 50 years, a statement that became known as the "Bobby Lane Curse." Detroit is still trying to win its first title since 1957.
Layne, who was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1967, played five seasons for the Steelers, earning two Pro Bowls over that span and posting a 27-19-2 record as the team's starting quarterback. He said in his autobiography that his biggest career regret was not winning a title in Pittsburgh.
In Week 5 of the 1983 season, the Raiders suffered their first loss after a 38-37 shootout to Washington, the defending Super Bowl champs who set the NFL single-season scoring record. Al Davis, the Raiders owner and general manager, responded by aggressively pursuing Mike Haynes, who was stuck in a contentious holdout with the Patriots .
While Davis offered Haynes a way out of his situation, Haynes acknowledged decades later that joining the Raiders wasn't an easy decision.
"I actually didn't like the Raiders at all," Haynes told CBS Sports in a 2020 interview . "I didn't like any other team except the Patriots. When Al Davis called, I actually had to think about it. The Raiders were the team where one of my teammates [receiver Darryl Stingley] was paralyzed. I had to think about all that. But I justified it because they had just moved from Oakland to L.A. I grew up in Los Angeles … In my head, I needed to do that to be open to going there. I told Mr. Davis I'd love to go there."
It ended up being a perfect fit for both parties. Haynes teamed up with Lester Hayes to form one of the best cornerback duos in NFL history. The duo shut down Hall of Fame receiver Steve Largent in the AFC title game, and in Super Bowl XVIII, they helped hold Washington's explosive offense to just nine points. The Raiders' 38-9 win remains one of the most surprising outcomes in Super Bowl history.
Haynes played six more seasons with the Raiders, earning three Pro Bowls over that span. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1997. The Patriots, who received a 1984 first-round pick and a 1985 second-round pick, reached the Super Bowl in 1985. Irving Fryer, who was drafted using the 1984 first-round pick, played a key role in the Patriots' first AFC title.
Despite rushing for over 1,000 yards in each of his first two seasons, Lynch was found to be expendable by the Bills midway through the 2010 season. Before the deadline, Buffalo traded Lynch to Seattle in exchange for a 2011 fourth-round pick and a 2012 fifth-round pick.
Simply put, Lynch and the Seahawks were the perfect fit. After running over the defending champion Saints in the 2010 wild card round, Lynch earned Pro Bowl honors in each of his first four full seasons in Seattle.
He was among Seattle's key figures during the team's Super Bowl run in 2013 and NFC Championship run in 2014. In six seasons with the Seahawks, Lynch rushed for 6,347 yards and 79 touchdowns during the regular season, plus 937 yards and nine scores in 11 postseason games.
McCaffrey was dealt to the 49ers in a blockbuster deal that landed the Panthers 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks, plus a fifth-rounder in 2024. The trade ended a six-year run in Carolina for McCaffrey, who was selected No. 8 overall in the 2017 NFL Draft .
The deal paid immediate dividends for both McCaffrey and the 49ers, who were 3-3 at the time of the trade. San Francisco reached the NFC title game that year before injuries proved too much to overcome. In 2023, however, the 49ers reached the Super Bowl behind a banner year from McCaffrey, who won his first rushing title that season. San Francisco had the lead in overtime in that year's Super Bowl before falling victim to Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes .
McCaffrey has remained a highly productive player for the 49ers. This past Sunday, he broke Marshall Faulk's record for the most career touchdown receptions (37) for a…
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: NFL pretenders and contenders after Week 9: NFC North is fierce, no faith in Giants and Steelers
summary: Breaking down all 14 teams currently in playoff position at the midway point to separate the legitimate Super Bowl threats from the impostors
full_text:
Now that we are halfway through the 2026 NFL season, it's time to start paying attention to the playoff picture -- and it's a pretty wild picture to look at right now.
The NFC North is the only division to ever feature four teams three or more games above .500 through Week 9, while the NFC South is the only division to feature four teams two or more games below .500. Is every NFC North team going to make the playoffs? And which NFC South team will likely go one-and-done in the postseason?
Below, we will break down the pretenders and contenders in the NFL right now. We will look at the 14 teams that would make the playoffs if the season ended today, and examine if they have a legitimate shot to hoist the Lombardi Trophy. Let's begin with the contenders.
Credit to CBS Sports Research
The 7-1 Buffalo Bills are off to their best eight-game start to a season since 1993, which was when they made their last Super Bowl appearance. Josh Allen is again an MVP favorite, James Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in seven straight games, and Jim Leonhard's defense left the Minnesota Vikings front office scrambling after Carson Wentz registered one of the worst quarterback showings in franchise history on Monday night. The Bills are again a contender.
The San Francisco 49ers are your Super Bowl favorites right now over at DraftKings Sportsbook (+540), and it's easy to understand why. They have started 7-1 or better for the first time since 2019, when they made the Super Bowl. Brock Purdy is an MVP favorite, and he leads an offense that is averaging 29.4 points per game -- which ranks No. 3 in the NFL. This past week against the Las Vegas Raiders , the 49ers scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. However, health will again be a major talking point when it comes to San Francisco. Wide receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are still sidelined, and defensive tackle Gracen Halton suffered a broken ankle on Sunday. If they can return some players for the stretch run, this could be the 49ers' year.
The Denver Broncos have been dancing with the devil all season in these one-score games, but I'll remind you Bo Nix and Co. did the same thing last year, and could have made the Super Bowl if Nix didn't suffer that ankle injury in the divisional round. The Broncos have won five straight games since their 2-2 start, and while they have the worst yard differential (-699) by any team that started 7-2 or better in NFL history, all Nix has done is step up in crunch time. He's 18-12 in his career when trailing in the second half, and 13-12 when trailing in the fourth quarter. Those are the best win percentages by any quarterback since 1970, with a minimum of 20 games. Defensively, Denver is giving up more yards per game than last year, but still ranks top 10 in scoring with 20.7 points allowed per game. You could make the case that the Broncos are pretenders, but I'm leaning the other way. They beat Josh Allen and the Bills in the playoffs last year, and have already defeated the Jacksonville Jaguars and Kansas City Chiefs this season. Denver could make the AFC Championship again.
The Jaguars are all-in this year. At the trade deadline, they sent a first-round pick, second-round pick, a future second-round pick, a future fifth-round pick and a conditional sixth-round pick for defensive tackle Jordan Davis , defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and safety Jessie Bates III . Giving up first- and second-round picks for Davis was shocking, but there's no doubt the Jaguars roster got better this week.
The Jags are running away with the AFC South at 6-2, and have as many wins as the rest of their rivals combined. They are 14-2 in their past 16 games dating back to last year, and Trevor Lawrence has statistically been the best quarterback during that stretch with 42 total touchdowns and a 108.8 passer rating. The Jaguars have the second-best scoring defense in the NFL (15.1 points allowed per game) and one of the best run defenses in the league as well, allowing just 89.3 yards per game. Justice Hill actually just became the first running back to rush for 75 yards against the Jags in 25 games.
The Chiefs got back on track this past week against the New York Jets , registering their largest win (23 points) since Week 7 in 2025. Kenneth Walker III also got back on track with 143 total yards and three touchdowns. There's still some concern around Patrick Mahomes ' passing game, but the addition of Josh Downs will be helpful. Chiefs receivers are averaging 117.5 yards per game, which ranks 28th in the NFL. That hasn't stopped Kansas City from having what is statistically the second-best offense in the NFL (384.1 yards per game).
This may be Joe Burrow's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games. Five of the previous seven players to score that many touchdowns through eight games won MVP. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. We know what Chase is capable of, but Higgins is having the best year of his NFL career. He's averaging 94.8 receiving yards per game and has caught six touchdowns in eight games.
Where there's concern with the Cincinnati Bengals is their rushing attack. The 85.6 rushing yards per game are the fewest by a team to start 6-2 or better since the 2014 Detroit Lions . We'll see if the Bengals can pass their way to a Super Bowl. Cincy's defense still isn't "great" statistically, but it's much improved compared to the past couple of seasons. That in itself gives the Bengals a legitimate shot.
It's hard not to like the Chicago Bears . They have an offensive madman scheming up talented weapons open downfield, a quarterback who looks like Josh Allen, and a defense that has been sparked by the addition of Jeffery Simmons . The Bears can't turn the ball over five times every game as they did on Sunday night, but I'm not too worried about that issue.
The Bears have the firepower offensively to be a Super Bowl contender, from the rushing attack to the passing attack, and a defense that is good enough to support a playoff run. The addition of Simmons affects that unit in more ways than one. He can stuff the run and can pressure the quarterback from the interior -- which in turn makes life easier on those in the secondary.
I'm on the fence with the Lions. We all know about the offense with Jared Goff , Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown , but the issue has always been Detroit's defense.
The reason I'll place the Lions in the "contender" category is that Kelvin Sheppard's unit has been better in recent weeks. After a disastrous start, the Lions have allowed just 15.5 points per game during this current four-game win streak. They were allowing 31.8 points per game during the 2-2 start. With Brian Branch back, hopefully Kerby Joseph soon, and the addition of Andre Cisco , I think the Lions can be a contender.
If I were power-ranking the teams in the NFC North, I would have the Green Bay Packers third or fourth. So, does that make them a contender or pretender? I'm still trying to figure that out.
The turnaround in Green Bay has been incredible. After that horrific 1-2 start, the Packers are playing better on both sides of the ball. Jordan Love is the best deep-ball thrower in the NFL, and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are looking like Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle did in Miami during those fun Mike McDaniel years. The two have combined for 1,662 receiving yards thus far. However, like the Bengals, the Packers can't run the ball. They rank dead last in rushing offense with 68.2 yards per game, and just lost Josh Jacobs to a broken finger.
I'm not placing money on the Packers to win the Super Bowl, but I can't get over how good this passing attack has been. Plus, the defense just picked off Drake Maye three times and will return Micah Parsons soon.
The Vikings were perhaps the most obvious pretender in the NFL…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline grades for every team: Four teams earn an A, Rams and Chargers among disappointments
summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and we've got a full report card for the league
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, a whirlwind of activity changing the NFL landscape halfway through the season. After countless rumors, reports and hypothetical moves, there were 18 trades between the beginning of the regular season and the trade deadline, including six on deadline day itself.
A quarterback reunion stole the show on Tuesday, with Kirk Cousins heading back to the Vikings in exchange for a third-round pick going to the Raiders . It's the second quarterback deal by Minnesota this year; the Vikings also sent J.J. McCarthy to the Giants . And if the postseason started today, McCarthy's Giants would host Cousins' Vikings in a wild-card matchup.
Defensive tackle, normally not a headlining position, was in the spotlight, with the Bears acquiring Jeffery Simmons from the Titans and the Jaguars acquiring Jordan Davis from the Eagles . Also on the move at the position were DeForest Buckner and Davon Godchaux .
Sometimes, though, it's the moves not made that tell a bigger story. Here's how all 32 teams fared with trade deadline grades for everyone in the league.
The Bills saw several other Super Bowl contenders making significant win-now moves and decided to make their own on deadline day, acquiring safety Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Titans for a 2027 second-round pick. It's a big move for a player in the middle of his best year: Hooker has five interceptions this year, including three off Joe Burrow in one game. Other Bills safeties have one pick combined. He is a versatile defender who's willing to tackle -- a strong addition to a Bills secondary that needed help. It was expensive, but worth doing. Buffalo got significantly better Tuesday.
It was a rough deadline day for the Dolphins : Quarterback Malik Willis landed on IR, and veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler -- a potential trade candidate -- is done for the season with ruptured biceps. The timing couldn't have been worse regarding Sieler. It might have been nice for this one-win team to get some compensation there.
The Patriots not making any moves was a bit of a surprise considering Rhamondre Stevenson is hurt (knee), TreVeyon Henderson is dealing with an illness, and the offensive line and wide receiver group are truly beat up. This felt like a chance for New England to improve Drake Maye's surroundings, even if it was just via modest improvements, but New England didn't make any moves.
The Jets got a sixth-round pick for trading Andre Cisco to the Lions but held otherwise. That was probably the right move, even with Will McDonald IV asking for a trade amid decreased playing time. If needed, they can act on that request this coming offseason. The Jets already did tremendous work last trade deadline and will have three first-round picks next year, giving them great flexibility.
The Ravens needed to make a move for a quarterback -- Joe Fagnano simply wasn't going to cut it -- and they did, paying a reasonable price, given the situation, for Jacoby Brissett . Best-case scenario, the Ravens stay alive long enough for Lamar Jackson to return. Worst-case scenario, at least they have a workable product. Trading for center Ryan Neuzil right at the deadline buzzer was an interesting move considering Baltimore had already traded for Cam Jurgens earlier this season; perhaps Neuzil moves to guard. The Jurgens move was a bit of an overpay.
The Bengals would hypothetically get a C for their effort on Tuesday, but they earned an F for the execution. They aimed to add EDGE Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles on deadline day, but the deal fell through after Cincinnati realized it would have lost its 2027 third-round compensation pick by acquiring Ebiketie. Oops! Bad look by Cincy, which did not end up making any moves.
The Browns held firm at the trade deadline, neither buying nor selling. Names such as wide receiver Jerry Jeudy's were in the rumor mill, but it's fine that Cleveland didn't make a move. He has ceded targets to talented rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion , but he is still playing over 60% of the team's offensive snaps. The Browns will battle for a playoff spot or at least to play spoiler and look to really make strides in 2027, when Deshaun Watson's contract ends.
The Steelers were reportedly on the hunt for a wide receiver, but nothing materialized for the AFC North leaders. Cornerback reinforcements might have been nice as well, considering the past health issues of Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr . and the age of Jalen Ramsey , but for now, Pittsburgh will look to keep it rolling with the group it has.
The Texans paid more for the name than the game when they traded for Marvin Harrison Jr. , sending a second-round pick to the Cardinals for a player who hasn't come close to living up to the hype. Harrison is yet to top three catches in any of his three games for Houston this season, and he still played less than half of his new team's snaps coming out of the bye in Week 9. Unless he becomes a more major contributor soon, the overpay looks even worse.
The Colts were the busiest sellers, sending Quenton Nelson to Seattle, Buckner and Keenan Allen to San Francisco and Josh Downs to Kansas City, but them not trading Jonathan Taylor was a gigantic missed opportunity. Taylor is almost 28 years old, and keeping him will only add wear and tear on his body. A contending team likely would have paid more now, with a half-season to go, then next year, when he will only be older and more worn down. The Colts have no chance of contending soon, either. Furthermore, the Colts also decided against moving Grover Stewart , who reportedly garnered mid-round pick interest. One can also wonder if the Colts got enough in the trades they did make, especially for Buckner.
The Jaguars did well acquiring safety Jessie Bates III , even if second- and fifth-round picks were a bit pricey. Bates is a tremendous playmaker (28 career interceptions, 14 career forced fumbles) joining a play-making unit; Jacksonville's defense has forced 15 turnovers, third-most this season. After losing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the season, getting defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to help in the middle was reasonable. But a first-round pick and a second-round pick for hulking defensive tackle Jordan Davis was a massive overpay, even if Davis were playing like he did last year, which was a contract year. He's a one-dimensional run plugger who had nine tackles for loss in 2025; he has eight in the rest of his career combined. The Jaguars paid a near-Jeffery Simmons price for a player nowhere near Simmons in terms of all-around talent or disruptiveness, even at his best. He can be a good player who helps -- the Jags will hope they get his best now that he's on a winning team -- and stopping the run is important. But from a value perspective, this was a poor deal. Keeping Brian Thomas Jr . was smart. For an all-in season, they had no need to trade him for future assets, and they can revisit a move this coming offseason.
Whether the Titans should have parted ways with Simmons or not is worth arguing, but the return is inarguable. Tennessee having extra first-round picks each of the next two years is outstanding business, and Cam Ward's recent improved play should make the Titans feel all the better. The extra picks will allow Tennessee to surround him with talent at several positions. Getting a second-round pick for Hooker is also good work; Tennessee wanted a strong return, and it got it. The Titans had other players to trade away, such as Tony Pollard , and it's worth wondering if they should have. For now, though, keeping a hot hand helps the young quarterback.
The Broncos quietly made a helpful deal, acquiring Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley for a couple of mid-round picks. Henley has plateaued a bit the past couple of seasons after a strong start, but he's an impressive athlete who could benefit from a change of scenery. Vance Joseph has gotten the most out of lots of players, and…

title: Cardinals post-NFL trade deadline moves & workouts
summary: The Arizona Cardinals weren’t buyers or sellers at the NFL trade deadline. They simply stood pat, and life – and the schedule – moved along. It was assumed that at least two Cardinals players would be shipped off to new homes, but that never happened. RELATED: CARDINALS TURN DOWN TRADE OFFER FOR BUDDA So, after […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 08: Michael Wilson #14 of the Arizona Cardinals warms up before a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on November 08, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals weren’t buyers or sellers at the NFL trade deadline. They simply stood pat, and life – and the schedule – moved along. It was assumed that at least two Cardinals players would be shipped off to new homes, but that never happened. RELATED: CARDINALS TURN DOWN TRADE OFFER FOR BUDDA So, after the trade deadline, there was plenty of activity with the franchise. Roster moves The big news is that the Cardinals announced they had placed QB Gardner Minshew on IR. There was some question as to whether Minshew would need to be placed on IR, or if his torn UCL in his throwing arm wasn’t as serious as first thought. But it was. The word is that it could be season-ending, but that has not been confirmed. There are some non-trade Cardinals moves today: – QB Gardner Minshew, WR Michael Wilson to IR. – Officially sign QB Josh Johnson and QB Joey Aguilar – Sign veteran WR Phillip Dorsett to PS — Darren Urban (@Cardschatter) November 10, 2026 Arizona also placed WR Michael Wilson officially on IR as expected. He injured his neck on the fourth offensive play during last week’s game against the Seattle Seahawks. But get this: He played the entire game. One word: Ironman. Obviously, both of these injuries are crippling events for the offense. This side of the ball is already without OT Paris Johnson, WRs Jalen Brooks and Kendrick Bourne, OG Chase Bisontis, RBs Jeremiyah Love and James Conner, and TE Tip Reiman. The only other roster move is that WR Phillip Dorsett was signed to the practice squad. Dorsett (5’-10”, 185 pounds) was a beast in college at Miami, where he was clocked at 4.33 in the 40. As a senior, he led the conference in average yards per catch (24.2) and touchdowns (10). He was drafted 29 th overall in the first round of the 2015 NFL Draft by the Indianapolis Colts, but after two seasons, he was traded to the New England Patriots for QB Jacoby Brissett. Arizona is his 10 th NFL club. Now age 33, Dorsett has been signed to six different practice squads. He did not appear in any regular-season NFL games in 2024, 2025, or this year. Obviously, the receiver position is a need for the Cardinals. Dorsett joins WR Shedrick Jackson and WR/KR James Proche on the practice squad. Center Hjalte Froholdt is on concussion protocol from the Seahawks game. That usually takes 10 days to get clearance, which most likely means he won’t be available for the home contest this weekend against the Los Angeles Rams. The depth chart lists Kingsley Eguakun as his backup. He has played in seven NFL games with two starts. Workout news On Tuesday, while the league was swirling with trade news, the Cardinals worked out five players: QB Cooper Rush, age 32 QB Trevor Siemian, age 34 WR Phillip Dorsett, age 33 WR Malick Meiga, age 25 WR Eli Pancol, age 26 At one time, Rush (6’-3”, 224 pounds) was considered the heir apparent to the starting quarterback position with the Dallas Cowboys. This is his ninth NFL season, and he has been a member of three NFL clubs. He has played in 44 games with 18 starts, thrown for 3,995 yards with a 60.8% completion ratio, and thrown 21 TDs to 18 picks. He appeared in two games for the Atlanta Falcons this year before being released on October 19. Siemian (6’-3”, 220 pounds) is a former seventh-round selection of the Denver Broncos who eventually became the starter in his second year after Peyton Manning retired. He ended up on IR after Week 15, and then was traded to the Minnesota Vikings for a fifth-round pick, but never played backing up Kirk Cousins. He ended up on three other NFL rosters. He was placed on two practice squads in 2023 and 2024, and hasn’t played a single down since the 2023 season. Meiga (6’-4”, 201 pounds) played for Coastal Carolina with a 16.7 average yards per reception and went undrafted in the 2024 NFL Draft. He signed with the Seahawks and then the Carolina Panthers. He is Canadian-born. Meiga has not appeared in any regular-season games. Pancol (6’-3”, 205 pounds) went undrafted in 2025 after a good career at Duke. He signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars and was waived in August with an injury designation as part of final roster cuts. He then signed with the Indianapolis Colts, who placed him on their practice squad but he was not re-signed for 2026. He was placed on the practice squad of the Denver Broncos on October 27, then waived on November 3. He has not appeared in any regular-season games. Out of the five, Dorsett was the only player signed to a deal. Often, teams bring in guys to update their free agent database in the event a player (or two) becomes injured, but in this case, both the quarterback and receiver positions were recently hit with the injury bug, so talent was brought in for a closer look. Bonus news At the movies, sometimes there is a short little blurb right after the credits have ended. Every CG cartoon has one, as do the horror and superhero flicks. So, this is our blurb for those who are still reading. RB Dameon Pierce was a fourth-round draft pick of the Houston Texans back in 2022 and became a Pro Bowl alternate that same year. His highlight was a 98-yard kickoff return for a touchdown in 2023. After his four-year rookie contract expired in 2025, the Texans decided to keep Nick Chubb instead. Pierce was signed by the Kansas City Chiefs to their practice squad and then was elevated to the main roster in late December. In free agency this year, he signed a one-year $1.29 million deal with the Philadelphia Eagles, but was a last-day cut and then signed to their practice squad. Before Week 6, Pierce was elevated to the main roster. He suffered a hamstring injury, and Philly released him with an injury settlement. He is now a free agent. Seven teams have reached out to his agent: San Francisco, Miami, Tennessee, Baltimore, Jacksonville, Carolina, and the Cardinals. Arizona has three running backs on its active roster: Tyler Allgeier, Bam Knight, and Evan Hull, plus veteran Jerome Ford on the practice squad. They are expecting James Conner to return at some point. What does this mean for the team to go fishing on Pierce? Knight has had some injury issues, but with the availability of Ford, why the looksy? Does this indicate that the team doesn’t have any confidence in Conner’s return this season? Hmmm……

title: Week 9, 3 up and 3 down: A disappointing result triggers a sell-off
summary: The Atlanta Falcons Spanish expedition was fruitless, and the team returned to the States with another L to their name. The front office responded by doing something we haven’t seen in years: sell off assets. There were role players with good contributions to highlight, but a handful of starters let the team down. Here’s the […]
full_text: Falcon's tight end #89 Charlie Woerner (L) throws a pass during the 2026 NFL Madrid Game American football match between Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid, on November 8, 2026. The National Football League return to Madrid with this 2026 NFL regular season game for the second time following 2025 first edition at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons Spanish expedition was fruitless, and the team returned to the States with another L to their name. The front office responded by doing something we haven’t seen in years: sell off assets. There were role players with good contributions to highlight, but a handful of starters let the team down. Here’s the Week 9, 3 down and 3 down. 3 up Ian Cunningham The Falcons are 3-6, and while they are technically in play for the NFC South title, that’s not good enough for Cunningham, and that’s a refreshing mentality. It’s never easy losing a player like Jessie Bates , but with free agency looming and the team being far from a Super Bowl-caliber roster, Cunningham made the trade with an eye toward the future, collecting a 2nd and 5th-round pick. He also made a buzzer-beater trade that shipped Ryan Neuzil to the Ravens and netted the team a 2028 6th-round pick and Andrew Vorhees. Neuzil doesn’t fit this new scheme, and instead of getting nothing for him and knowing the comp formula wouldn’t go their way with future spending, the GM took a proactive approach. Charlie Woerner Woerner has been pretty steady after a slow start and had himself a respectable game. While the Falcons run game has been in a slump, it’s not due to him. On the Falcons best runs you’ll almost always find Woerner in the mix. He wins most of his battles against opposing linebackers and can be quite stout on the edge. It was nice to see the team reward him early with a touchdown. He still needs to work on that Tush Push, but that’s gonna be hard to do behind the centers on the roster, especially when Dexter Lawrence is across from you. Charlie Woerner had a solid outing, nice seeing him get rewarded early with a TD pic.twitter.com/ZL8YchRuNr — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 11, 2026 LaCale London London is a bargain for what he provides. His presence was felt against the Bengals; he had two pressures, a sack, and a tough run stop on the goal line. Year after year, he’s proven he can handle double teams and make plays off pure effort. He’s a glue guy that plays with an edge, and every roster needs guys like these. London is playing on a one-year deal and looks like a no-brainer for a new contract in 2027. We know LaCale London is strong at the point of attack, but his lateral movement has been a lot better this year, and you never need to question his motor pic.twitter.com/HPthYprLIc — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 11, 2026 3 down A.J. Terrell Terrell got worked early and often in this matchup. Ja’Marr Chase picked up where he left off in the 2019 National Championship, and had his way with Terrell. Tee Higgins was also able to haul in a touchdown on the corner. Man, press, zone—it didn’t matter what the coverage was; Terrell got scorched. It has been somewhat of a down year for the corner, who spent time on IR, but this game has fans irate. I understand where they’re coming from, but this did happen against the best QB-WR pair in the league, and it’s not like the Falcons are better off without Terrell, for now. Still, his days as a top-flight corner in this league are fading. Terrell loses immediately at the line and Watts can't get over the top in time. If you're gonna line up in press, press pic.twitter.com/o2VPZ2kcRN — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 11, 2026 Divine Deablo It was another rough performance for the linebacker, who has taken a massive step back during his second year in Atlanta. I respect his willingness to play through injury, but it’s hurting the team, and his odds of getting anything more than a cheap one-year deal somewhere in 2027. He can’t even perform a form tackle right now. If it was just his body breaking down, that’d be one thing, but his coverage drops have been sloppy, and he isn’t diagnosing plays close to the speed he was last year. He may have been an X-factor in 2025, but he is one of the weak links in 2026. If a player is so injured that they're unwilling to throw their arms to make an open field tackle they probably shouldn't be playing pic.twitter.com/aaCDaEO3fM — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 11, 2026 Nick Folk I begged for Folk to be cut and Cunningham delivered. It was one thing when the missed kicks happened from the 50s, but from 38?! Folk will still be remembered as one of the best to do it over the past decade, but unfortunately he ran out of gas when he got to Atlanta. The Falcons are 3-6 and without some familiar names heading into Week 10. The team is in full evaluation mode, and while it’s hard to get excited about that in-season, it’s the right call.

title: Winners and losers from Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars
summary: The Baltimore Ravens’ 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars was their third consecutive game decided by at least 22 points. There was more bad than good in this one for the Ravens, as you would expect in such a lopsided contest. Winners RB Justice Hill: Hill was one of the few bright spots for Baltimore […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - NOVEMBER 05: Marlon Humphrey #44 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium on November 5, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens’ 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars was their third consecutive game decided by at least 22 points. There was more bad than good in this one for the Ravens, as you would expect in such a lopsided contest. Winners RB Justice Hill: Hill was one of the few bright spots for Baltimore on Thursday night. The seventh-year veteran showed he still had burst on a 65-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. Hill’s 85 rushing yards were the most allowed to a single player by the Jaguars in their last 24 games. C Cam Jurgens: Jurgens rebounded from a poor game last week with a solid outing against Jacksonville. His 72.7 PFF grade was the highest of any offensive player for the Ravens. RG Vega Ioane: Ioane’s return to the lineup after missing the previous game with a knee injury was a welcome sight. The rookie’s 66.7 PFF grade was only behind Jurgens among offensive players. RT Roger Rosengarten: Rosengarten allowed zero pressures against the Jaguars and was third among offensive players with a 66.4 PFF grade. Losers QB Joe Fagnano: The rookie undrafted quarterback making his first start on a short week with an injured ankle played how you would expect. Fagnano struggled to move the ball through the air, racking up just 60 yards on 18 attempts, while throwing two interceptions. LG John Simpson: Simpson has been perhaps the most criticized starter on Baltimore’s offensive line after signing a three-year, $30 million contract this offseason. His 4.5 pass-blocking grade against Jacksonville should only stoke the flames. TE Mark Andrews: Highly-paid veterans continue to let the Ravens down this season, and no player exemplifies that more than their once Pro Bowl tight end. Andrews and Ronnie Stanley appear to be in competition at this point for who can have the most false starts, as the duo committed the penalty on consecutive plays to move the ball back 10 yards on second down. Andrews later fumbled the handoff on a fourth down, turning the ball over on downs. CB Marlon Humphrey: Humphrey continues to draw the ire of fans with comments made off the field, and his play on it only strengthens the criticism. Humphrey allowed a 52-yard completion to a tight end on the game’s opening drive when he appeared to get stuck watching Trevor Lawrence on a scramble, allowing the rookie Nate Boerkircher to get behind him down the field. WR LaJohntay Wester: Wester has failed to make much of an impact in the return game this season, and his lost fumble on a kickoff against the Jaguars could put his job security in question.

title: Ravens film study: Keyon Martin, T.J. Tampa could be secondary’s future
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars handed the Baltimore Ravens their fourth consecutive loss on Thursday night, extending a disappointing midseason skid that has left the team searching for answers on both sides of the football. Despite the loss, three Ravens delivered noteworthy performances that could have significant implications moving forward. Keyon Martin flashed his versatility and physicality […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - NOVEMBER 05: Keyon Martin #38 of the Baltimore Ravens lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium on November 5, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars handed the Baltimore Ravens their fourth consecutive loss on Thursday night, extending a disappointing midseason skid that has left the team searching for answers on both sides of the football. Despite the loss, three Ravens delivered noteworthy performances that could have significant implications moving forward. Keyon Martin flashed his versatility and physicality in the nickel, T.J. Tampa provided much-needed run support from the outside cornerback position, and Cam Jurgens continued to strengthen Baltimore’s rushing attack with his work along the interior offensive line. CB Keyon Martin 23 snaps | 12 run defense | 2 pass rush | 9 coverage | 1 pressure | 4 tackles Keyon Martin played a versatile role against Jacksonville, lining up in the slot on 18 of his 23 defensive snaps. Martin made his presence felt primarily in run support, showing the physicality and willingness to come downhill that Baltimore has been missing from its secondary. He also provided value as a blitzer, giving the Ravens another option to generate pressure from the nickel position. Keyon Martin plays like he was shot out of a cannon pic.twitter.com/W7KPTCSH8A — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) November 7, 2026 On one rep, Martin worked up toward the line of scrimmage on a run blitz, fitting his gap and making the tackle for a minimal gain. On another, he did an excellent job shocking Jaguars receiver Parker Washington at the point of attack, creating an angle to disengage and make the tackle on the ball carrier. As a blitzer, Martin flashed his awareness by working into Trevor Lawrence’s throwing lane and getting his hands up to disrupt the passing window, forcing an incompletion. Martin’s emergence as a potential starting nickel could be an important development for a Ravens secondary that has struggled throughout its midseason skid. His ability to contribute in run support, blitz off the edge, and play with physicality in the slot gives Baltimore a versatile defensive back who could see an expanded role moving forward. With the secondary searching for answers, Martin has an opportunity to establish himself as a consistent contributor. T.J. Tampa 27 snaps | 16 run defense | 11 coverage | 3 tackles T.J. Tampa flashed in his opportunity at outside cornerback against Jacksonville, particularly with his willingness to come downhill and contribute in run support. Tampa recorded two defensive stops against the run and showed the physicality needed to set the edge and finish tackles in space. In coverage, he was targeted just once, allowing an 18-yard reception across his 11 coverage snaps. TJ Tampa in run support pic.twitter.com/CgeaXzpIIy — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) November 7, 2026 On one rep, Tampa worked downhill from his outside cornerback alignment, navigating through traffic to meet the ball carrier and secure the tackle for a short gain. On another outside run, he did an excellent job shocking an oncoming blocker at the point of attack, disengaging and making the tackle on the running back. Tampa’s ability to work through traffic, take on blockers, and maintain his positioning stood out, especially for a Ravens secondary that has struggled with tackling and run support. With Marlon Humphrey struggling, Baltimore could look to expand Tampa’s role at outside cornerback moving forward. His physicality as a tackler and natural instincts in zone coverage give the Ravens an intriguing option on the perimeter. While his coverage ability will need to be evaluated over a larger sample size, Tampa’s willingness to contribute against the run could provide Baltimore with some much-needed stability at the position. Cam Jurgens 56 snaps | 33 run blocking | 23 pass blocking | 1 pressure allowed Cam Jurgens continued to provide stability along Baltimore’s interior offensive line against Jacksonville, allowing just one pressure across 23 pass-blocking snaps. However, his most impressive contributions came in the running game, where he consistently showed his ability to work laterally, flip his hips, and climb to the second level to create running lanes. His athleticism and spatial awareness were particularly noticeable on zone and duo concepts. Cam Jurgens run blocking pic.twitter.com/I8Il5swHSH — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) November 7, 2026 On one outside zone rep, Jurgens worked laterally to assist a fellow offensive lineman before climbing to the second level and pancaking a defender, creating additional space for the running back. On another rep, he did an excellent job flipping his hips to establish leverage and create a narrow rushing lane. On a duo concept, Jurgens worked through his initial assignment before climbing to the second level and sealing off a defender, opening a clean lane for the running back to accelerate through. With Jacoby Brissett stepping into the offense, Baltimore will need to lean heavily on its rushing attack to remain competitive while awaiting a potential late-season return from Lamar Jackson. That starts with Derrick Henry, whose physical running style becomes increasingly valuable as the weather gets colder and defenses are forced to tackle him over the course of a game. Jurgens’ ability to create movement at the point of attack, reach the second level, and open rushing lanes could make him an integral piece of Baltimore’s offensive identity down the stretch.

title: Ravens discussion: reactions to Ryan Neuzil trade
summary: The Baltimore Ravens swung a last-minute trade-deadline deal with the Atlanta Falcons to acquire center Ryan Neuzil in exchange for guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s reactions to the move; be sure to add yours in the comments section below! Nikhil Mehta This is ultimately a minor trade that […]
full_text: Dec 21, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Atlanta Falcons offensive lineman Ryan Neuzil (64) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens swung a last-minute trade-deadline deal with the Atlanta Falcons to acquire center Ryan Neuzil in exchange for guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s reactions to the move; be sure to add yours in the comments section below! Nikhil Mehta This is ultimately a minor trade that will, in all likelihood, have little or no impact on either team’s short- or long-term future. But I still like it. The Ravens have watched three centers go down this year and acquired Cam Jurgens as their new starter, a player with his own injury history. So upgrading from Kyle Hergel to Neuzil at backup is a sensible move at such a low cost. No one in Baltimore will miss Vorhees, and the Ravens could quickly get a compensatory 2028 Day 3 pick (likely a seventh-, maybe a sixth-rounder) when Neuzil leaves in the offseason. The only wrinkle is that ideally, he does not play a snap in purple and black, likely lowering his free agent valuation in the offseason and reducing the chances of another comp pick for Eric DeCosta. Still, that last factor makes this a head-scratcher from the Falcons’ end. Why did the they give up a starting lineman for an unneeded backup and a draft pick they would receive if Neuzil signed even a low-end starting contract in the offseason? As the Ravens found out the hard way, the NFL’s center ranks are quietly very thin, so simply being able to snap the football and hold down the fort can earn good money. A strong finish to the year could have raised Neuzil’s value further, and it’s not like Atlanta’s new regime does not know how to play the com ppick game. They are projected to net two extra picks in 2027 as a result of this offseason’s moves, per OverTheCap , their most since 2021. I’m sure they have their reason(s); I just can’t see them. Kevin McNelis I understand the front office standing pat at the deadline for the most part, even if I don’t agree with it. This felt like an opportune time for the Ravens to try to sell off some of their more bloated contracts, but based on the lack of large moves outside of Jordan Davis, maybe they just felt like the market wasn’t there. The pessimist/cynic in me says that they hold a stubborn belief that this team has more viability than it appears, and I hope they’re right, because otherwise, they missed a window. The Neuzil acquisition makes sense given his familiarity with Coach Ledford, and maybe the staff just felt like they reached the end of the road with Andrew Vorhees. Elsewhere, I didn’t see much that would have been a quick fix for any of Baltimore’s holes, but there was a small part of me hoping that after Cincy’s deal for Arnold Ebiketie fell through we’d see Baltimore swoop in and grab him. Ebiketie played his high school ball in Maryland, and I know he would’ve embraced the chance to provide a much-needed boost to the pass rush. Dustin Cox I would have personally preferred for the Ravens to be sellers at this year’s deadline, but I understand why Eric DeCosta wouldn’t go that route of there is a real chance of Lamar Jackson coming back this season. I am rather indifferent towards the trade for Ryan Neuzil as I believe it to be nothing more than a move to bolster depth at center behind Cam Jurgens. I don’t believe that he will replace John Simpson at left guard, like I have seen some speculating, as he has only player center in the NFL and I can’t see the Ravens sending Simpson to the bench after handing him a three-year, $30 million deal this offseason. Frank Platko I would have personally preferred for the Ravens to be sellers at this year’s deadline, but I understand why Eric DeCosta wouldn’t go that route of there is a real chance of Lamar Jackson coming back this season. I am rather indifferent towards the trade for Ryan Neuzil as I believe it to be nothing more than a move to bolster depth at center behind Cam Jurgens. I don’t believe that he will replace John Simpson at left guard, like I have seen some speculating, as he has only player center in the NFL and I can’t see the Ravens sending Simpson to the bench after handing him a three-year, $30 million deal this offseason. Now, it’s your turn! How did you react to the Ravens trading for Ryan Neuzil?
