title: Best available free agent edge rushers for Bengals to target after failed Arnold Ebiketie trade
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals rarely make a trade at the deadline, which is why it was somewhat surprising that a trade was reported on Tuesday when they (briefly) acquired Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles. However, the trade seems to have dissolved behind the scenes after the team realized the deal would also cost them a third-round […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals rarely make a trade at the deadline, which is why it was somewhat surprising that a trade was reported on Tuesday when they (briefly) acquired Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles. However, the trade seems to have dissolved behind the scenes after the team realized the deal would also cost them a third-round compensatory pick they are hoping to receive from Trey Hendrickson signing with the Ravens. Then, for the rest of the deadline, no more moves were made, although it is unknown if any more trades were attempted or if they elected to stand pat once the Ebiketie deal fell through. The attempted trade for Ebiketie, though, is a clear indicator that the Bengals are not happy with the depth of their defensive end room. Cashius Howell is on IR for an unknown amount of time, and Shemar Stewart is getting few snaps and was even a healthy inactive for a game. With all of that, the failed trade, and no more trade possibilities, the Bengals could target the position through one of the free agents still available on the market, so let’s take a look at the top available defensive ends. Joey Bosa The 31-year-old Bosa was one of the top edge rushers in the NFL for most of his career; he last played in Buffalo in 2025 on a one-year, $12 million deal. In the offseason, he was in the discussion for many fanbases, but no rumored meetings or potential signings popped up, and in the summer it was hinted he may have even quietly retired, with Adam Schefter saying he may have played his final snap. However, in the last month there has been more buzz about him possibly coming back and joining a team for a run to the Super Bowl, mainly his previous team, the Bills, or joining his brother Nick Bosa in San Francisco. It is not impossible to imagine, though, a world where he wants to join his close friend Joe Burrow in Cincinnati for a title run as well, and the Bengals should not hesitate to call and see if it is possible. Leonard Floyd The 34-year-old Floyd is another older pass rusher who was productive relatively recently, now getting a lot of buzz as a potential addition for teams looking to make a Super Bowl push. On a one-year, $10 million deal in 2025, Floyd had a decent year and can still get involved as a pass rusher. The Bengals should be a desirable destination for any free agent edge rushers with their talented offense and impactful interior, giving edge rushers a lot of one-on-one matchups in obvious passing situations. As a rotational pass rusher, Floyd would fit exactly what the Bengals need. Haason Reddick The 32-year-old Reddick was one of the best pass rushers in the league for several years and was a double-digit sack player with Philadelphia. His production in recent years has really taken a nosedive, but the Bengals could sign him with the hope that he has fresh legs, not playing most of the year, and could be effectively deployed in a limited capacity to keep him fresh. If Reddick could find something even close to his 2023 form, he could be extremely impactful. Yetur Gross-Matos The youngest player on the list by a long shot, 28-year-old Yetur Gross-Matos signed a two-year deal with the 49ers in free agency in 2024. During that contract, though, he missed roughly half of his games with the team and wasn’t a consistent performer in the games he did play in. Gross-Matos did have flashes, and with him now either healthy or very close to it after a knee injury last year, he could be one of the more intriguing options, since he is still young and could have several years of impactful football ahead of him. The Bengals have quite a few options available if they want some fresh legs and some help in the pass-rushing department. If they were willing to spend a sixth-round pick, they should be more than willing to spend a few million dollars if it is the difference-maker in getting the Super Bowl win. What free agent defensive end would you target?

title: Ja’Marr Chase says 2026 Bengals are better than 2021 Super Bowl team
summary: Cincinnati Bengals superstar wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase has done a lot of winning in his football career and has been a part of many talented teams at different levels. From playing in the LHSAA Division I state championship game his sophomore season, to winning the NCAA National Championship in 2019 to going to the Super […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals superstar wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase has done a lot of winning in his football career and has been a part of many talented teams at different levels. From playing in the LHSAA Division I state championship game his sophomore season, to winning the NCAA National Championship in 2019 to going to the Super Bowl in 2021, he’s been on fantastic teams. He says the 2026 Bengals are the best. When Chase was asked if the 6-2 Bengals are the best Bengals team he’s played for, he said yes, and it’s not particularly close. “I would say, by far [this team is the best Bengals team I’ve played on],” he told Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer on Tuesday . “I know we went to the Super Bowl. We had a good run with those guys. This is another great group we have… Honestly, I think the whole team is one unit.” The Bengals’ improbable Super Bowl run following the 2021 season, and their narrow loss in the AFC Championship game the following season, were their last two playoff appearances. After three straight seasons of no playoff football, and a roster turnover on the defensive side of the ball, the Bengals are hoping to get back to the postseason once the 2026 regular season comes to an end. Burrow and the offense have put up staggering numbers over the last three weeks. If that trend continues, the sky’s the limit. What do you think? Are the 2026 Bengals better than the 2021 squad?

title: Dohnte Meyers continues excelling in the 3rd receiver role
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 on Sunday in Madrid, Spain. The Bengals offense put on a show for the international crowd to improve to 6-2 on the season. Andrei Iosivas has been on injured reserve since Week 3 with a torn ligament in his thumb. The injury required surgery, but the staff […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 on Sunday in Madrid, Spain. The Bengals offense put on a show for the international crowd to improve to 6-2 on the season. Andrei Iosivas has been on injured reserve since Week 3 with a torn ligament in his thumb. The injury required surgery, but the staff has indicated that he is close to making a return to the 53-man roster. When he does, it should not come at the expense of offensive snaps for Dohnte Meyers. Meyers provides more of an explosive weapon when he is in the lineup over Iosivas. When he goes into motion, that is something teams have to be cognizant of. His ability to take an end around or jet sweep when in motion is an added weapon that can help to open things up offensively. The Bengals were able to get one of these to Meyers early in the game on Sunday, and he proceeded to take it 16 yards before Jessie Bates was able to make a potential touchdown-saving stop. Dohnte Meyers should not lose snaps when Yoshi comes back pic.twitter.com/KgBpXygRVE — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 8, 2026 Meyers has also started to develop some chemistry with Joe Burrow the last couple of weeks. We have seen big plays on a Burrow scramble each of the last two weeks. His ability to get open for his quarterback in those situations and make chunk plays should not go unnoticed. The one last week came in a critical moment with the Bengals needing to tie the game to send it to overtime against the Titans. The one this week was a big play that helped the Bengals add a field goal right before halftime to take a 24-10 lead. Joe Burrow to Dohnte Meyers for the big gain right before halftime. Great play by Burrow and then Meyers with the run after catch for additional yards. pic.twitter.com/fhCAPZyrtq — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 8, 2026 What Meyers can do after the catch is something the Bengals don’t really have outside of Ja’Marr Chase in their offense. He can make guys miss out in space, and is one of the most elusive players on the roster. That element is a dynamic that needs to continue getting plenty of snaps each game, regardless of Andrei Iosivas eventually coming back to the lineup. That doesn’t mean Iosivas doesn’t have a role at all on this team going forward, but I think Dohnte Meyers has overtaken his spot in the lineup as the third receiver. Meyers is also under contract going forward, whereas Iosivas is in the last year of his deal.
author: Dale Altman

title: Bengals Film Room: Joe Burrow now a frontrunner for MVP?
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals put on a show in Madrid, Spain, defeating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17. Quarterback Joe Burrow was 24 for 29 for 271 yards. He threw 3 touchdown passes and, most importantly, did not throw an interception this week. Jordan Love currently leads the NFL in passing yards with 2,618 yards on the season. […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals put on a show in Madrid, Spain, defeating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17. Quarterback Joe Burrow was 24 for 29 for 271 yards. He threw 3 touchdown passes and, most importantly, did not throw an interception this week. Jordan Love currently leads the NFL in passing yards with 2,618 yards on the season. Burrow is currently second with 2,386 passing yards. It is important to note that Burrow has also played one less game than Jordan Love this year. Burrow has a better completion rate, completing an elite 74% of his passes this season. Burrow is also leading the league in touchdown passes, having thrown 23 of them already this season. It isn’t just the stats that are jumping out for Burrow; he is in full control of an explosive Cincinnati offense that is firing on all cylinders. Let’s take a look at some of his biggest plays from the win against Atlanta. After the Falcons drove down the field and scored a touchdown to start the game, Joe Burrow and the offense were able to answer right back. The biggest play of the drive came on a 47-yard touchdown strike to Ja’Marr Chase. The Bengals tried to hit that play last week, with Burrow not getting enough on the ball and ultimately throwing an interception. That wasn’t the case this week, as he hit Chase in stride to help tie the game up 7-7. Burrow missed Chase on this deep ball last week, but not this time. Perfect throw from Burrow to Chase. The camera guy must have thought he was Jeff Blake for a second… pic.twitter.com/S5SARC48zJ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 After an Atlanta Falcons field goal, the Bengals offense was able to drive right down the field again. Burrow got some incredible catches from his wide receivers on this drive. The first one was a 7-yard completion to Tee Higgins on a third down that allowed the Bengals to keep the drive alive. Higgins caught the ball with strong hands in traffic. He was also being held on the ball, though no flag was thrown. Joe Burrow to Tee Higgins for 7 yards and the 1st down conversion. pic.twitter.com/A6MQTC2aKF — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Not long after that completion, it was Ja’Marr Chase making a spectacular play for his quarterback. Burrow threw a pass a bit too far out in front of Ja’Marr. The defender thought he had an interception, until Ja’Marr decided to snag the ball out of the air with one hand. He immediately turned upfield for yards after the catch. Nah Ja’Marr, you are an alien pic.twitter.com/bXbNmGTAva — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Burrow and the offense were able to get up to the line quickly after getting down to the 1-yard line on this drive. Burrow caught the Falcons off guard and called his own number for the quarterback sneak. He recorded his second rushing touchdown in as many weeks as a result. This score put the Bengals up 14-10. Falcons moving around and Burrow sneaks it in for the touchdown and 14-10 lead. pic.twitter.com/BTXWk3Mati — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 After the defense forced a Falcons punt, Joe Burrow and the offense were back on the field for their third series of the game. They started the drive with Burrow going to Ja’Marr Chase once again. This time for a 31-yard catch-and-run. Burrow to Chase for 31 yards kicks off the Bengals third drive of the game. Shoutout to the 🐐Drew Sample getting down the field to pick up a block. pic.twitter.com/hKPYGcESBa — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Burrow displayed his toughness on a crucial third down during the drive. He had to scramble out to his right and was able to extend the play just long enough to get a patented Ja’Marr is down there somewhere pass off. Burrow got leveled on the play, but the result was a big completion to a diving Chase down the field for another first down. Burrow gets absolutely leveled here but still gets enough on the pass for Ja’Marr to come back and dive for the reception and keep the chains moving. pic.twitter.com/dzlJqkJZW1 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 With pressure coming off the left side of the line, Burrow was able to convert another crucial third down on this drive. He had to double clutch, but stood tall in the pocket and delivered a pass that only his receiver could catch. That receiver just so happened to be Ja’Marr Chase again, who made a spectacular extension for the ball while getting his feet down just in bounds in the process. The Joe Burrow to Ja’Marr Chase connection was strong in the first half, with Chase going for over 140 receiving yards and a touchdown. Filthy stuff from Burrow to Chase. Huge conversion with 6:34 left in the first half and up 14-10. Phenomenal toe tap job by Ja’Marr. pic.twitter.com/TMobi9T99X — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Speaking of quarterback-to-receiver connections that have been on fire all season, Joe Burrow found Tee Higgins for the touchdown to cap off this drive. Burrow threw a perfect strike to Higgins just inside the end zone. Tee once again displayed strong hands to extend the Bengals’ lead to 21-10. The Joe Burrow to Tee Higgins connection has been en fuego all season pic.twitter.com/VFN3Bsnbsj — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 It isn’t just the top two receivers that Burrow has been finding for big plays this season either. Dohnte Meyers had a big play last week to help the Bengals ultimately force overtime and get the victory against Tennessee. This week it wasn’t as dramatic of a moment, but Burrow once again scrambled out and was able to hit Meyers for a big play before halftime. The Bengals would ultimately kick a field goal on this drive, making their lead 24-10 at halftime. Joe Burrow to Dohnte Meyers for 42 yards before the half to set up an Evan McPherson field goal. pic.twitter.com/MY6SDCeNLZ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Burrow and the rest of the offense didn’t have to do a whole lot the rest of the way, but after Atlanta cut the lead to 24-17 in the third quarter, they did need to put together another scoring drive. That is exactly what they were able to do. Maybe one of the most impressive plays of the game for Joe Burrow was the touchdown at the end of this one. He went through his progression, stood tough in the pocket, and delivered an absolute strike to Tee Higgins in the middle of the end zone. That touchdown put the Bengals back up by two scores, a lead that was too much to overcome for the Atlanta Falcons. Burrow stands in the pocket as long as possible going through his progressions, and then throws a strike to Tee Higgins in the middle of the end zone while taking a hit. pic.twitter.com/QbDuqZahxH — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 It is only halfway through the season, so there is a ton of football to be played. With that said, Joe Burrow is firmly in everyone’s midseason conversations for MVP. It won’t just be up to him to keep playing at the level he is; the defense will also have to find ways to continue helping to win games. The MVP award is typically going to be given to a player who is part of a team with a lot of regular-season wins. A win against Pittsburgh in primetime Sunday Night Football would ramp up the MVP talk even more.
author: Dale Altman

title: Bengals now have best 8-game start under Zac Taylor
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals put together another convincing win over the Atlanta Falcons this morning in Madrid. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins put on an absolute show in front of a massive international audience, leading the Bengals to 6-2 on the season. With the win over Atlanta, the Bengals have officially put together the […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals put together another convincing win over the Atlanta Falcons this morning in Madrid. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins put on an absolute show in front of a massive international audience, leading the Bengals to 6-2 on the season. With the win over Atlanta, the Bengals have officially put together the best start through eight games in the Zac Taylor era at 6-2. Cincinnati has started 5-3 through their first eight games twice under Taylor (2021, 2023), but 2026 now takes the cake as the best start under their current head coach. The Bengals truly are just two plays away from being 8-0 on the season, but it is hard to complain about where the team is right now. With Burrow playing at an MVP level and the defense doing enough to support the best offense in the NFL, it could be an exciting year for Bengals fans. Taylor and the Bengals will now return home for a massive, and I mean massive, AFC North showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers next weekend on Sunday Night Football.

title: Bengals News: Embarrassing Trade Deadline for Cincinnati
summary: The 4 PM NFL trade deadline came and went on Tuesday, and the Cincinnati Bengals didn’t make a single addition to their team. Not for lack of trying, though. They tried to send a sixth-round pick to the Eagles in exchange for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie, a move most would have celebrated. At least at […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals director of player personnel Duke Tobin takes questions from the press during the annual season kickoff media day event at Paycor Stadium in downtown Cincinnati on Monday, July 27, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The 4 PM NFL trade deadline came and went on Tuesday, and the Cincinnati Bengals didn’t make a single addition to their team. Not for lack of trying, though. They tried to send a sixth-round pick to the Eagles in exchange for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie, a move most would have celebrated. At least at first. They backed out, though, after they learned—likely on X from OverTheCap.com’s Nick Korte and not even someone from inside their own building—they’d lose the third-round compensatory pick they earned in the ‘27 draft if the trade went through. So yeah. We learned the Bengals likely don’t even have anyone on the staff that could foresee how trading for a guy who was signed as a compensatory free agent could affect their future. We also learned the defense that has shown flashes of really good and flashes of really bad is the one Joe Burrow and the offense is going to be tethered to for the entire season. What a day. Here’s what else is going on: Bengals Face Harsh Reality After NFL Trade Deadline People are going to put a lot of blame on the Bengals and their front office for not making a swing. In some ways, it will be unfair. In other ways, they have built up a reputation of not going all-in when they have to. How Bengals’ top opponents in the AFC handled Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline There wasn’t a more aggressive team in the AFC than the Jacksonville Jaguars, however, who added three veterans before the deadline. Former Bengals safety Jessie Bates III came over from Atlanta, defensive tackle Jordan Davis was dealt from the Eagles to the Jaguars and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux arrived in a trade with the New Orleans Saints. Hidden strength of Bengals’ roster just took a hit and there was nothing they could’ve done to stop it The Bengals were lucky to bring Johnson back on their practice squad. Having both him and Flacco behind Burrow was such a luxury, and made the QB room arguably the best in the league. Even if Johnson wasn’t on the active roster, his presence in the building and experience of nearly 20 years playing professional ball were valuable on their own. title: Cleveland Browns news: Silencing the QB noise
summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken is still new to town, so he can be excused for not understanding how things work around here when it comes to quarterbacks. Every decision relating to the position must be questioned and defended on a daily basis. It does not matter how many names are on the infamous […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken is still new to town, so he can be excused for not understanding how things work around here when it comes to quarterbacks. Every decision relating to the position must be questioned and defended on a daily basis. It does not matter how many names are on the infamous quarterback jersey; the mob always wants another one added to it. Because where is the fun of simply knowing who the starter is and practicing for that week’s opponent? Monken appears to be catching on, however, as he showed during Wednesday’s announcement that quarterback Deshaun Watson would be back as the starter for this week’s game against the Houston Texans after missing one game with a concussion. It is the type of standard move that NFL teams make all the time. A starter misses a game (or games) with an injury, and once healthy, they return to their former status. Maybe the fact that Monken is trying his best to run the Browns like a real NFL team is throwing people off. After all, despite not playing well for a full game yet this season, Watson has been instrumental in helping the Browns stay relevant into November, which is a rare feat around these parts. Why would Monken want to go away from that, especially after watching the same script play out against New Orleans only to end with a crucial loss instead of a key win? The answer, as it has been since the start of the season, is that he never wanted to, and it was only Watson suffering a concussion that brought a conversation no one wanted to have back into the light. Now that Monken has answered the question, the team can focus on getting ready for the Houston Texans and attempt to avoid going into the bye week on a three-game losing streak. title: 2027 Browns mock draft: Help on defense and finally a QB
summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken finally delivered the answer on Wednesday to the question that has kept the NFL on edge since Sunday evening. Deshaun Watson is indeed returning as the team’s starting quarterback for this Sunday’s game against the Houston Texans. It was the only logical decision for Monken to make given that […]
full_text: (Photo by Eston Parker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken finally delivered the answer on Wednesday to the question that has kept the NFL on edge since Sunday evening. Deshaun Watson is indeed returning as the team’s starting quarterback for this Sunday’s game against the Houston Texans. It was the only logical decision for Monken to make given that Watson helped the Browns to a 5-3 record before missing last week’s overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints with a concussion. Because this is Monken’s first year in Cleveland, a town where manufactured quarterback debates go to thrive, he seemed genuinely puzzled on Wednesday about why he would need to make a formal announcement about the starting quarterback : “I don’t even know why I have to say it publicly, because it’s really only our business in terms of who’s going to play and who’s not going to play. But I mean, he played well enough to earn to still be our starter.” Even though the Browns now have their starting quarterback established for the rest of this season, there are still going to be questions about what they will do in 2027. Watson’s contract is up at the end of this season, and no matter what happens the rest of the way, the Browns really need to move on from the most controversial quarterback that has ever been on the roster. That leaves Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, both destined for careers as backup quarterbacks, and rookie Taylen Green, whose future role in the NFL has yet to be determined. So the Browns will need a new starting quarterback – or at least a rookie that projects to actually be a starting quarterback – which should lead general manager Andrew Berry to select one in the 2027 NFL Draft. Berry will be holding a pair of first-round selections come draft, both Cleveland’s and the one received from the Los Angeles Rams as part of the Myles Garrett trade, but neither appears as if they will be at the top of the draft. Which means that Berry will have to either work a trade or wait and see who might fall to him on draft night. Clemson EDGE Will Heldt this season: 6 sacks 27 pressures 15 defensive stops pic.twitter.com/2jvIO1qABM — Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) October 29, 2026 That is the path that The Athletic ’s Nick Baumgardner sees Berry taking in this Round 1 mock draft, with Baumgardner projecting that the Browns will be selecting at No. 15 and No. 19 overall. With quarterbacks Drew Mestemaker (Miami at No. 3) and CJ Carr (New York Jets at No. 6) off the board, but with (gasp!) Arch Manning still in the green room, the Browns select Clemson defensive end Will Heldt with their first pick : Big enough, at 6-6, 260, to be an edge setter, Heldt is also crafty enough with his hands to rack up pass-rush wins. His build somewhat resembles that of Aidan Hutchinson. Heldt is in his second season with the Tigers after playing two years at Purdue. In 46 career games so far, he has 146 tackles, 19.5 sacks, and 37.5 tackles for loss. Four picks later at No. 19, Berry finally ends the suspense, and the Browns select quarterback Darian Mensah from Miami : The College Football Playoff — assuming Miami gets in, as it should — figures to be a huge stretch for Mensah. The Hurricanes’ star has the potential to be a top-10 pick, but he still needs to show more consistency, both downfield and as a processor when facing high-level teams. His arrow is firmly pointed up, though. Mensah is in his first season with the Hurricanes after playing one season at Tulane (2024) and one at Duke (2025). In helping Miami to an 8-1 record, Mensah is completing 76.8 percent of his passes for 2,694 yards, 28 touchdowns, and just two interceptions. Two first-round picks and the Browns add an impact player on defense and take their latest and greatest shot at fixing the quarterback situation. What do you think? full_text: The Cleveland Browns roster did not see any major changes at the NFL trade deadlin e, and surprisingly few changes since the initial 53-man roster came out, but GM Andrew Berry kept making moves following the deadline. As previously reported, the Browns brought back TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden to the team’s practice squad. Mitchell-Paden has only played in eight career games, six with the Baltimore Ravens and two with the New Orleans Saints in 2025, after entering the league as an undrafted free agent with Cleveland in 2022. The 6’5”, 257-pound tight end played at Notre Dame, Ohio, and Florida Atlantic in college and has caught two passes for 17 yards so far in his career. The Browns also brought back punter Wes Pahl to the practice squad, again, despite Corey Bojorquez seemingly having a great year . To make room for Mitchell-Paden and Pahl, Cleveland released TE John FitzPatrick and DT Eric Johnson II from their practice squad.

title: Browns roster has several players listed on the midseason All-Rookie Team
summary: The Cleveland Browns are in the middle of a roller coaster season. Currently, the franchise is in a two-game losing skid. So far, they have only beaten one good team, lost to two bad clubs, and only have two games against a good team left on their schedule. Those would be both games against division […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are in the middle of a roller coaster season. Currently, the franchise is in a two-game losing skid. So far, they have only beaten one good team, lost to two bad clubs, and only have two games against a good team left on their schedule. Those would be both games against division foe Cincinnati Bengals. RELATED: ROSTER RESET AFTER TRADE DEADLINE The team has had its good points and bad. Of the five wins, all of them have been the comeback variety. At no time has this franchise ever put anybody away and coasted to a victory. In the first battle against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Browns had a 21-7 lead with 1:22 left in the second quarter, and were leading 21-10 with 14:19 left in the game, but then failed to keep the Steelers from scoring two late touchdowns to come within two points of tying the game. The roster was viewed as talented on paper going into the season. There was a new head coach and OC. The offense had brought in new talent; the offensive line was five new guys; the quarterback wasn’t new, with Deshaun Watson, just new to this offense, and the defense was suggested to be a Jim Schwartz clone. But the roster was also very young. Before the season began and any players who were cut or placed on some sort of injury list, Cleveland was the second-youngest team in the league at 25.57 years. The 2026 draft class highlighted this aspect. Of the 10 players drafted, four have become starters: OT Spencer Fano, WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, and RG Austin Barber. TE Joe Royer was placed on the non-football injury list; C Parker Brailsford is a backup offensive lineman; S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren plays quite a bit, with 126 special teams snaps on punt and kickoff coverage plus another 246 defensive snaps, or 41% of defensive reps; QB Taylen Green has mainly been listed as inactive/emergency quarterback for most games; LB Justin Jefferson is a backup who has played 35 snaps (60%) on special teams; and TE Carsen Ryan has been a roster member for eight games, waived two times, and placed on the practice squad twice. Now that half of the schedule has come and gone, The Athletic is offering its annual “NFL Midseason All-Rookie Team,” put together by staff writer Dane Brugler. One thing that is interesting about Brugler’s list is that draft round or position has nothing to do with his rankings. He hasn’t forced any player to be pushed to the top just because they were a first-or second-round draft pick, nor does he care about conference affiliation or whether they played at big schools or came out of lesser-known programs. So, it becomes a fair assessment. The Browns are well-recognized on Brugler’s list. Wide receiver: First Team – Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion It is no secret that Cleveland’s young duo are having a good year through the first nine games. Both players have come up with clutch receptions and have found ways to get open. Both QB Deshaun Watson and QB Shedeur Sanders have become familiar with this pair’s route running and have gone to each repeatedly. Brugler stated: “No surprises here. They’re led by Boston, the seventh receiver drafted in April. He leads all rookies in receiving yards (507), first-down receptions (21) and receiving touchdowns (three). Against the Saints on Sunday, Boston recorded his third catch of 50-plus yards, which ties him with Green Bay’s Christian Watson for the NFL lead. Not far behind is Concepcion, who scored his first NFL touchdown on Sunday in New Orleans. He ranks No. 1 among rookies in receptions (37) and second in receiving yards (437). Concepcion also leads all rookie receivers in catches of 20-plus yards (eight) and yards after the catch (237), which ranks Top-20 in the NFL, one spot behind Amon-Ra St. Brown.” KC FIRST TOUCHDOWN ON A 64 YARD PLAY #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/p4CPhjtQPA — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 These two have been a complete triumph for Browns GM Andrew Berry when he had other receivers to consider. But how often are two rookie receivers on the same roster honored as being the best first-year players? Offensive Tackle: Second Team – Spencer Fano The Browns feel that Fano offers them everything they are looking for as a left tackle. He has had his ups and downs, and is a slightly better run blocker than in pass protection. Fano has collected six penalties, along with two others that weren’t accepted, but he has allowed just three sacks. Brugler’s assessment: “Fano’s tape has been full of high highs and low lows. He has struggled against better talent (see Chase Young this past Sunday), but he played above average against the Jets, Titans, and Ravens before that. Fano has performed well enough to believe he can be a long-term solution for the Browns.” Interior offensive line: First Team – OG Austin Barber Barber played left tackle throughout high school and mostly at Florida, with just two starts at right tackle. In training camp, he was moved to offensive guard, and when Teven Jenkins injured his back, he remained at right guard. Brugler has noticed the young buck who was taken by Cleveland in the third round, who has played well in games, and then has struggled as most rookies experience: “Barber is coming off arguably his worst game as a pro, but there has been far more good than bad on his rookie tape. He has been an iron man while battling through injuries and is tied with his teammate, Fano, for the rookie lead in snaps played (588).” Safety: Honorable Mention – Emmanuel McNeil-Warren McNeil-Warren was Cleveland’s surprise in the draft in that he had a late first-round grade, yet was taken by the Browns with the #58 pick in Round 2. And he came in as a position of need. He has played in all nine games, with three starts and 42 total tackles on the regular defense and also on the punt and kickoff coverage teams. The Browns will play some three-safety sets, which is perfect for the young defender. Are you surprised by how many Browns rookies are recognized among the best from the 2026 NFL draft? title: Cowboys report card: Grading the first half of the season
summary: If the first nine weeks of the regular season were like an amusement park ride for the Dallas Cowboys, they’d be bumper cars. You remember them being great as a kid, so you’re excited to hop in the car and take it for another spin. It’s different. Now that you’re older, the mystique is gone. […]
full_text: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images | Getty Images If the first nine weeks of the regular season were like an amusement park ride for the Dallas Cowboys, they’d be bumper cars. You remember them being great as a kid, so you’re excited to hop in the car and take it for another spin. It’s different. Now that you’re older, the mystique is gone. The gas pedal doesn’t work anymore; sometimes you don’t fit in the car, and you walk out with more back pain than you’ve felt in your lifetime. The defense is the cool bumper car in the corner no one can seem to fix, and the offense is the bumper car that can only turn right. After Brian Schottenheimer’s first year as head coach finished with a 7-9-1 record, it feels as if the team has somehow taken a step back. In the first four weeks of the season, it looked like the offense would carry the defense to the finish line. After three horrible losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Green Bay Packers, and Arizona Cardinals, the Cowboys’ offense struggled to find its identity. There have been some bright spots over nine weeks and a win over the Indianapolis Colts helps, but the report card for the first half of the season isn’t filled with A-grades, despite the roster’s star power. A grades: Quinnen Williams (A): When Quinnen Williams signed his contract extension with the Cowboys this offseason, it set the clock on whether or not the Micah Parsons trade officially pays off. It took Williams some time to find his footing in a system he hasn’t played in since college, but over the last five weeks he looks like an All-Pro at defensive tackle. Quinnen Williams in 2026 Weeks 1-4: • 13 tackles, 1 sack, 4 TFLs, 3 QB hits Weeks 5-9: • 23 tackles, 4 sacks, 10 TFLs, 6 QB hits Big Q has turned a big corner. #DallasCowboys pic.twitter.com/kBdkJEvMNA — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) November 9, 2026 Among all defensive tackles, Williams is tied for fifth in sacks (5), third in total pressures (31), and is first in tackles for loss (14). His leadership in the locker room has been praised as a big reason why the defense is starting to turn a corner. Just like his counterpart on offense, Dak Prescott, Williams will have to help carry his unit the rest of the way if they want to make a postseason push, starting Sunday vs. the 49ers. CeeDee Lamb (A): After starting out of the gate extremely hot, CeeDee Lamb cooled off vs. the Packers, Cardinals, and Bucs. He had a dominant performance against the Philadelphia Eagles, but against those three teams, Lamb caught 18 passes for 137 yards and zero touchdowns. Then he bounced back vs. the Colts, with 10 receptions for 195 yards and a touchdown in the absence of George Pickens. The offense needs to be more consistent with getting Lamb the ball because when he is cooking defensive backs, this team looks better overall. In four out of the five games where Lamb has scored a touchdown, Dallas has won. It’s not always that simple, but in this case, it might be. His ability to bring up the entire team keeps him at an A grade for the year. Tyler Guyton (A-): No one has surprised more this season than Tyler Guyton and his development. The Cowboys have put all their faith in Guyton and never gave up on him, and it’s paid off. Guyton might not be a Pro Bowl player yet, but he’s looked better than he has in the last two years at left tackle and, more importantly, has stayed healthy. Coming into the year, he was the team’s biggest question mark. Now he’s turned into one of the team’s most consistent players up front. Joey Porter Jr. (A-): Like Lamb, Joey Porter Jr. has been able to raise all boats when he’s been healthy and on the field. I think it's safe to say that Joey Porter Jr. has quickly become one of the most valuable players for the #Cowboys . https://t.co/JHIts03BvE pic.twitter.com/783t3Tb0a2 — John Owning (@JohnOwning) November 3, 2026 The biggest disappointment of Porter’s tenure so far in Dallas is that he hasn’t been fully healthy and has been bouncing between the field and the sideline. That’s why this grade is more on a curve of what he can be. He rolled his ankle in practice a few weeks ago, and he doesn’t seem 100 percent healthy, considering he only played 36 snaps on defense vs. the Cardinals and missed the Colts game. Christian Parker has shown he likes to rotate his cornerbacks, but JPJ needs to be on the field for almost every snap when healthy because of his impact. The Cowboys don’t have their bye week until Week 14, so they may have to manage him until then, but he’s been an All-Pro-level corner when he locks down wide receivers for Dallas. B grades: Dak Prescott (B+): There have certainly been A+ moments for the Cowboys quarterback, but overall, Dak Prescott has been very good this season—not elite. His inability to find answers against the blitz, which he’s normally great at, hurts him here. Prescott was phenomenal in the second half of the Houston Texans game and in the Philadelphia Eagles matchup, but given what those teams have turned into, it wasn’t high-level competition. Prescott is currently third among quarterbacks in passing yards (2,381), tied for seventh in touchdown passes (16), and is third in quarterback rating (77.0). The second half of the season will define his 2026 campaign more as he tries to dig Dallas out of the playoff hole they’re in right now. He’ll have to do it against big-time competition in the San Francisco 49ers, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Seattle Seahawks. Otito Ogbonnia (B): Just when the pro personnel department looks like its decision-making needs to be questioned, they find a diamond in the rough like Otito Ogbonnia. The Cowboys defensive tackle has been a force in stopping the run. Ogbonnia leads all defensive linemen with 18 run stops, per Pro Football Focus. Prior to joining Dallas, Ogbonnia never had more than 12 stops in a season. He’s only here on a one-year deal, but the Cowboys need to find a way to re-sign him to a long-term contract because he’s shown he’s worthy of it, and he complements what Dallas wants to do up front with their defensive tackle rotation. Javonte Williams (B): The Cowboys bell cow picked up right where he left off a season ago. After having a career year in Dallas, Javonte Williams looks poised to repeat the same success that earned him a contract extension this offseason. Williams sits ninth in rushing yards for the year (629), averaging 4.1 yards per carry, and is tied for second in rushing touchdowns (9). While the Cowboys were trying to find their identity in the run game, there were a few times Williams didn’t seem to see the holes well or couldn’t bounce the ball outside. He’s never going to be Bijan Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs, but he can be the best back Dallas needs when they are trying to establish the run. Look no further than his career performance vs. the Eagles when he rushed for 155 yards off 25 carries. Caleb Downs faced his older brother Josh for the first time in the NFL and delivered his best performance yet. 3 TKL, 1 SACK, 1 INT, 2 PD, 1 TFL vs Colts. The rookie was making plays everywhere and is looking like a future star for Dallas. pic.twitter.com/DhpDtwsSdl — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 8, 2026 C grades: Cowboys Top 3 rookies (C+): Caleb Downs’ and Jaishawn Barham’s performance vs. the Baltimore Ravens is doing the heavy lifting for the overall grade of Dallas’ top three draft picks. Downs has had to rotate from nickel corner to safety a few times this season while the defense dealt with injuries in the secondary. That’s a lot for a rookie—even one with his football intelligence—to process. That’s why at times Downs has looked like a fish out of water. However, his game vs. the Colts is exactly what the Cowboys hoped for when drafting him and what they’re hoping to see the rest of the season. As for Barham and first-round pick Malachi Lawrence, there have been moments, but largely inconsistent. With DeMarvion Overshown coming back healthy, Barham is back on the…

title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: Here come the 49ers
summary: Although it seemed at times that they would find a way to lose the game, the Dallas Cowboys managed to prevail over the Indianapolis Colts. It didn’t exactly save a season that still is teetering on the edge of the precipice, and any good feelings from this win are likely to dissipate when Dallas host […]
full_text: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images | Getty Images Although it seemed at times that they would find a way to lose the game, the Dallas Cowboys managed to prevail over the Indianapolis Colts. It didn’t exactly save a season that still is teetering on the edge of the precipice, and any good feelings from this win are likely to dissipate when Dallas host the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Our Tom Ryle and Sean Martin take a look at what faces the Cowboys. Tom – I have to compare the narrow 27-23 win over the Colts to cotton candy. We wanted it, but it turned out to be messy and rather unsatisfying. And it didn’t exactly presage a strong showing against the Niners, who are one of the best teams in the league. While Dallas has managed to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory more than once this season, San Francisco keeps finding ways to win with an injury list that runs on and on. They have a clearly winning culture, while the Cowboys have something. And there is absolutely no comparison between the head coaches. Sean – Speaking on the league at large for a second, we’ve been past the point where teams mostly are what they are for just a little bit prior to this Cowboys-Colts game even kicking off. The Cowboys have blown so many games though that they are now on a desperate march to prove they aren’t defined by those losses, one that will require stringing together wins, which is something us fans all need to see anyway considering Brian Schottenheimer hasn’t proven he can do that at any point from last year on. Like you sort of said, the 49ers game either way will add the Cowboys to the list of teams around the NFL that we know what they are here in mid-November. It’s either another setback where all the things the Cowboys didn’t do well to let the Colts be close to them get them exposed, confirming many other suspicions about what Dallas is anyway, or a possible season-defining win. A win for Schottenheimer against Kyle Shanahan, which will require Schotty’s offense to look more Shanny-like, would send a message that this team does have the fight in it to contend for the NFC East until the end. Beating the 49ers also feels like it will take having Christian Parker’s fingerprints all over it, after his defense mostly found a way to do so against the Colts. Momentum for players and coaches is there for the taking if they can somehow keep the winning vibes around longer than one week at a time. I’m not over-the-moon excited about beating the Colts by four, but I’ll also never be as upset after a win as I can be after a loss. Making this win mean something, anything at all, is up to the Cowboys to step up against the 49ers. Not as excited for that, but also ready for the peace of mind of knowing what this team really is one way or another by the end of it. Tom – Is it weird to say that a win over the 49ers would make the rest of the season more mentally taxing to deal with? If Dallas loses, especially by double digits, I think there will just be a sense of resignation and no expectations that the Cowboys can claw their way back into the playoffs. But any victory on Sunday, no matter how close, would keep those postseason hopes alive and well. Of course delivering what would certainly be seen as a shocking win would make us feel better about the team, as well as being the signature win of Schotty’s career to date. On the other hand, it would hardly prove that all the myriad warts of the team are suddenly cleared up. Based on what we have suffered through this year we will be just waiting for the other shoe to drop and Dallas to fall apart. I remember thinking that Indianapolis at least tying the game up was feeling inevitable until Caleb Downs came to the rescue. It will take a whole string of strong performances to get us over that particular hangup. The worst thing is how this all seems largely irrelevant. Not only have the Cowboys done nothing to really make us think they can win, they have also shown no carryover from a previous win. And if they do lose, we can just relax and start digging into potential draft picks and replacements for the coaching staff. Sean – Man, I’m going to have to show you the highlight of Montana State winning with a trick play in triple overtime from this past Saturday to get you back to being fired up about football again, Tom. I do wholeheartedly agree there is a weird calming sense about this 49ers game feeling like a definitive point to find out for good who these 2026 Cowboys are. So, continuing down the improbable path of how we might feel if they actually win, you’re right that it likely means nothing to confirm they’ll be ready to actually win in the postseason should they continue on (with two more tough NFC West opponents on the road still to go) to make it. Coming out of the Colts win though, there is a real line in the sand between the way Dak Prescott talked as the season vet wanting the message to be more about improving and not being happy with all the penalties and mistakes, and Schottenheimer flying high after a win like usual. We can add CeeDee Lamb and even Schotty’s boss Jerry Jones to the first side of this fence too, so whatever dynamic this has when the going inevitably gets tough against the big, bad 49ers will be super telling on Sunday. The one position we should be the absolute most worried about this organization finding the next guy at is quarterback, so more Dak-ball that leads to a win over the 49ers would be a sight for sore eyes to know at least #4 still gives you a chance – even against the best of the best. It hasn’t always played out that way, but this is a new opportunity, the defense can be trusted a little more and more each game, and I’m excited to see one way or another what Dallas does with it at home. Tom – I’m glad you are feeling some optimism, but I just can’t share it. They are facing one of the best teams in the league this weekend, and so far they have just been a wildly dysfunctional mess. While it would be great for the Cowboys to play them close, at least looking like they belong on the field with San Francisco, I fear this game will lay bare just how bad this year’s team is. Yet even a thorough drubbing will not make them dead in the water in their division. Bounce back the next week, and we will still be going over scenarios that could get them into the playoffs as the representative from the NFC East. As long as Dak remains healthy, they still have that slim hope to cling to. I just wish it did not feel so desultory already. Sean – I will admit, I think a fair amount of my still-mild optimism for this game comes from how much I just want any way off the rollercoaster of win, lose, win, lose. It is mentally draining enough to the point where I understand fans that have already checked out a little bit through this pattern that Schottenheimer has ingrained into not only the fan’s heads, but worse yet, the team’s attitude itself. Any path to beating the 49ers starts with coming out in the first few minutes and showing they’ve squashed this mentally, which is what excites me most about trying to steal this game. Sure, a loss may not mathematically eliminate them, but it would likely be yet another example of Schottenheimer and his staff being outcoached thoroughly by Kyle Shanahan’s side in a losing effort. In doing so, the Giants who made the best head coaching hire of the entire offseason would have even more of a stranglehold on the NFC East. These facts make it very hard to not think coaching is the Cowboys’ biggest problem, and one that would make gamedays feel hollow all through December. Is there anything less fun than not being excited to watch talented players because of the coaches holding them back? I think not. Here’s hoping for legitimate new life on the season after Sunday. Enjoy all the football this weekend Tom, always great to chat!
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Penalties, defense, and the 49ers
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  The Cowboys committed an embarrassing 14 penalties for 153 yards. At what point does this become a direct reflection of Brian […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. The Cowboys committed an embarrassing 14 penalties for 153 yards. At what point does this become a direct reflection of Brian Schottenheimer’s coaching, and what needs to change? Mike – We’re well past the point where this becomes a reflection of Brian Schottenheimer’s coaching, it already is. Fourteen penalties is absolutely embarrassing, especially in a game Dallas dominated statistically but nearly threw away. The Cowboys are repeatedly giving opponents free yards and killing their own momentum through completely avoidable mistakes. Schottenheimer needs to stop talking about accountability and start enforcing it. You cannot expect to compete with the NFL’s best teams when you’re handing away 153 yards through sheer carelessness. Jorge – It already is a direct reflection of his coaching, or lack thereof. Bone-headed penalties are nothing new in Dallas; however, that many penalties with that much yardage is absurd and completely disqualifying for a coach. The funny part is Schotty blew so much smoke in the preseason that he really had people fooled that the culture was changing in Dallas. Remember when he had players running sprints after the Rams scrimmage? This team is as undisciplined as they come, and the perfect example is their now-seemingly weekly unraveling against lesser opponents. Ultimately, execution falls on the players on the field, but the plans, the culture, the techniques and the approaches are set by the coaches, and it seems, every week, that there is a fundamental failure to apply measures that would help this team play complementary football. Tom – I’ll second that, Jorge. Penalties reflect a lack of discipline, with the most glaring example against the Colts being the celebration penalty. But most flags go back to the same thing, even some of the questionable calls. The refs were clearly watching for offensive pass interference, yet the Cowboys repeated that mistake. Clearly there are no meaningful consequences for getting flagged, and without some kind of hammer, it isn’t likely to change. Sean – We can’t forget that the closest relevant experience Schottenheimer had prior to actually becoming head coach was basically sitting in on meetings with former head coach Mike McCarthy. He was an OC that didn’t call plays. McCarthy’s teams never had accountability for being heavily penalized, so I guess in this way we shouldn’t be surprised that Schotty’s are the same way. I did think that both pass interference calls against CeeDee Lamb were pretty soft calls, but the lack of discipline hardly stopped there, and even included a player that wasn’t in uniform. Preposterous. Dyllan – The Cowboys ranked 10th in raw penalty volume before this Week 9 matchup. It’s been a concern, especially the pre-snap penalties that keep opponents’ drives alive. Now I’m normally not a “blame the ref” guy, but I’m going to somewhat chalk this week up to poor officiating. Two pass interference calls on CeeDee Lamb were nonsensical. The officials were also quick on the trigger with holding calls on Dallas while foregoing calls when Quinnen Williams was actively tackled by the guard. Just a terrible week for officiating deciding to insert themselves into the game which is typically what happens when a team has 14 calls against them. With that said, however, there were concerning moments. The DeMarvion Overshown flag should result in disciplinary action from the head coach. At a certain point, an example needs to be made and that was a clear chance to do so. If Overshown isn’t at least sat down for a series upon his return, it’ll be a missed opportunity by the head coach. Christian Parker’s defense held Jonathan Taylor to just 46 rushing yards and Indianapolis to three conversions on 13 third downs. Was this the most complete defensive performance of the season? Mike – For me, yes, this was arguably the most complete defensive performance we’ve seen from Dallas all season, and Christian Parker deserves credit for it. After watching this defense get bullied on the ground against Arizona, holding Jonathan Taylor to just 46 rushing yards was a massive improvement. Indianapolis converted just three of 13 opportunities on third down and I’ve been extremely critical on the Cowboys third down defense, so this is a huge positive. The challenge now is consistency. One strong performance is encouraging, but doing it against San Francisco this weekend would be a much bigger statement. Jorge – No, I still think the best this defense has played was against Philadelphia. That said, that was the most complete defensive performance against an opponent’s rushing attack this season. In that Philly game, a hobbled Saquon Barkley almost ran for 100 yards. Sunday was better, but the penalties are atrocious; Bland seems to be doing his best Anthony Brown impression, and the rest of the defense still cannot play cohesively. Tom – I can’t think of a defensive performance as complete when they allow a 36 yard touchdown run. And this was against a clearly struggling Colts team. It was perhaps a step forward, but the defense is still not carrying its share of the load. Sean – I also agree it might not be the most complete, but for now it’s one that makes you feel like this team can continue having a chance in every game – even against better competition. We won’t even have to wait more than one gameday to test this theory of course, with the 49ers coming to town. This defense is getting off the field enough for a better offensive play-caller and personnel with more attention to detail on this side of the ball to be playing the type of complementary ball that’s seen the Cowboys win double-digit games and many by big scores before. That is all we asked of the defense this year, and they’re getting closer, at a time when the offense may unfortunately be getting further from their “elite” status. Dyllan – This game should have been a blowout. Dallas surrendered seven points in seven drives to start the game, with the lone touchdown coming from a Dak Prescott fumble deep in Cowboys territory. The offense was a disappointment while the defense played undoubtedly their best game of the year. San Francisco forced five turnovers against Las Vegas, while Dallas committed two turnovers against Indianapolis. Can the Cowboys realistically beat a 7-1 team while continuing to make so many costly mistakes? Mike – Absolutely not. Dallas cannot keep making these mistakes and expect to beat one of the best teams in football. What makes this question so frustrating is that the Cowboys have enough offensive talent to compete with anybody, but they’re constantly making life harder for themselves through turnovers, penalties and poor decision-making. Schottenheimer needs to make ball security and discipline his biggest priorities this week, because you cannot beat elite teams while repeatedly beating yourself. Jorge – Realistically, the only shot this Cowboys team has to beat this 7-1 Niners team is that good ol’ “any given Sunday” thing. About four teams own the Cowboys. The Packers, the Cardinals, the Ravens and the Niners. Outside of the Cardinals, all those teams are the antithesis of the Cowboys model. Structured, well-run organizations with a culture of success and standards, and we bear witness to that every time Dallas lines up against them. The Cowboys will not beat San Francisco if they keep making costly mistakes. If they clean it up, they’ll have a chance. If they force the Niners into their own mistakes, they may even cover. Otherwise, be prepared for what could be a shellacking on Sunday. Tom – The 49ers are playing like the best team in the league, and that is with a very long IR list. And like penalties, there is…

full_text: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images | Getty Images This is that week. author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys Week 10 opponent: A look at the 2026 San Francisco 49ers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are coming off a 27-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts, but their next opponent presents a much more difficult challenge. The San Francisco 49ers enter Week 10 with a 7-1 record, sitting atop the NFC and are looking like one of the most complete teams in the league. San Francisco is averaging […]
full_text: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are coming off a 27-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts, but their next opponent presents a much more difficult challenge. The San Francisco 49ers enter Week 10 with a 7-1 record, sitting atop the NFC and are looking like one of the most complete teams in the league. San Francisco is averaging 29.4 points per game while allowing just 19.5. The offense has found success through the air and on the ground, while the defense has consistently made opponents work for every yard. The 49ers are coming off a 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, a game in which they forced five turnovers, including three interceptions and two fumble recoveries. For Dallas, this is a major test. The Cowboys have shown they can put up points, but they’ll need to be far more disciplined and consistent to keep pace with a San Francisco team that has very few obvious weaknesses. Brock Purdy is playing some of the best football of his career Brock Purdy launches it deep to Jordan Watkins to extend the 49ers lead 🚀 LVvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DgGxhzVHmb — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Brock Purdy has become the engine of Kyle Shanahan’s offense, and his production through eight games explains why San Francisco has been so difficult to stop. Purdy has completed 69.1% of his passes for 1,980 yards, 17 touchdowns and five interceptions. His 109.8 passer rating ranks among the league’s best, and he’s averaging 8.4 yards per attempt. He’s also contributed 201 rushing yards and two touchdowns on the ground, giving Shanahan another way to stress opposing defenses. Purdy’s performance against the Raiders was a good example of what makes him dangerous. He completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns, while adding 40 rushing yards and a score. His second touchdown pass was also the 100th of his career, making him the fastest quarterback in 49ers franchise history to reach that milestone. Crazy to think Mr. Irrelevant is atop a list that include Joe Montana and Steve Young, but here we are. The Cowboys can’t afford to focus exclusively on Purdy’s arm. His mobility has become another dimension of the offense, and his ability to extend plays can turn a seemingly successful defensive snap into a first down. Dallas will need to pressure him without losing its discipline in the backfield. If Purdy has time to work through his progressions or escape the pocket, he has enough weapons around him to make the defense pay. Kyle Shanahan has an offense that can beat you in multiple ways The 49ers’ offensive success, however, starts and ends with Shanahan, whose system continues to create opportunities for players across the roster. San Francisco has accumulated 3,014 total offensive yards through eight games, averaging 6.2 yards per play. The team has also scored 31 touchdowns, with 17 coming through the air and 12 on the ground. Probably my favorite Kyle Shanahan run design Both guards help part the sea and Brendel climbs with ease. pic.twitter.com/FiQQXX5o4V — Gridiron Gold Mine (@GridironGoldM_) November 10, 2026 The rushing attack remains a major part of the identity. The 49ers have totaled 1,082 rushing yards on 234 attempts, averaging 4.6 yards per carry. Christian McCaffrey leads the team with 457 yards and nine touchdowns, while rookie Kaelon Black has added 303 yards and another score. Purdy’s 201 rushing yards give the offense yet another threat to account for. San Francisco’s ground game was particularly effective against Las Vegas, finishing with a season-high 190 rushing yards. The 49ers also ran the ball 43 times, their most in a single game since 2022. Under Shanahan, San Francisco has won all 10 games in which it has recorded at least 40 rushing attempts. The passing game is just as versatile. George Kittle leads the team with 483 receiving yards and five touchdowns, while Mike Evans has contributed 420 yards and three scores. McCaffrey has added 270 receiving yards, and Deebo Samuel Sr. has 206 yards and three touchdowns. Jordan Watkins, meanwhile, is averaging an impressive 22.4 yards per reception on 10 catches and has filled in during Evans’ absence. Oh and the Niners just added vet Keenan Allen to top it all off, so he could face the Cowboys in consecutive weeks. There is the challenge for Dallas: there isn’t one player the defense can simply take away and expect the rest of the offense to disappear. Kittle can hurt defenses over the middle, Evans provides a downfield threat, Samuel can create yards after the catch, and McCaffrey can contribute as both a runner and receiver. Shanahan’s offense is designed to make defenses account for all of those possibilities. The Cowboys will need to tackle well, communicate in coverage and avoid allowing San Francisco to dictate the matchup. Something they haven’t done in a whole game all season. A defense that makes life difficult The Raiders are…STOPPED @49ers defense force the goal-line fumble for a touchback 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/aaI0wj2S17 — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 8, 2026 The 49ers’ defense has been just as important to their 7-1 start. San Francisco is allowing 19.5 points per game and has surrendered only 2,335 total yards through eight games. Opponents are averaging just 3.3 yards per carry, with the 49ers giving up 647 rushing yards on 194 attempts. The Niners defense has shown an ability to create game-changing plays. The 49ers forced five turnovers against the Raiders, including three interceptions and two fumbles. Fred Warner was at the center of that performance, recording a forced fumble and a recovery. He now has five forced fumbles this season, a career high. The secondary has been productive, too. Cornerback Renardo Green leads the team with four interceptions, while rookie linebacker Jaden Dugger returned his first career interception 35 yards for a touchdown against Las Vegas. Malik Mustapha added another interception to close out the win. San Francisco’s pass rush has been more of a collective effort. Keion White leads the team with 3.5 sacks, while former Cowboy Osa Odighizuwa has two and Gracen Halton also has two. The return of Nick Bosa against Las Vegas is another important development. Bosa had missed five games before returning from the team’s bye week, and his presence gives the defensive front another established playmaker. A rivalry renewed — and one-sided lately There was a time when Cowboys-49ers games helped define the NFL. The rivalry, spanned decades and produced some of the most memorable postseason battles in league history, but the recent chapter has belonged entirely to San Francisco. The 49ers have won each of the last four meetings with Dallas, dating back to the 2022 playoffs. The streak began with a 23-17 San Francisco win in the 2022 NFC Wild Card round, followed by a 19-12 victory in the Divisional round in January 2023. The 49ers then delivered a 42-10 blowout during the 2023 regular season, before beating Dallas 30-24 in October 2024. The numbers paint an even clearer picture. San Francisco has outscored Dallas 114-63 across those four games, an average margin of 12.75 points. The 49ers have also outgained the Cowboys by an average of more than 116 yards per game across that stretch. Dallas has struggled to find answers against San Francisco’s physicality and defensive pressure. The all-time series is much closer, with San Francisco holding a 21-19-1 advantage. But history won’t offer much comfort to Dallas heading into this matchup. The Cowboys haven’t beaten the 49ers since December 2020, and they’ll need to change that trend against one of the league’s best teams.
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: Cowboys rookie report: One player rises above the rest
summary: The Dallas Cowboys needed somebody to finish the job, and Caleb Downs answered. After the offense reclaimed the lead late in Indianapolis, the rookie intercepted Daniel Jones to seal a 27–23 victory. His first NFL interception capped an afternoon that also included a sack and gave the Cowboys a much-needed response to last week’s collapse. […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys needed somebody to finish the job, and Caleb Downs answered. After the offense reclaimed the lead late in Indianapolis, the rookie intercepted Daniel Jones to seal a 27–23 victory. His first NFL interception capped an afternoon that also included a sack and gave the Cowboys a much-needed response to last week’s collapse. But here is how each rookie fared this week, listed in draft order, and any undrafted players worth noting after that. Caleb Downs (64 defensive snaps | 3 tackles | 1 TFL | 1 sack | 1 INT | 2 passes defended | 1 QB hit | 1 pressure) This was the playmaking performance Dallas wanted from its first-round safety. Downs hit Daniel Jones for a blind-side sack, then ended the Colts’ final possession with an interception. His coverage was strong throughout, allowing one completion for 12 yards on four targets. There was little to criticize in his individual production as he affected the quarterback, limited completions and made the decisive play. That is a strong response after leaving the Arizona game with a concussion. Jaishawn Barham (3 defensive snaps | 0 tackles | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 0 QB hits) Even with DeMarvion Overshown unavailable, Barham barely featured on defense. Shemar James and Dee Winters handled the bulk of the linebacker work. Three snaps offer little room for a fair performance judgement, but the lack of opportunity is the story. He finished without a defensive statistic. His fall has been rapid. Drew Shelton (0 offensive snaps | 6 special team snaps) Shelton was active, but he recorded no offensive snaps. There is no blocking performance to assess and he stayed on the bench other than to come on for special team duties. LT Overton (17 defensive snaps | 0 tackles | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 0 QB hits | 1 pressure) Overton generated one hurry on 10 pass-rush snaps, but otherwise had a quiet afternoon. He did not record a tackle or sack. There was a small contribution to the rush, although Dallas will want more disruption as his opportunities continue. Camden Brown (28 offensive snaps | 0 targets | 0 receptions | 0 receiving yards | 0 TD | 3 kickoff returns, 78 yards) Brown contributed most visibly as a returner, averaging 26 yards on three kickoffs. His offensive involvement brought no targets despite George Pickens being unavailable. The return work gave him a useful role, but he has yet to turn his receiving opportunities into production.

title: Cowboys are still reaping the benefits of previous big trade deadline move
summary: The NFL trade deadline came and went without any splashes from the Dallas Cowboys. That can be upsetting for some fans as the opportunity to add reinforcements is now gone, and now the team has no choice but to roll with who they got. That’s okay. The team feels that hanging on to their limited […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images The NFL trade deadline came and went without any splashes from the Dallas Cowboys. That can be upsetting for some fans as the opportunity to add reinforcements is now gone, and now the team has no choice but to roll with who they got. That’s okay. The team feels that hanging on to their limited 2027 draft resources is the best decision, but that doesn’t mean they’re missing out on something good, because the team is still reaping the rewards of the monster trade they pulled off this time a year ago. We are talking about the acquisition of Quinnen Williams. Before his arrival, the interior of the Cowboys’ defensive line was a glaring weakness that opposing teams routinely exploited. And this was even after the addition of Kenny Clark, who came over as part of the Micah Parsons trade. The defense desperately lacked a dominant presence who could single-handedly wreck the line of scrimmage and force teams to plan against. Without such a force, the back end of the defense was left exposed to oncoming blockers, and the run defense remained a major liability. Additionally, the lack of an interior push also allowed quarterbacks to comfortably step up in the pocket and make plays, leaving the entire defense vulnerable. To acquire Williams from the New York Jets, the Cowboys gave up a 2026 second-round pick and a 2027 first-round pick. Considering the going rate of premier defensive tackles, this now feels like quite the discount. The front office wasted little time re-upping their commitment, signing him to a three-year, $105 million extension in August that now puts him under team control through 2030. The Cowboys essentially repurposed part of their Parsons value in terms of both draft capital and cap space to secure one of the league’s best interior disruptors. What makes Williams such a terrifying match for opposing linemen is his unique combination of processing speed, burst, and raw physical leverage. He is such an intelligent player, anticipating the snap, picking up on blocking schemes right away, and attacking spots before blockers are even ready. His first-step quickness is extremely impressive for a 300-pound athlete. His speed and power allow him to shoot gaps and push people around as he fast-tracks his way to the action. Defensively, things have been messy for the Cowboys as they have a lot of things going on. New coaches and new players bring about new challenges, but Williams has been a stabilizing force who repeatedly shows up in games. Early in the year, he had his moments, but they were fewer and farther between than expected. The entire unit was struggling, but he was also under scrutiny because we weren’t seeing the dominant player we’ve all come to expect. All doubts have since been erased, as Williams has been on an absolute tear over the last five games. He’s in the backfield more, and he’s finishing. In a few short weeks, he’s gone from a guy some questioned was overpaid to now having one of the best seasons of his career. It’s only been nine games, but already Williams has 14 tackles for a loss, eclipsing the 12 he had during his All-Pro season he had in 2022. On Sunday, Williams came through in a big way at a big time against the Indianapolis Colts. First, he split a double team and rammed Jonathan Taylor so hard that he lost the ball, forcing a turnover that spoiled a potential scoring opportunity. Then, when the Cowboys needed a stop in the biggest way, he darted inside and met Taylor again in the backfield, blowing up the play. This resulted in another loss and put the Colts in a tougher down-and-distance. They failed to get a first down to run down the clock, giving the Cowboys’ offense the one final chance they needed to win the game. Those were huge plays for Dallas. Looking back a year ago, Williams didn’t come cheap, but it’s clear that the front office had a plan, and he’s done everything right to help carry out that plan. While the team still needs more help, he’s proven to be a cornerstone piece for this defense, and the Cowboys are incredibly fortunate to have a player of his caliber anchoring their defense. Quinnen Williams is an absolute savage. pic.twitter.com/MAYJY8LFdC — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) November 10, 2026

full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images After a career game against the Indianapolis Colts, backup running back Tyler Goodson is expected to miss some time with a knee sprain. Instead of signing someone from their practice squad to the active roster, the Dallas Cowboys looked outside their building for some help. The trade deadline also came and went without the Cowboys making a move. Let’s check in on today’s headlines. Dallas Cowboys signing former TCU leading rusher for needed running back depth – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Kendre Miller has been circled by Cowboys fans since coming out of the draft a few years ago. Miller was cut on Saturday by the New Orleans Saints in his fourth season since being drafted by the franchise in the third round of the 2023 draft. He reunites with Cowboys running backs coach Derrick Foster who coached him in New Orleans in 2024. In his three-year TCU career, Miller rushed for 2,410 yards and 26 touchdowns while also grabbing 29 receptions for 229 yards and one touchdown. In 2022, he led the Horned Frogs with 1,399 rushing yards, and his 7.5 yards per carry as a sophomore in 2021 led the nation. His career rushing total is 14th in program history and the fourth-most for a running back that played just three seasons in Fort Worth. Transactions: Reddy Steward released from PS – Staff Writers, DallasCowboys.com To make room for Kendre Miller, Dallas released a former starter from their practice squad. On Tuesday, the Cowboys released DB Reddy Steward from the practice squad. Steward played in three games for the Cowboys this season, starting in two, after being elevated from the practice squad for Dallas’ games against the Baltimore, Houston and Tampa Bay. He tallied 11 total tackles in those three games this season. Steward initially joined the Cowboys in August of 2025, and last season played in all 17 games, starting five. Cowboys let NFL trade deadline pass quietly. What could lack of moves mean for Dallas’ roster? – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News The Cowboys stayed quiet during a crazy trade deadline. The Cowboys didn’t make any trades before Tuesday’s deadline passed. Instead of seeking external improvement, they opted to see what this year’s team could do in its remaining 10 games and where it could improve on its own. “I’m very comfortable in our team,” Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday when asked about potentially making a trade. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Cowboys’ Quinnen Williams trade looks like an underpay after Jordan Davis deal – Mike Luciano, The Landry Hat After the Philadelphia Eagles traded Jordan Davis away, do the Cowboys have the best DT duo in the division? While Davis is a very good player who was a key part of a championship defense, he comes with some issues. He doesn’t play a plurality of snaps every single game, and his 9.5 sacks in five years show somewhat limited upside as a pass rusher. Williams comes with none of those concerns. Williams’ five sacks in 2026 are right on par with his usual career averages, and he is leading the NFL in tackles for loss with 14 this year. If the Cowboys didn’t pull off this trade, they would have likely used one of those picks on an inferior tackle from a very thin 2026 class. Impact: Keenan Allen trade pits him against Cowboys, again – Staff Writers, DallasCowboys.com The San Francisco 49ers acquired a wide receiver at the trade deadline the Cowboys just faced. Last week, the Cowboys’ defense squared off against Keenan Allen as a member of the Indianapolis Colts. Seven days later, they’ll likely face him again but, this time, he’ll be in a San Francisco 49ers jersey.
