Green II on the Reserve/Injured; Designated for Return list and opened his 21-day practice period. @Shift4 | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/LpBI1haTca — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) November 11, 2026 The move officially starts a 21-day practice period, during which Green can be activated to the 53-man roster at any point. The team has not clarified expectations for when that may happen, however. An Early Injury Green’s 2026 season ended almost as soon as it began. He appeared in the opener against the Cleveland Browns, but an elbow injury on the opening kickoff sent him to the Reserve/Injured list on September 16. That left him with a single game played this year, in which he played less than a quarter of the game, with an injury no less. Yes, he finished off the quarter, playing through the injury that sent him to IR for nearly two months. A Strong Rookie Showing Green arrived in Jacksonville as an undrafted free agent after the 2025 draft and quickly became a fan favorite. He appeared in 14 regular-season games and one playoff game as a rookie. On defense, he recorded nine tackles (three solo), two sacks, two tackles for loss, and a quarterback hit. Herbert BODY SLAMMED by BJ Green. Wicked hit 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Pu2N5AmJU — Nash Henry (@NashJagsNats22) November 16, 2025 His impact on special teams was equally notable: six tackles (three solo) and a fumble recovery. What His Return Means Green’s return should help the Jaguars in two areas. Special teams is the first, since he took 42 percent of the snaps there in 2025 and was one of the unit’s regulars. The second is in the edge rotation. He played only 9.6 percent of the defensive snaps entering this season, a small role, but his 2026 training camp suggested a clear step forward in his second year. With a number of significant additions to the defense this week, Green would be returning to a deeper and more competitive front four. If the camp buzz around him is justified, the coming weeks could give fans their first real look at what he can do in an expanded role. B.J. back to work💪🏾 @ActionSportsJax #DUUUVAL https://t.co/7F6ku3LTmz pic.twitter.com/Vc7VrRP7Ox — Alivia Tassely (@AliviaASJax) November 11, 2026 The practice window gives the coaching staff time to evaluate his health and conditioning as he works his way back into football shape before deciding when, or if, to activate him from IR. Should the team forgo activating him by Day 21, Green would remain on IR for the remainder of the season. Keep an eye on the team’s transaction wire over the coming weeks. It’s been good news all around in Duval lately, huh?

title: Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards: The Chiefs’ top Defensive Rookie
summary: There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award. In this post, we’ll reveal our most improved player to this point in the season. CB Mansoor Delane VOTING: CB Mansoor Delane (8), DE R Mason Thomas (1) It took Mansoor Delane three defensive snaps to show why the Chiefs traded up to No. 6 overall to draft the former LSU star. On third-and-11 of the season’s opening drive, Delane picked off a Bo Nix pass intended for Courtland Sutton. A shoulder injury ended his NFL debut after that series, but he had already given Kansas City its first takeaway of the season in a pivotal matchup against the Denver Broncos . The interception was the highlight. In the next two games Delane played, he showed how much else he could give the defense. In road wins over the Miami Dolphins and Las Vegas Raiders , he recorded 10 tackles, seven of them solo, and a pass defended in each game. Some of an outside corner’s toughest snaps come when a runner gets to the perimeter, and the corner has to come downhill and make the tackle. Delane’s work in those situations has been an early strength of his game. Entering Week 8, his 81.6 run-defense grade from Pro Football Focus ranked ninth among cornerbacks. His coverage grades held up, too. Through Week 8, Delane’s 77.4 coverage grade led all rookie cornerbacks, while his 79.7 overall grade ranked fourth in PFF ’s rookie rankings. He defended five passes in five appearances. Second-round defensive end R Mason Thomas earned the other vote. He made an immediate impact against Denver, recording a sack in his NFL debut. Delane’s shoulder injury kept him out of the rematch with the Broncos and the win over the New York Jets, but his work in coverage and run support made him the clear choice at midseason. Cornerback was one of the biggest holes on Kansas City’s roster after the team lost All-Pro Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson in the same offseason. Delane has already helped ease that transition. Five appearances into his career, the Chiefs have seen him take away a third-down throw and do the less visible work of finishing plays when the ball comes his way on the ground. For a defense replacing two starting corners at once, that’s a promising start. Is Delane the Chiefs’ top defensive rookie so far this year? Let us know in the comments.
author: Maurice Elston

title: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid is sticking with Harrison Butker this week
summary: After another remarkable miss by Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker in Week 9, a 51-yard field goal that missed in good conditions, it felt like it was the end of the line for the Chiefs’ long-time kicker. That was not the case. Head coach Andy Reid is standing by Kansas City’s three-time Super Bowl […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images After another remarkable miss by Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker in Week 9, a 51-yard field goal that missed in good conditions, it felt like it was the end of the line for the Chiefs’ long-time kicker. That was not the case. Head coach Andy Reid is standing by Kansas City’s three-time Super Bowl champion placekicker. “As far as the kicking part goes, I’m going to stick with Butker this week,” Reid shared during the opening statement of his Wednesday press conference. “And we’ll go from there.” The miss was Butker’s seventh of the season and put his field-goal percentage at a league-low 63% among active kickers; former Los Angeles Rams kicker — who was hosted by Kansas City for a tryout before Justin Tucker was signed — is the only qualified kicker with a lower rate (56%). Still, Reid is loyal to Butker because of his history of clutch kicks in Kansas City. The 31-year-old has been doing it since the first game of his Chiefs career, a “Monday Night Football” game against Washington in 2017; Butker hit a 43-yard field goal with less than five seconds to go to clinch a victory after being signed from the Carolina Panthers ’ practice squad earlier that year. “Harrison has done such a great job for us over time here,” Reid said. “Sometimes, you go through these little peaks and valleys things. So you have to give him a chance to work through them; we’ll see how things go.” Whether Kansas City’s patience with Butker will pay off remains to be seen; it feels like the team is waiting to react to a disastrous miss instead of being proactive with one of the league’s least accurate kickers over the last two years. When asked about the length of the leash Butker has moving forward, Reid moved on from the topic. “I’m not going there,” Reid responded. Any of the other 32 NFL teams can sign Justin Tucker off Kansas City’s practice squad at any moment. In Week 10, Reid all but confirmed the Chiefs would not be one of those teams, and Kansas City will kick this problem down the road another week.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs ’ pass rush delivered a resurgent performance against the New York Jets , and the CEO of Sack Nation was recognized by the NFL for leading the way on Sunday. Sack Nation stand up 🗣️ Congrats, @StoneColdJones ! pic.twitter.com/B7JIQX0xhU — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 11, 2026 The Chiefs announced that defensive tackle Chris Jones was named AFC Defensive Player of the Week for his Week 9 performance. He earned two sacks, broke up a pass, made a run stuff on third-and-5, and registered five quarterback pressures, according to Pro Football Focus . It was the fourth time Jones has won the award, and the first time since Week 4 of the 2024 season. He registered two sacks and an additional quarterback hit in a 17-10 win over the Los Angeles Chargers in that performance. That was also the last time a Chiefs player has earned the award. Current Los Angeles Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson was the previous honoree after a pick-6 in Week 2 of his rookie year (2022), also against the Chargers. He is the third Chiefs player to win an AFC Player of the Week award from the NFL this season: running back Kenneth Walker earned the Offensive honor in Week 1, and punter Matt Araiza was named Special Teams Player of the Week after an excellent performance against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. Let’s see if Jones can build on the award-winning performance and continue to look like the dominant, All-Pro version of himself he was against New York.

title: Chiefs Mailbag: Is Josh Downs more of the same in KC’s WR room?
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! The Chiefs beat the New York Jets in virtually every aspect of the game in Sunday’s 35-12 victory. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds with a new weapon […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! The Chiefs beat the New York Jets in virtually every aspect of the game in Sunday’s 35-12 victory . Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds with a new weapon joining the team for Week 11. Swaf asks: Josh Downs. A 5’9″ 170-pound small WR. Is this what the Chiefs really need at WR? He was held without a catch on Sunday. Sounds familiar to me. I just don’t think another small WR is the answer. Downs definitely has a body type that many Chiefs fans are tired of, but he also plays the role the Chiefs envision much better than the other options they have gone through since Tyreek Hill left town in 2022. Downs isn’t a project where there is a major question about how he will fit or what he can do in the NFL. This is a player who has racked up 2494 receiving yards over three and a half seasons. When he joins the team on Wednesday, he will walk into the room as the most accomplished member of Kansas City’s wideouts. The 2023 third-rounder has proven himself apt in the catch-and-run situations that make Kansas City’s offense go. What is encouraging is that he has been better on deep routes in 2026 than in his first three seasons. His average depth of target (ADoT) in 2026 is a career high of 9.5. He will not be Tyquan Thornton, but there may be a little downfield action to further unlock with him. Throughout his career, Downs has generally played bigger than his size and has only missed three games in his career. He probably isn’t the superstar we continually ask Kansas City to add, but he should greatly raise the floor of the offense even as he works his way in over the next few weeks. PettyMahomes asks: Is there any sense that Josh Simmons will play this year? The o-line is terrible and needs a big infusion of talent. Rarely does a player put themselves into head coach Andy Reid’s doghouse as Simmons appears to have done. Once those players play themselves out of the team’s plans (such as cornerback Marcus Peters or wideout Kadarius Toney), there isn’t a great track record for making their way back into the team’s good graces. I do not have any inside information. If I had to guess, I would fathom that Simmons never playing for Kansas City again is a more likely outcome than playing in 2026. I definitely hope that I am wrong. Certainly, the ability to play a position at a level that is almost impossible to acquire outside of a top ten draft selection could see Simmons given another opportunity. If there is another chance for Simmons to get back onto the field, I would watch for the weeks leading up to the Week 14 game against the Cincinnati Bengals , when Kansas City will come off of a mini-bye after consecutive Thursday games. I don’t think anyone is counting on Simmons, and any contribution would be seen as a pleasant surprise. KCDane asks: Why aren’t offensive and defensive line part of the trade needs and discussions before deadline? The Chiefs appear set to get a front seven reinforcement back in second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, who seems on the verge of returning from last season’s ACL tear. Perhaps Norman-Lott is activated ahead of Sunday’s road contest with the Atlanta Falcons . His 21-day practice window to come off of the Physically-Unable-to-Perform (PUP) list will expire before Week 12’s game against the Arizona Cardinals . The Chiefs’ priority truly needs to be to get Norman-Lott back in the fold while working with rookies R Mason Thomas and Peter Woods to improve over the season’s second half rather than rental players. We will see if Simmons presents a similar opportunity to add a player from within the system this season. Even so, the league-wide supply of starting tackles is so thin that such players are rarely available at the trade deadline. Even if teams fall out of contention and shift the focus to evaluating in-house talent, the offensive line has to hold up to make any real conclusions about players in question. If the Chiefs had touched another position group besides wide receiver, I would have liked to have seen them add a safety or coverage linebacker with a proven history of matching up with tight ends. BuckeyeChief asks: Is there any chance the AFC West leading Denver Broncos stumble? For a hot minute, I thought the Carolina Panthers might sneak by and get a win on them, but that didn’t happen. Many are saying that the AFC West title is already lost for the Chiefs, but like Lee Corso says, “not so fast, my friend.” It’s going to be hard to catch the Broncos based on remaining schedules. Simply put, Denver’s schedule is significantly easier the rest of the way than Kansas City’s. The Broncos certainly aren’t perfect, and their dependence on second-half comebacks — as against the Chiefs and Panthers the last two weeks — will probably fail them once or twice. I won’t be surprised if the teams finish with the same record and with 5-1 division records. One result that could prove unfortunate for Kansas City if tiebreakers go to common opponents is losing to the Seattle Seahawks while the Broncos were able to come out on top of them. Kansas City would do well to win against the Los Angeles Rams as Denver did. Beating the San Francisco 49ers (who handed Denver their second loss) would also greatly help Kansas City’s case. Both the Chiefs and the Broncos have the Buffalo Bills and New England Patriots remaining on the schedule. There is still much football to be played, and sometimes teams just don’t finish the season as strong as expected. The division should not be written off for Kansas City. For it to happen, the best thing would be simply to keep winning — while holding our noses and cheering on the Las Vegas Raiders when they travel to Denver in Week 11. OzarkEd asks: Will we play a complete game from start to finish this season? The Jets possessing the ball for so long on their first two drives (resulting in field goals) probably gave Sunday’s game more of a sour note than the performance deserved. Momentarily fearing that Patrick Mahomes needed Tommy John surgery also did not help. A better start would have been great, but I’d call that a pretty complete game, overall. The Chiefs won 35-12, scoring five touchdowns without allowing one and shutting out an opponent in the second half. New York never advanced past the Chiefs’ 22-yard line after halftime. Kansas City outgained New York 391 yards to 229, even with the game ending almost evenly split in time of possession. The pass rush even came to life, delivering five sacks. Perhaps the Chiefs can get off to a faster start in one of their next two games against opponents who have probably moved into player evaluation mode. But it’s hard to control a game against any opponent like Kansas City did in Week 9. Thank you for reading this week’s Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! We will be back after the Chiefs try to keep the winning going in Atlanta. Keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to ask your questions.
author: Jared Sapp

title: Chiefs waive return specialist Nikko Remigio after midseason trade
summary: On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs executed a trade to acquire wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. To make room on the 53-man roster, the Chiefs reportedly waived rookie defensive end Jack Pyburn. Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com was the first to report it, but Pyburn was not the only player cut after the […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs executed a trade to acquire wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts . To make room on the 53-man roster, the Chiefs reportedly waived rookie defensive end Jack Pyburn. Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com was the first to report it , but Pyburn was not the only player cut after the midseason move. We have traded for WR Josh Downs. We have waived WR Nikko Remigio and DE Jack Pyburn. pic.twitter.com/bdZIgClbIW — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 11, 2026 On Wednesday morning, the team also announced that wide receiver and return specialist Nikko Remigio was waived. He has been the Chiefs’ primary returner for three seasons, but he is now on waivers and will likely return to the team’s practice squad by the end of the week if he clears. The former undrafted free agent out of Fresno State in 2023 went from training-camp darling to starter by the 2024 season. To this day, his most memorable play may be the 41-yard punt return in the first half of the AFC Championship Game against the Buffalo Bills , which set up a touchdown drive and helped clinch a third consecutive trip to the Super Bowl. Remigio’s most memorable play in a Chiefs uniform is still the big return from the 2024 AFCCG 🫡 pic.twitter.com/fhoqQ1sHD9 — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) November 11, 2026 In each of his three NFL seasons, Remigio’s punt-return average has dropped. In the 2024 regular season, he averaged 9.5 yards per punt return, but this season his average is 5.6 yards; out of 14 “qualified” punt returners, that is the lowest average in the NFL, according to Pro Football Reference . Rookie running back Emmett Johnson has emerged as a strong option for kick returns, and rookie wideout Cyrus Allen has repped the returner spot in the preseason and last week, though he fumbled his one shot. It will be worth seeing if Downs becomes an option for Kansas City on punt returns. This season, Downs has returned only two punts for 20 yards, but he has 32 career punt returns in the NFL and averages 9.8 yards per return. The release of both Remigio and Pyburn frees up a spot on the 53-man roster ahead of the Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons . Editor’s note: Second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) needs to be activated before November 17th, which is next Tuesday, so he could be the player who fills the vacancy.

title: The Chiefs’ pass rush came alive against the Jets
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the New York Jets 35-12 on Sunday, improving to a 6-2 record. While the game was close early on, timely red-zone defense and a dominant second half kept the Jets out of the end zone and held them scoreless. A big factor in the performance was the pass rush. Leading […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the New York Jets 35-12 on Sunday, improving to a 6-2 record. While the game was close early on, timely red-zone defense and a dominant second half kept the Jets out of the end zone and held them scoreless. A big factor in the performance was the pass rush. Leading up to the game, the Chiefs’ pass rush failed to make any meaningful impact in the losses to the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos . After being called out this week for the lack of production, the defensive line showed up and played their best game since the opener. Here is how they did it Chris Jones returns to form The Chiefs’ All-Pro defensive tackle has had a slow start to the season, but he exploded for his best game of the year on Sunday, recording two sacks and creating pressure throughout. Early on, Jones applied quick pressure using power rushes, setting the table for his counter moves later in the game. Jones still has the power to move opposing linemen at will when left single-blocked, and this week he made Geno Smith uncomfortable by crushing the pocket early in the game. The power moves are designed to put offensive linemen on skates and force them into overaggression off the snap, which is when he can work his counters like his hand swipe-to-rip combo. Throughout his career, this has been Jones’s go-to move. On the snap, the right guard tries to set quick on Jones and gets his hands on him first to stop the power rush. Jones lined up with a running start from his alignment in front of the tackle, took advantage of the guard’s flat set, and swatted his hands away while ripping through the B-gap. The guard’s quick set means he didn’t get much depth, which gives Jones a very quick path to the quarterback. Jones interior pass rush was good all game, but later on he had his best rush of the season from the edge. At this stage in his career, Jones does not have the same explosion and quickness that he did to beat tackles off the edge consistently as he did in years prior, but as shown with his sack of the right tackle, he can still load up and bring his full force and quickness for one play in late-game situations. It’s not a spot the Chiefs should line him up in frequently at this stage in his career, but it is a good curveball for them to throw in late-game situations. Karlaftis continues playing well Arguably the Chiefs’ best defensive player so far this season, defensive end George Karlaftis continued his strong season on Sunday, finishing good pass-rush attempts with sacks. His effort and hustle on a game-in, game-out basis are undeniable, but the main criticism of his game has been his failure to finish plays with sacks. Before the Chiefs’ Week 5 bye, Karlaftis did not record a sack, but since then he has recorded four, including two on Sunday. On the snap, Karlaftis lands inside with his hands on the right tackle and walks him into the pocket. He gets to the quarterback’s level, disengages the block, and engulfs him for a sack. Karlaftis has used the bull rush a few times this season to compress tackles into the pocket, and he is playing with more power than he has shown so far in his career. A relentless motor and good timing also helped him collect another sack. The Jets sell a play-action look off the snap, which makes Karlaftis hesitate out of the gate initially. As the quarterback pulls the ball, Karlaftis gets a bead on the play and quickly accelerates around the tackle. Sensing danger and under duress from rookie edge R Mason Thomas, the quarterback attempts to flee, but Karlaftis bends and gets just enough of his ankles to bring him down for a sack. Ashton Gillotte Getting in on the sack party was second-year defensive end Ashton Gillotte, who had his best game as a pro rushing the passer. Finishing with five pressures and one sack, Gillotte strung together a well-deserved performance getting after the quarterback. One of the Chiefs better run-stuffing defensive linemen this season, Gillotte found himself on the field when the Jets would try a trick play. The Jets sell a duo look on the snap, but the running back quickly flips the ball back to the quarterback, who surveys down the field. Lined up as a 6-technique off the snap, Gillotte is solo-blocked by a tight end, but uses a fierce start off the line of scrimmage to drive him off the line. Recognizing the trick play, he uses a long arm to help disengage, and then hustles to attack the quarterback. His sack came as the offense was preoccupied with Jones and Karlaftis. With six defenders on the line, Gillotte inside, with Karlaftis as a 4-technique, and Jones a wide 5-technique, the Jets slide protection to the right. Jones loops inside while Karlaftis attacks the right B-gap. This causes the right guard to take Karlaftis, but the center lets Gillotte go with Jones looping. The trap was set, and Gillotte quickly runs down the quarterback. The bottom line This is the kind of performance the Chiefs should expect from Jones and Karlaftis. They are the two highest-paid defensive players on the team, and as seen in Gillotte’s big game, they need to open up looks for the rest of their teammates. Smith has been one of the most sacked quarterbacks so far this season, so this isn’t a game the defensive line can rest on; they should use it as a building block for where they want to go this season.
author: Caleb James

title: Film review: What Josh Downs brings to the Chiefs’ offense
summary: Christmas came early this year for Kansas City Chiefs fans asking for a wide receiver. Before the trade deadline on Tuesday, general manager Brett Veach struck a deal with the Indianapolis Colts for receiver Josh Downs. The 25-year-old playmaker has the skill set to be one of quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ top weapons. This season, Downs […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Christmas came early this year for Kansas City Chiefs fans asking for a wide receiver. Before the trade deadline on Tuesday, general manager Brett Veach struck a deal with the Indianapolis Colts for receiver Josh Downs. The 25-year-old playmaker has the skill set to be one of quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ top weapons. This season, Downs was the Colts’ leading receiver by yards (354), more yards than any Chiefs pass catcher besides tight end Travis Kelce (482). Through three weeks, Downs was on pace for a career season (62 yards per game), but the Colts quickly went into fire-sale mode amid a lost season. This is reflected in his most recent production. The fourth-year wideout — a former third-round pick — was ready for a change of scenery, and there’s reason to believe Kansas City will be a good place to maximize his talents. Let’s take a closer look at why that’s the case: Getting open quickly In his NFL career, Downs has played nearly 80% of his pass-play snaps aligned in the slot, according to Pro Football Focus . He is constantly used to win on quick-hitting routes, showing off route-running chops against man coverage and the elusiveness to find creases in zone coverage. His ability to win against man coverage is arguably the biggest reason he will make a difference for the Chiefs’ offense the rest of the year. On this play, he runs an option route and stays patient coming off the line, reading the defense’s movement. He identifies the vacancy over the middle and makes a decisive move to create separation. These option routes have not been as common in the Chiefs’ offense, especially with a wide receiver. In his prime, Travis Kelce ran these routes very well, but it takes the right combination of physical and mental tools to make them a constant play call. In general, Downs will be a reliable option on short throws because of his feel for spacing on his routes and toughness after the catch. He has urgency to turn upfield, which helps him slip off tacklers; he runs hard and purposefully for his stature (5 feet 9 inches tall and 171 pounds at the 2023 NFL Scouting Combine). Getting open downfield This season, over 65% of Downs’ targets have come on throws nine yards or closer to the line of scrimmage. However, he seems to make the most of his chances to run longer routes downfield. Here, one of his many chains-moving catches against the Chiefs in Week 2, he makes quick work of cornerback L’Jarius Sneed with acceleration inside and a subtle move at the top of his route to completely shake Sneed despite his outside leverage. He uses the same quickness that gets him open to separate at the second level. Another case in point of Downs’ shiftiness translating downfield. When Downs releases vertically, it’s his acceleration that can earn him separation on a route like this. The two-way go out of the slot forces defenders to respect in, out and vertical releases, and Downs uses his suddenness well to create the separation regardless of which direction he goes. Here, he makes a nice finish at the catch point and in bounds. Tough catches In the last clip, Downs shows strength to finish a contested catch. For his size, he shows a willingness to go up and fight for the ball. The instincts when the ball is in the air is what can help quickly earn the trust of quarterback Patrick Mahomes when Downs isn’t wide open — because no player gets wide open often. Especially over the middle, Downs looks fearless and natural at finishing tight-window completions. The bottom line It’s clear that Downs is more of a pure receiver and route runner than the Chiefs currently have. Rashee Rice is a strong runner after the catch and understands how to settle into zone windows, but he has never shown off the route-running chops that Downs has. Xavier Worthy’s route running stands out as choppy compared to Downs’ smooth, gliding routes. It appears he will need to work off the ball, using pre-snap motion and free releases to get open quickly in crucial spots. He won’t beat press constantly, so Rice and Worthy should take the bulk of those on-ball reps and allow Downs the space to accelerate into his routes. Josh Downs' first game in a Chiefs uniform will be a bounceback opportunity. Off day against Dallas on Sunday pic.twitter.com/iViArXxwyj — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) November 10, 2026 According to PFF , Downs has four drops, tied for the sixth-most in the NFL this season. When a team punts on its season as early as Indianapolis did, there’s reason to believe Downs could improve on this mark being in a more locked-in environment with the Chiefs. There’s little reason for Downs’ debut to be delayed. He is a strong fit in the offense and should make a big impact on the field by getting open, whether by breaking off a man defender or angling correctly between zone defenders. The last piece of the puzzle will be whether Mahomes and Downs can develop chemistry quickly enough to make the most of the midseason move, giving the Chiefs answers to the issues they’ve faced targeting wide receivers this year.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Chiefs News: Josh Downs trade is worth it in the Mahomes era
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have acquired wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts, a move that feels inevitable in retrospect, given the constant reports of the Chiefs’ interest in adding a wide receiver over the last few weeks. In an ideal world, the Chiefs’ roster is strong enough to win a Super Bowl without […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have acquired wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts , a move that feels inevitable in retrospect, given the constant reports of the Chiefs’ interest in adding a wide receiver over the last few weeks. In an ideal world, the Chiefs’ roster is strong enough to win a Super Bowl without a midseason trade, but general manager Brett Veach rightfully acknowledged that quarterback Patrick Mahomes needed more help in order to make the most of this season. title: Rams won’t put Puka Nacua on IR, but return timeline is unclear
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will not put Puka Nacua on injury reserve with his knee injury according to head coach Sean McVay, but that does not mean that the receiver will miss fewer than four games. ESPN’s Sarah Barshop reports that the decision to keep Nacua on the 53-man roster is due to “semantics” and […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams will not put Puka Nacua on injury reserve with his knee injury according to head coach Sean McVay, but that does not mean that the receiver will miss fewer than four games. ESPN’s Sarah Barshop reports that the decision to keep Nacua on the 53-man roster is due to “semantics” and that Nacua missing IR is likely with regard to the Rams only having so many spots and too many players being injured. There is also the chance that the Rams are thinking Nacua can suit up in Week 14 against the San Francisco 49ers , in which case he would only miss three games. This could be wishful thinking however. Week 14 may be the earliest Nacua rejoins the Rams as they reportedly expect him to miss “extended time” . Whatever the reason(s), Nacua may have avoided a mandatory missing of four games by staying off IR, and that could be a positive development for the Rams. On the bright side, McVay indicated that Davante Adams may be able to return after the bye week, which would bring him back in Week 12 against the Packers. The Rams are not going to put Puka Nacua on IR related to roster semantics, but he is still expected to miss an extended period of time, Sean McVay said. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) November 11, 2026 On the season, Nacua has in some ways been the Rams offense with over 700 receiving yards and four touchdowns. The veteran wide receiver has also hauled in 70 catches on 94 targets. Davante Adams is the only other receiving weapon “close” to Nacua with 30 receptions, 480 yards and matches Nacua with four touchdowns of his own. Sean McVay said the expectation is that Davante Adams’ return will be sooner rather than later. McVay said the Rams are targeting after the Packers game. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) November 11, 2026 The only other receiver on the Rams with 30 or more receptions is Kyren Williams and he’s a running back. There are real questions for what L.A.’s offense will look like without Nacua, and at the time of this reporting/tweeting from Barshop, the Rams may only have to live in that realm for a few weeks, with Nacua expected to be back sooner than initially projected. Of course, if Terrance Ferguson can have an injury setback , so can Nacua. Nacua isn’t out of the woods yet in terms of how much time he’ll miss , but reports are more optimistic on Wednesday then they were Sunday/Monday after Nacua’s injury was first reported .

title: Rams will face quarterback who they didn’t draft this year
summary: Les Snead had his blinders on when it came to picking a quarterback in the 2026 NFL Draft, as the Rams’ GM was even the one who convinced Ty Simpson to enter this year so that L.A. could pick him 13th overall. That’s exactly what the Rams did and there wasn’t any apparent consideration to […]
full_text: Les Snead had his blinders on when it came to picking a quarterback in the 2026 NFL Draft, as the Rams’ GM was even the one who convinced Ty Simpson to enter this year so that L.A. could pick him 13th overall. That’s exactly what the Rams did and there wasn’t any apparent consideration to wait for day two and draft Carson Beck instead, so it’s fitting that the rookie third-round pick of the Arizona Cardinals will make his NFL debut against L.A. on Sunday. Beck is now in position to start the rest of the season with the Cardinals, giving him a head start on Simpson to show the Cardinals if they made the right decision or not. Carson Beck thrived in the preseason. Now, he's suddenly QB1. https://t.co/xIOxNbYa7i — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 9, 2026 Beck was one of Arizona’s standouts in the preseason , but that is a much different game than starting against professional, starting, superstar caliber players like Myles Garrett. This will be an even harder test for Beck because the Cardinals placed number one receiver Michael Wilson on season-ending IR this week. Instead, Beck’s top wideouts will be Simi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil, and Devin Duvernay. Ironically, nobody can say for sure which team will have the better receiver room on Sunday since the Rams have lost Puka Nacua for a period of time, possibly joining Davante Adams on IR soon. L.A. is set to start some combination of Tutu Atwell, C.J. Daniels, and Konata Mumpfield. Carson Beck is going to debut against Myles Garrett + Aaron Donald on Sunday. His starting wide receivers will be Simi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil and Devin Duvernay. — Kyle Odegard (@Kyle_Odegard) November 9, 2026 Beck will have the best pass catcher in the game period, as Trey McBride was a first team All-Pro in 2025. McBride has a league-leading 73 catches in 2026. The opportunity to throw to a tight end is not new to Beck, a former teammate of Brock Bowers at Georgia. Although Carson didn’t lead Georgia to a national championship like predecessor Stetson Bennett (twice), he had success there and then nearly won a national championship with Miami as a transfer in 2025. The Cardinals are decimated at WR. TE Trey McBride is Carson Beck's only established playmaker. Beck is no stranger to an offense built around an elite TE, Brock Bowers was the focal point at Georgia in 2023. pic.twitter.com/n20pQ7ELX3 — Bo Brack (@BoBrack) November 11, 2026 Similar to Bennett, few people in the NFL actually see Beck as a starter. He lacks the arm strength that most NFL starters have, he hasn’t proven to have a good ability to read a defense, and he has made poor decisions too often. He is also not a good athlete. Arizona’s offense shouldn’t be unpredictable or surprising, and Mike LaFleur will have his work cut out for him against his old team this time. Carson Beck is making his first start this week against the Rams. I expect the Cardinals to keep things simple, get the ball out fast, and space out the defense for zone-beaters. Here's a look back at his collegiate profile on @RecepPerception pic.twitter.com/vtDytFCwph — Alfredo Brown (@AlfredoABrown) November 10, 2026 This doesn’t make Beck a better or worse prospect than Simpson. It just makes him the 2026 rookie who started first. And he’s not alone. Coincidentally, Tuesday’s trade of Kirk Cousins has opened the door for Fernando Mendoza to start against the Seattle Seahawks. Mendoza, like Beck and Stafford, won’t have much to work with except for his starting tight end. Also in this case, Bowers. Meanwhile, the Rams have no plans to see Simpson this season. Unless there’s a situation where L.A. has nothing to play for in Week 17 or Week 18, even the backup continues to be Bennett. McVay might only play Simpson if the Rams are either locked into a playoff seed or knocked out of the playoffs altogether. Beck is being forced into action early because the Cardinals benched — then traded — Jacoby Brissett, and now Gardner Minshew is on IR. Beck got the call. Will he answer? Cardinals to Carson Beck pic.twitter.com/bCI3mkBMWG — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) November 9, 2026

title: Rams create cap space with Kyren Williams’ contract
summary: The Los Angeles Rams created $3 million of 2026 cap space on Wednesday, according to Spotrac. The Rams converted $2 million of Kyren Williams’ salary into a signing bonus and added two void years, which created $1.7 million worth of new space in 2026. They also did the same with $1.7 million of Kam Curl’s […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams created $3 million of 2026 cap space on Wednesday, according to Spotrac. The Rams converted $2 million of Kyren Williams’ salary into a signing bonus and added two void years, which created $1.7 million worth of new space in 2026. They also did the same with $1.7 million of Kam Curl’s contract, creating $1.3 million in new space. The Rams were in need of immediate space because they had gone over the cap, according to Over the Cap. The #Rams … Converted $2M of RB Kyren Williams' salary into signing bonus, adding 2 void years, creating $1.7M of cap space. Converted $1.7M of S Kamren Curl's salary into signing bonus, adding 2 void years, creating $1.3M of cap space. — Spotrac (@spotrac) November 11, 2026 The moves do not extend or alter the contracts of Williams and Curl in any way, other than to move money around on the salary cap by giving the players millions in cash upfront on Wednesday. The Rams were about $600,000 over the cap as of Wednesday morning. Signing Xavier Smith to replace Jordan Whittington may have something to do with that . This is why it is important for fans to realize that teams can’t just spend all of their cap space in free agency in order to field a roster. Not only must they pay their rookie class, undrafted free agents, and late signings, but teams have to pay their practice squad and they have to be able to afford transactions that will come during the season. Such as when players get injured. The Rams have had so many injuries and placed so many key players on IR this season that it was inevitable that the team that ranked 32nd in cap space going into the season would have to find ways to find money. Today they did that with Williams and Curl. With roughly $2.4 million in cap space now, will it be the last?

title: Rams cited as potential Brandon Aiyuk destination
summary: The Los Angeles Rams need to at least check in on wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk if the San Francisco 49ers release him, which seems like an inevitability. Aiyuk is not necessarily a transformative player after being out of football for so long, but after inactivity at the NFL trade deadline, the Rams need to find […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams need to at least check in on wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk if the San Francisco 49ers release him, which seems like an inevitability. Aiyuk is not necessarily a transformative player after being out of football for so long, but after inactivity at the NFL trade deadline, the Rams need to find some way to boost a position group that’s currently in dire straits. SI’s Grant Cohn named the Rams as a potential destination for Aiyuk : Davante Adams is on Injured Reserve with a torn hamstring, and Puka Nacua is expected to be placed on IR after he recently suffered MCL, PCL and turf-toe injuries. So the Rams are desperate. And Aiyuk would be cheap. And he probably would be their No. 1 wide receiver until Nacua and Adams return. And nothing would make Aiyuk happier than to face the 49ers at some point this season. Keep in mind, the 49ers and Rams are scheduled to meet at Levi’s Stadium on December 13. Puka Nacua is on injured reserve. Adams is as well. Now Jordan Whittington will miss time . Quarterback Matthew Stafford is running out of options at wide receiver, so it behooves Los Angeles to be aggressive with what’s left on the free agent market. Brandon Aiyuk timeline Aiyuk’s dramatic saga with the 49ers has ben well-publicized. After an All-Pro season in 2023, Aiyuk held out until signing a four-year, $120 million deal ahead of the 2024 campaign. His production dropped off and then he suffered a season-ending injury after playing just seven games. From then on, he refused to report back to the team and has been out of the sport for the better part of two years, while Kyle Shanahan has been dismissive at best about his former starter . Why wasn't Brandon Aiyuk released today? A provision in the CBA allows them to not pay him during his two-week roster exemption. So they're basically delaying the inevitable — simply because they can. https://t.co/oyNM8lw8hj — ProFootballTalk (@ProFootballTalk) November 11, 2026 This ordeal could be close to an end, however, with Aiyuk applying for reinstatement and passing a physical this week. Rams wide receiver needs It took Aiyuk a few seasons to take off in San Francisco, but his breakout campaign was stellar, posting 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. That was in 2023, which by NFL standards is an eternity, but anything close to that ceiling would be a boon for L.A.’s offense. Some more Aiyuk propaganda from @MattHarmon_BYB 🔥 pic.twitter.com/kv46WbVwmL — FFBirdGang (@FFBirdGang) July 11, 2024 At his best, he’s a strong route runner and separator with a knack for gaining yards after the catch. He’s also a willing and able blocker on the boundary, which would assist an already excellent Rams rushing attack. Clearly, he comes with sizable off-field baggage, but that feels like a secondary concern at this point. Meanwhile, with Whittington hitting IR, the Rams’ subsequent move was to sign Xavier Smith back to the active roster, which adds back a player with experience on this team but not exactly one who strikes fear in opponents’ hearts. That leaves the Rams with a wide receiver corps of Smith, Tutu Atwell, C.J. Daniels and Konata Mumpfield. That’s just not a good enough group for a Super Bowl contender, which is exactly why there were so many receiver-related rumors swirling around the Rams for weeks heading into the trade deadline. There are a handful of other veteran free agent wide receivers available right now, although none have the kind of ceiling that Aiyuk has. Maybe Darius Slayton or Curtis Samuel gets a call from Les Sneed instead in the coming days. But if you’re going to take a shot at adding some kind of additional talent to the wide receivers room, you may as well go for broke with Brandon Aiyuk. It’s not the most exciting addition Los Angeles could make, but there’s only so much it can do with the trade deadline in the past and a slate of daunting games coming up down the stretch.

title: Both the Rams and Cardinals enter Week 10 hurt
summary: The Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals face-off in Week 10 as both teams enter this contest beat-up and missing key players. The Rams won’t have their best offensive weapon in Puka Nacua, and they are still without Davante Adams as well as Terrance Ferguson. L.A.‘s offense already was a question mark and that’s even […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals face-off in Week 10 as both teams enter this contest beat-up and missing key players. The Rams won’t have their best offensive weapon in Puka Nacua, and they are still without Davante Adams as well as Terrance Ferguson. L.A.‘s offense already was a question mark and that’s even more so going into Week 10. The Cardinals just lost their lead wide receiver in Michael Wilson for the season. Arizona also won’t be starting Garder Minshew who was hurt in Week 9 against the Seattle Seahawks, so they will likely turn to rookie Carson Beck. Even with all the changes over the course of the NFL season, neither the Rams or Cardinals likely expected the rosters they have available to them entering Week 10. Keep an eye out for anymore injury news as the NFL keeps on rolling, whether the players are ready or not. Can Carson Beck convince the Cardinals not to draft a QB? He has eight games to make his case (cbssports) “Now the third-round rookie is in line to make his NFL debut against the Rams this Sunday. And Beck will have eight games to convince the Cardinals they don’t need to use what will almost certainly be a top-10 pick on another quarterback next spring. (I say “almost certainly” because while the Cards are currently 3-6 and everything appears to be going wrong, a year ago at this time, the Saints were 1-7, turned to Tyler Shough to finish 5-4 and ended up with the eighth pick instead of something higher. Shorter version: We’ll see.)“ Cardinals WR Michael Wilson out for the season due to ‘fracture in his neck area’ (sports.yahoo) “Wilson played through the injury and finished the game, but will miss the remainder of the season. The wide receiver had also been playing through two broken ribs. He brought in six of his seven targets for 60 yards against the Seahawks. Arizona was relying on Wilson to be its No. 1 wide receiver. His breakout season last year, plus a strong start this year, gave the franchise the confidence it needed to trade away Marvin Harrison Jr. earlier this season . Without Wilson and without Harrison, Arizona’s wide receiver depth is sufficiently depleted. Barring other signings, the Cardinals’ top wideout options are currently Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Harrison Wallace III, and Devin Duvernay.“ Rams reunite with Xavier Smith (nbcsports) “With all the injuries at wide receiver, the Rams decide to bring back a familiar face in Xavier Smith in lieu of trading for a receiver. Smith was on the 49ers’ practice squad after the Rams waived him earlier this season. He caught 18 passes for 303 yards for the Rams last year, seeing the bulk of his opportunities as kick returner. Smith figures to operate as receiving depth with special teams utility once again. – Aditya Fuldeore ” Los Angeles Rams Have No Easy Answer to Their Receiver Emergency (athlonsports) “ Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is expected to miss significant time after suffering MCL and PCL sprains and turf toe on the final offensive play in the 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 9. Sean McVay said the team will likely place Nacua on injured reserve, a move that would keep the offense without its leading receiver for at least four games and intensify an already difficult challenge for quarterback Matthew Stafford . Locked On Rams co-host Gavin Carlson argued the injury reflected an avoidable pattern, pointing to the number of screens and other underneath play calls that exposed Nacua to repeated contact. Carlson focused especially on McVay’s third-and-11 end-around call, which came after Nacua had briefly left the game and returned.“ Rams WR depth chart: Who’s left with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams out? (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams came into the season with one of the best wide receiver duos in the NFL in Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Unfortunately, they haven’t been on the field together very much this year. Nacua missed two games in Weeks 2 and 3, while Adams has been on IR since injuring his hamstring in Week 6. Now, Nacua is expected to join him on IR after injuring his knee in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Nacua will likely miss at least a month, with an IR stint forcing him to miss the next four games and return in Week 15 at the earliest. To make matters even worse, Jordan Whittington is a candidate for IR due to his lingering back injury .“ The NFL’s 6 biggest disappointments so far (sbnation) “Sitting at 5-4 the Rams are a middling football team. Nothing more, nothing less. What makes this so mind-boggling is how confident we all were that Sean McVay’s team would be a dominant force in football. Sure, we can point to Myles Garrett being hurt for the bulk of the first half of the season, but that doesn’t explain how we reach Week 9 and Los Angeles can only beat the hapless Commanders by one-score. Everything got off on the wrong foot with McVay having a horrific miscalculation on how to approach the season opener in Australia against the 49ers. Now it’s as if the Rams have never really shaken that rust off. Matthew Stafford has taken a significant step back after an MVP-winning 2026 season. He has thrown nine interceptions already, on pace for 17 — which would be his highest total since the 2021 season. While slated to throw for 30 touchdowns this year, which would be 16 fewer than a year ago. We didn’t expect Stafford to match his 2026 totals, but there’s been a pronounced drop-off which has damaged the Rams’ offense.“ Stephen A. Smith says Sean McVay has done something ‘inexcusable’ with the LA Rams (hitc.com) “Speaking via NFL on ESPN , he said: “I have to say to Sean McVay, what has happened to you? What’s happened to you? I think he’s an elite coach. I think he’s big time. He’s a brilliant dude, next level with football, a wonderful dude to talk to, the whole bit. Got nothing but love for him. “I don’t know what the h*** has happened to him this year. You go to Melbourne, Australia, and land 28 hours before kickoff. The 49ers were there for a week. For some reason, you’re the only human being alive, the only adult that I’ve ever known that didn’t take into consideration jet lag and the kind of impact that will have on you.” Rams earn poor trade deadline grade after taking big risk at WR (sports.yahoo) “When addressing the media on Monday, head coach Sean McVay told reporters they would be looking at “all avenues” to improve the position group. “Putting our heads together and figuring out just the semantics of, what is the 48/53 (man roster)? What does our practice squad look like?” he said. “How does that shape the different areas of our football team, defensively, offensively and in the kicking game?” Ultimately, it appears Snead and McVay have decided to go in a different direction.“ Rams Trade Deadline Winners and Losers: Les Snead Fails Matthew Stafford (si.com) “This is not the Les Snead that we are accustomed to seeing. The Snead that we’ve seen operate over the past several years would have made a move for a wide receiver, even if it wasn’t for a big name. It’s hard to fathom how the offense could lose Puka Nacua for several weeks and the front office could look at the roster and come to the conclusion that it was enough. Not doing anything felt like the Rams are punting on the 2026 season.“ Rams Power Rankings: Week 10 (therams.com) “ Each week, TheRams.com will be taking an aggregate look at where the team ranks across different outlets in the sports media landscape. Here are the power rankings for the Rams heading into Week 10: “ NFL.com, Nick Shook Rank: 17 Last Week: 18 Change: +1 ESPN.com Rank: 12 Last Week: 12” Comment of the day: Feedpost of the day:

title: Treydan Stukes provides silver lining in Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 9 blowout loss to San Francisco 49ers
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders’ defense is searching for answers after giving up 30 or more points for the sixth consecutive game in the Week 9 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. However, the Raiders might have found at least one solution with rookie safety Treydan Stukes. Stukes has been playing well and getting better just […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ defense is searching for answers after giving up 30 or more points for the sixth consecutive game in the Week 9 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . However, the Raiders might have found at least one solution with rookie safety Treydan Stukes. Stukes has been playing well and getting better just about every week, and last Sunday in San Francisco was his best performance to date. The former Arizona Wildcat nabbed his second career interception (first since the season opener) and yielded just 19 yards on five targets (four catches) while coming up with a couple of ‘ defensive stops ’ in coverage, according to Pro Football Focus . That was good enough to earn PFF’s fifth-highest coverage grade (85.8) among safeties for the week. While there’s plenty to be negative about when it comes to the Raiders’ defense, let’s focus on one of the few positives and break down the second-round pick’s outing. Treydan Stukes setting the edge against Trent Williams #Raiders pic.twitter.com/VeXMnHEK2k — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 10, 2026 As the numbers above indicate, Stukes’ impact was primarily in coverage against the 49ers. But the clip against the run above caught my eye. San Francisco comes out in 22 personnel with fullback Kyle Juszczyk as one of three strong-side tight ends initially. That’s how Kyle Shanahan likes to run 13 personnel plays/formations while keeping Juszczyk on the field. Meanwhile, the Raiders had the rookie safety cover George Kittle frequently throughout the game, so he’s on the line of scrimmage and on the strong side of the formation. When Juszczyk motions to the weak-side pre-snap, linebacker Quay Walker signals for Stukes to stay inside so that Stukes can cover Kittle with inside leverage if it’s a pass play. The problem with that is it puts a defensive back in the C-gap, where he’s in future Hall of Fame left tackle Trent Williams’ path if the 49ers run outside zone, which is exactly what Shanahan dials up. That’s a mismatch in the offense’s favor since a safety is taking on a block from one of (if not the) best offensive tackles in the game. However, the rookie doesn’t back down. Stukes eyes Kittle initially, and once he reads run, he redirects to take on Williams’ block and ends up resetting the line of scrimmage by winning at the point of attack. That helps force running back Christian McCaffrey to cut upfield and right into linebacker Tommy Eichenberg for a short gain. While Stukes doesn’t make the tackle here, he makes the play by beating a high-quality opponent in a disadvantageous matchup to force the running back to redirect into an unblocked defender. That’s pretty impressive run support from a defensive back. Nice close from Treydan Stukes -Spins down from 2-high to play curl/flat in C3 -Stays deep in his area to encourage short throw on 2nd & 20 -Rallies & tackles to put SF in 3 & 15 #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/ep0mXrqzRv — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 10, 2026 But again, the safety’s impact was felt the most in the passing game. While the interception was undoubtedly the best play he made on the afternoon (don’t worry, that play is coming later), Stukes made a handful of quality tackles that kept San Francisco behind the sticks. Here, it’s second and 20, and the Raiders line up in a two-high look pre-snap before rolling a safety down into the curl-to-flat area and running Cover 3 post-snap. Stukes is the safety spinning into the second level, and he shows some situational awareness by staying deep in his area. That does two things: it makes it more difficult to throw a pass over his head and influences the quarterback to make a short throw. Thus, Brock Purdy throws the quick out route to the slot receiver, which is what the Raiders want him to do in this situation. That’s where Stukes’ closing speed comes in, as he rallies to the football and makes a nice open-field tackle to limit the yards after the catch. Now, San Francisco faces 3rd and 15. Just don’t ask what happens on the next play…(Purdy scrambles for 18 yards). Another quality coverage stop from Treydan Stukes -Eyes Kittle initially while dropping into C2 -Sees Kittle chip release into the flat -Shifts eyes to backfield & sees crossing route -Breaks on throw to make stop on 3rd & 5 #Raiders pic.twitter.com/ckJkQSdWmy — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 10, 2026 This time, Las Vegas starts in a one-high look and rotates into Cover 2. Stukes, playing nickelback, lines up over Kittle and is responsible for the hook-to-curl area of the coverage. Initially, the safety reads the tight end and sees the tight end chip block before releasing into a flat route, taking Kittle out of Stukes’ area/assignment. So, the rookie shifts his eyes to the backfield and starts looking for a crossing route from the other side of the field. Meanwhile, the 49ers have their outside receiver in the trips formation at the bottom of the screen run a drag route into Stukes’ area. He sees that, parks himself at the sticks and pounces once Purdy lets the ball go. That’s where the closing speed comes in, again, as he makes the tackle just short of the sticks to put the offense in a fourth-and-short situation. That set up one of the Raiders’ few stops last Sunday. 49ers do get 5 on 1st & 10 here, but this is a pretty impressive close from Treydan Stukes, covering a lot of ground to bring George Kittle down on the flat route #Raiders pic.twitter.com/SICgyiWlYi — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 10, 2026 Technically, this play is still a positive result for the offense since San Francisco gets five yards on first and 10 to stay on schedule. But considering the rookie safety’s assignment, this is still an impressive rep. He lines up as a deep safety in a two-high look pre-snap but is in man coverage with the tight end, Kittle. Meanwhile, the 49ers run an RPO where Kittle is on a flat route against not just off coverage, but a safety playing over 10 yards off the ball. That makes Purdy’s decision easy, as he aborts the run play and just dumps the ball into the flat. In theory, the tight end should have enough room to pick up the first down or at least set up the offense in a second-and-short situation. However, Stukes’ closing speed allows him to make contact right at the line of scrimmage despite how deep he was playing. Now, the tackle can be better since he does allow too many yards after contact. But Kittle is one of the hardest tight ends in the NFL to bring down, so there’s no shame in that. Plus, the defense still has a decent chance to get off the field in a second-and-five situation. Elite play from Treydan Stukes to get an INT -Starts in 2-high, rolls down for Curl-Flat in C3 -Picks up slot WR while keeping eyes on QB -Reads Purdy's eyes, comes off man/assignment & climbs ladder to make the pick #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/HW1fzEUibA — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 9, 2026 Now, the moment you all have been waiting for: the aforementioned interception! What really makes this rep impressive is that the first-year pro makes a play where he shows the awareness or football IQ of a well-tenured veteran. As we’ve seen on a handful of occasions already, Stukes starts in two-high and spins down into a Cover 3 look. Granted, the play call is a little different, where Taron Johnson blitzes off the edge for a three-deep, three-under fire zone. That means the safety essentially takes over the nickel’s coverage assignment by picking up the slot receiver, who is running a return route (out and then in). Stukes’ eyes are the big key here. He’s staring in the backfield throughout the rep, using his peripheral vision to read the receiver’s route and match the receiver’s movement patterns step for step. So when Purdy rears back to throw, the rookie safety is able to read the quarterback’s eyes, come off his man and sink on the drag route from the other side of the field to climb the ladder and pick the pass off. This is what…

Mendoza said he had “no inking” the Las Vegas Raiders were discussing trading starting quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday. Mendoza said he was at his locker on Tuesday when he heard his mentor was being shipped out. […]
full_text: . (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fernando Mendoza’s latest lesson learned about life in the NFL: Things can change quickly. Mendoza said he had “no inking” the Las Vegas Raiders were discussing trading starting quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday. Mendoza said he was at his locker on Tuesday when he heard his mentor was being shipped out. Of course, that meant, Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the draft, was being promoted to the starting quarterback position. Mendoza met with media members Wednesday after his first practice as the starting quarterback. Mendoza called this a “once in a lifetime opportunity” and he is excited to play with his “brothers” starting Sunday at home against the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Mendoza made a point to heap praise on Cousins and his family for taking in as a essentially a family member. He called Cousins, a 15-season veteran, an ideal mentor and he said the veteran didn’t hold back anything while trying to help him get used to the NFL. The Raiders have lauded Mendoza for his preparations and he credited Cousins for teaching him that. Raiders’ coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza was prepared in his first practice and he noted the team is not going to “peel back” anything against Seattle. thus, Mendoza will be asked to run the full playbook in his starting debut. . @fernandomendoza thanks @KirkCousins8 for his mentorship as he takes the podium as the #Raiders starting QB @VegasNation @reviewjournal pic.twitter.com/0P9Bv3PynR — Heidi Fang (@HeidiFang) November 11, 2026

title: Should the Las Vegas Raiders fire Rob Leonard?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are leading the NFL in every defensive category you don’t want to be a part of. Total yards, Yards Per game, rushing yards, passing yards, total points and points per game. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard, in his first year, is taking some nasty lumps. While it appears that he shouldn’t be […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are leading the NFL in every defensive category you don’t want to be a part of. Total yards, Yards Per game, rushing yards, passing yards, total points and points per game. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard, in his first year, is taking some nasty lumps. While it appears that he shouldn’t be long for this job, the question begs: with the roster he currently has, who could do better and who would want to try? For the last six consecutive weeks, the Raiders’ defense has allowed 30+ points, a feat that hadn’t been replicated since the Jacksonville Jaguars did it in the 2020 season. No team in the modern era has ever allowed seven straight weeks of 30+ points allowed on defense. Additionally, allowing 150+ rushing yards to opposing teams in five of the last six weeks. While Raider Nation wants heads to roll, as they rightfully should, ask yourself: is it his fault? Keep it real Last season, the Raiders finished with the worst record in the NFL, which secured the number one overall draft selection. When Leonard took over, he was given old toilet water and asked to make wine. His best player, Maxx Crosby, was rehabbing a knee injury and the defensive backfield was completely overhauled through the 2026 draft. His best young defensive lineman, Tonka Hemingway, was still a largely unproven commodity who had done his best work in the weight room during the offseason. During that very same offseason, the Raiders finally invested in the linebacker position, bringing in Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker. Along with the former Eagles linebacker position coach. As for the defensive line, the group was largely ignored and it wasn’t until week 2 of the preseason that difference-maker Folorunso Fatukasi was brought in to help. Furthermore, there is only so much scheming you can do for an undersized defensive line against 12/13 personnel. Especially when they struggle to defend the run in regular 5/6-man sets to begin with. So how do you scheme when your guys aren’t playing up to their expectations and/or pay? Call outs Eric Stokes is supposed to be the leader of the defensive backs, but at this point, he could be cut outright from the team and they wouldn’t miss a beat. Outside of a streak or a fade, there isn’t a single pass route he excels at defending. When he takes the field, the opposing offenses look at him and salivate like they were staring at Kyu Blu Kelly last season. Somehow, mediocre play, prefaced as not giving up a passing touchdown because teams preferred to throw at a worse defensive back, got him a 3yr/$30M contract extension. He has been nothing short of a liability. Kwity Paye was brought in for 3yrs/$48M to give the Raiders a secondary pass rush to complement Crosby and had a great coming-out party against the Miami Dolphins. For $16 million per year, Paye is producing 1.5 sacks every four/five weeks. Strangely, that means within the next week or two he should be producing another sack, because his last one was in week 6 against the Buffalo Bills. Is he being asked to mush rush, or hold contain and not rush the passer? A fair question. Considering this rendition of defense is eerily similar to years past that also got Ken Norton Jr., Paul Guenther, Gus Bradley and Patrick Graham relieved of their positions. The defensive line as a whole. Flashes don’t equal consistency and players who make a couple of plays with quickness don’t tend to hold up when physicality is required. The Raiders are giving up a league-worst 2.3 yards before contact on running plays. Meaning, they are getting knocked nearly 2.5 yards off the ball on every rushing attempt; there is no scheme that can offset that. At this point, with the production being generated, these guys are practically stealing money. Case for Keeping Leonard At week 10, no defensive coordinator is going to come in with a magic scheme that’s going to save the defense. Either the players are going to get tired of producing losing efforts and do something about it, or they will not. Right now, the Raiders hold the 15th draft spot in the 2027 draft. Losing will only cause that draft selection to rise and provide access to more premier talent or trade scenarios. At the start of the year, Leonard did a masterful job of masking weaknesses and accentuating strengths. As the weeks progressed and more and more film became readily available, there was only so much he could hide. As painful to watch as it may be, the best case for the Raiders, good or bad, is to keep Leonard and readdress the issue in the offseason.
author: Philip Robinson

title: Things to consider as Fernando Mendoza era begins
summary: Las Vegas Raiders’ rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his starting debut on Sunday at home against the Seattle Seahawks as he becomes the team’s full-time starter in wake of Kirk Cousins’ trade to the Minnesota Vikings this week. Here are some things to keep an eye on: He needs help: The Raiders’ offense is […]
full_text: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders’ rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his starting debut on Sunday at home against the Seattle Seahawks as he becomes the team’s full-time starter in wake of Kirk Cousins’ trade to the Minnesota Vikings this week. Here are some things to keep an eye on: He needs help: The Raiders’ offense is averaging 26.4 points a game this season, which is the fifth most in the NFL. But Cousins was a vital part of it. The Raiders’ offensive line needs to protect Mendoza, the running game needs to improve and his receivers must make strides. Mendoza could develop a nice relationship with Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor on deep routes since he has a better arm than Cousins. But everyone must raise their game, including the Raiders’ defense which is allowing 29.7 points a game, the worst in the league. The rookie will need help. Will young receiver get a chance? Sixth-round pick, Malik Benson, was a healthy scratch the past to weeks after having just two catches on nine targets in the first seven games of the season. Benson and Mendoza built a nice chemistry in training camp and in the preseason. Perhaps the Raiders will give him another chance soon. Reserve judgement: Mendoza is being thrown into the starting lineup with games against the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns before the bye. Those are some tough defenses. This will be a process and he needs time to grow. Expect to see him be a different quarterback at the end of the season than in the next couple of weeks. Be prepared for growing pains.

title: Dolphins center Aaron Brewer in concussion protocol
summary: The injury woes keep piling up for the Miami Dolphins. This week, the Dolphins learned that starting defensive tackle Zach Sieler will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn biceps he suffered on the first play of Miami’s defeat against the Detroit Lions last Sunday. Starting quarterback Malik Willis was also […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Miami Dolphins center Aaron Brewer (55) looks on after the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The injury woes keep piling up for the Miami Dolphins. This week, the Dolphins learned that starting defensive tackle Zach Sieler will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn biceps he suffered on the first play of Miami’s defeat against the Detroit Lions last Sunday. Starting quarterback Malik Willis was also placed on injured reserve due to a lingering groin injury — meaning Miami’s signal-caller will miss at least four games, if not more. If that wasn’t enough bad news for one week, on Wednesday, it was revealed that starting center Aaron Brewer is dealing with a concussion he suffered against Detroit and is currently in the league’s 5-step concussion protocol. As such, he missed Wednesday’s practice. This isn’t the first time this season that an offensive lineman for the Dolphins finished a game with no talk of a head injury, but exhibited symptoms in the subsequent days. Rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor missed Miami’s Week 8 tilt against the New England Patriots with the same issue. All eyes will now be on Miami’s practice reports throughout the rest of the week in order to see if Brewer will be able to clear protocol in time for the Dolphins’ Week 10 contest on the road against the Indianapolis Colts.
