title: Miami Dolphins Fans: Your Post-Game Week 9 Vs Detroit Lions Takeaways
summary: Following this past Sunday’s loss to the Detroit Lions by our Miami Dolphins, I asked the following question: What are your overall takeaways from this afternoon’s eighth game of the season between our Miami Dolphins and the Detroit Lions? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon’s game, as they apply to the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins runs the ball against the Detroit Lions during the second quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following this past Sunday’s loss to the Detroit Lions by our Miami Dolphins, I asked the following question: What are your overall takeaways from this afternoon’s eighth game of the season between our Miami Dolphins and the Detroit Lions? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon’s game, as they apply to the team overall and to individual units and/or players? Below are some of your thoughts and takes on Sunday’s loss- JUK has several points that end with the fact that we just can’t seem to get out of our own way at this point. I’ll do a longer fan post but main thoughts: defense was excellent. The whole front had easily their best game of the year, with good pressure from Uche and Chop, but the really encouraging thing was the quality from all 4 interior guys. Hopefully Grant has just been ramping up post injury, a strong second half from him would be huge. Makes the LBs job so much easier. Special teams is a joke. We need a new Kicker and Punter, but I don’t see how Tabor can or should survive. Teams like ours need to win at the margins. We lose at them, every week. Willis made a horrible throw for his interception but otherwise this wasn’t on him. I appreciate him toughing it out even when clearly hobbled and even with reduced mobility he saved the offensive line about 6 sacks. Not for the first time this year we managed to chalk off his biggest play and some poor drops too, but this isn’t really a week to talk about Willis, we should be talking about… The offensive line and Bobby Slowik. 7 penalties (5 holds and 2 false starts). 3 sacks, 5 throwaways and countless plays destroyed before they even began. We couldn’t run the ball with any consistency, but man the pass pro was an absolute joke. Brewer had a poor game, Jonah is regressing to 2025 before our eyes, but Austin Jackson cannot be left 1:1 against even a passable pass rusher never mind one like Hutchison. It’s insanity. Slowik does this every time against top edge guys and it destroys our game plan every time. It’s absolutely inexplicable at this point. Overall we are playing good teams hard (and man our schedule has been brutal) but we just can’t get out of our own way. 5 offensive penalties when we got over halfway. ST penalties, missed FGs and shanked punts. But… the margins are small and we are getting better especially on defense. There isn’t an easy fix on offense other than playing some weaker defenses and committing to help the right side of the line in pass pro. Just a thought Bobby JKBMia is like many of us, waiting to see if they manage to put it together on both sides of the ball. Malik is clearly not healthy, and he’s not a good enough thrower of the football to not be able to run. The offensive line had an absurdly terrible day. I don’t understand what Slowik was watching. I saw Aidan Hutchinson beat Austin Jackson 753 times today 1on1 off the edge. Not only did he get beat, but they probably could have called him for holding on every drop back. The defense played awesome. Holding that offense to one touchdown, especially considering they started at our 40+ 3 or 4 times today was no small feat. They made a ton of big plays, got a lot of pressure on Goff and made life really tough for Gibbs which is something almost no teams can do. Special teams once again absolutely sucked aside from the fake punt call – but who is surprised?? It would be nice to see one week where actually both the offense and defense are in sync. Would be cool. Really solid game from Caleb Douglas but that’s a tough drop there at the end. The game was basically out of reach anyways, but that’s one you’ve gotta bring in. phinette sees what the rest of us can see. A defense that gets better each week and an offense that keeps sputtering. The defense continues to improve with Rodriguez really making a run for defensive rookie of the year. The offense on the other hand is really limited in what it is able to do. Too many drives in the red zone fizzled and we continued to struggle on special teams. Overall, we hung tough. Left Shark , like many of us, isn’t sold on Willis, and this team won’t get right until they find the right guy to run that offense. I am no longer the overly emotional fan I used to be, and now try to view things through a lens of reality and reason. So, this season isn’t about wins or losses for me, but indeed the “process” as the front office often bangs on about. And I’m seeing many good things from the process. I’m sold on the Green Bay guys and think the future is bright with them drafting and running this franchise. They play hard, most have the right mindset (considering the circumstances) and are showing improvement. And that leads me to Malik. It wasn’t clear to me before yesterday how limited he was running due to an injury and he has been toughing it out the past couple of weeks. But, before then, he has seemed reluctant to run hard and use his legs as a dynamic weapon. I’ve read that he doesn’t want to be considered a “running QB”, etc. And if that is true, he’s, IMO, not going to make it as a pure pocket passer. I think of “football IQ” as seeing the field, processing and decision making. And in these areas he’s just not good enough- as Tua was before him- but in different areas. He seems to be affected by the pressure and has become more and more terse with the press after games. I see this from him more than any other player. I don’t like the look in his eyes and body language. I’m not seeing the leadership that is required from a franchise QB. So, he’s feeling more like a bridge at this point approx. half way through. I understand he’s not in a great position and I don’t like the overall flow of the game called by the OC. But, hanging his head and deflecting are not the signs I want to see. Hard times forge tough men, but all don’t make it through. I’m hopeful he can prove me wrong before the season is done. Zen4Phins is at least enjoying seeing all of these young guys go out and compete. Defense is fun to watch grow week to week. Got some pressure in there today and made Goff uncomfortable. When he had time, the coverage was sticky. Lions are a legit problem on offense even with some injuries so I thought they played awesome. Willis’s ability to takeoff is a must have with the oline being outmatched and that groin injury looks like it’s a factor. Douglas is looking sharp but gonna need some help. Ollie got some tough yards given the Lions looked ready for those runs between the tackles today. Special teams had a rough day and as a team had too many penalties. From the outside looking in, they appear to be competing and buying in. Man, you gotta enjoy the process. Let’s go Phins! Win out! I Hate Sports would love to win, but it’s also all good losing. Anther game we could have won but understand why we lost. As much as I would enjoy beating the Colts, we must lose to Colts due to their 1st round pick going to the Jets. tvegas897 loves what they are seeing from the defense and sees Willis as a placeholder. Loving what I see for the future of this young defense. Add some beef upfront (Grant is another miss by Grier) and a bonafied Edge rusher and they can be special. Secondary is getting better but they are still a couple players short there as well. Offense is a different story. AJ can’t hit the road fast enough. Savi and Brewer both played poorly. Way too many false starts. They cannot pass up on J Smith if they would be lucky enough to have a shot at him. There’s no Alpha reciever on this roster. And I am thinking Mailk might be handing over the reins as soon as mid next year if they draft a qb. He’s merely a placeholder DolphinsKings1 is someone I assume was pleased to see Malik sent…

title: 5 Things I Think I Think About the Miami Dolphins After Week 9
summary: If I told you before kickoff that the Dolphins would hold the NFL’s No. 1 offense to 19 points, sack Jared Goff three times, force his second interception of the season and limit Jahmyr Gibbs to 74 rushing yards, you’d probably assume Miami just won their second game of the season. Instead, the Dolphins scored […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Derrick Moore #8 of the Detroit Lions rushes Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins during the first half of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images If I told you before kickoff that the Dolphins would hold the NFL’s No. 1 offense to 19 points, sack Jared Goff three times, force his second interception of the season and limit Jahmyr Gibbs to 74 rushing yards, you’d probably assume Miami just won their second game of the season. Instead, the Dolphins scored just 9 points and wasted one of their best defensive performances of the season. In many ways, it was a repeat of what we just saw against New England: A dominating defensive performance in the first half, a little bit of give in the second and a flaccid counterpunch. For long stretches, Miami looked capable of hanging with one of the NFL’s best teams. Unfortunately, every positive seemed to be offset by a mistake, penalty or missed opportunity. Here are five more things I think I think. The defense is going to be the class of the division (someday soon) Last week, one of my thoughts was that there’s a good team hiding somewhere inside this Dolphins roster. You wouldn’t think another loss would contribute to that opinion, but even after the team fell to 1-7, the defense gave us plenty of proof to back it up. The Lions came into the game averaging nearly 400 yards per game and looking every bit like one of the NFL’s elite offenses. The Dolphins held them to 270 total yards and one offensive touchdown. They got Jared Goff off his spot. They forced him to throw away passes. They pressured him all afternoon. They limited the NFL’s best running back to 74 rushing yards on 20 carries. ESPN’s Total QBR measures a quarterback’s overall impact on winning, accounting for passing, rushing, sacks and game situation. A score of 50 is average; anything below 25 is considered poor. Goff finished with a QBR of 17.7. That’s a tremendous statement from Miami’s defense and a clear indicator of how uncomfortable they made one of the league’s best quarterbacks. (What was Malik Willis’ QBR, you ask? Shush, you. We’ll get to that.) The offense wasted a golden opportunity The defense handed the offense exactly the kind of game you dream about when facing a Super Bowl contender. Detroit managed just one offensive touchdown, and Miami had every opportunity to win this game. And the Dolphins responded with nine points. Nine! You could count that on two hands and still have one finger left over. (I’ll let you decide which finger that should be.) And this was against a defense that entered the game with some very real statistical warts. The Jets managed 24 points against Detroit earlier this season. The Bills hung 41 on them. Miami couldn’t reach double digits. The Dolphins finished 0-for-3 in the red zone. The biggest sign of offensive life wasn’t even generated by the offense. It came on a fake punt pass from Bradley Pinion. The offensive line never established control of the game. Detroit consistently disrupted the running game, and without a functioning ground attack, the entire offense fell apart. This system is built on running the football, using play-action and moving the launch point for the quarterback. Miami couldn’t do any of it consistently. Even when the Dolphins finally generated a game-changing play, a 51-yard completion to Kevin Coleman Jr., a holding penalty erased it. It’s hard enough to beat good teams. It’s impossible when you erase your own biggest plays. Special teams continue to be not-so-special At some point, these unforced errors stop feeling like isolated mistakes and start feeling like part of the team’s identity. The Dolphins opened the game with punter and kickoff specialist Bradley Pinion failing to put the kickoff in the landing zone, immediately handing Detroit favorable field position. In the second quarter, Pinion then shanked a punt 25 yards to the Dolphins 47, setting up an easy Lions field goal. And Zane Gonzalez missed an easy 38-yard field goal to prevent the Dolphins from entering halftime tied. The Dolphins’ habit of shooting themselves in the foot is what makes this rebuild so hard to watch. Which leads me to … The Dolphins keep finding ways to beat themselves If there were one play that captured this game, it would be the opening kickoff miscue. But if there were a second play, it would be the Dolphins’ last gasp on offense. Fourth-and-long, and Miami needs a first down to keep the game alive. Caleb Douglas works himself open beyond the sticks with nobody around him. The ball drinks off his hands. Game (essentially) over. That play wasn’t the reason Miami lost – it was simply the final example, a bookend of futility to the opening kick. On top of the mental mistakes were the penalties – the Dolphins committed 11 of them for 87 yards, including five (!) for offensive holding. Young teams are going to make physical mistakes. Receivers will drop passes. Quarterbacks will miss throws. Defenders will miss tackles. But mental mistakes are preventable, and right now, the Dolphins make far too many of them. Malik Willis probably shouldn’t have been playing Last week I said I was looking forward to seeing how Willis performed against the Lions. I would like to retract that statement from the record. This isn’t meant as an excuse – Willis was bad. The pass into double coverage was an easy pick that had no chance of being completed. As bad as Goff’s 17.7 QBR was, it’s miles ahead of Willis’ 7.8. Willis completed just 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards and rarely looked comfortable. To his credit, he seemed determined to gut it out. The problem is that the version of Willis that gives Miami a chance to win is the one that can threaten defenses with his legs. That player wasn’t available Sunday. The television broadcast mentioned a groin injury during the game, and that showed up on the field. Willis looked hesitant to run and a couple of times limped to the sidelines when pressured. I’m actually surprised they let him take the field. One more thing When you’re as young as the Dolphins are, you expect growing pains on all three phases of the game. But the defense is beginning to separate itself from the rest of the team. After failing to record a sack in their first three games, the Dolphins have notched 12 over the past five, including eight in the past three. They’ve also allowed 22.8 points per game over that five-game stretch, which includes matchups against explosive offenses like Detroit and Cincinnati. It’s hard to find comparable evidence of progress on the other side of the ball. The game marked the fifth time this season where the Dolphins managed fewer than 14 points, and this time at home against one of the statistically worst defenses in the league. There are plenty of possible explanations. Defense often develops faster than offense. Malik Willis is making his first attempt at being a full-time starter and couldn’t run. Injuries have disrupted the offensive skill positions throughout the season. And the Dolphins invested heavily in building this defense over the last two offseasons. All of those factors matter. That said, the gap between defense and the rest of the team seems to be getting wider by the week, and if each player is competing to be part of the Dolphins’ future, I’d have to assume offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik and special teams coordinator Chris Tabor are as well. By Week 9, it’s fair to expect evidence of progress. The defense is providing it – the offense and special teams are still searching.

title: Miami Dolphins vs. Detroit Lions Week 9 review: In-game course correction
summary: Full disclosure: I had to re-write my article that I was writing during the game. Here’s how the original article started: Are we the Miami Dolphins or the Mediocre Dolphins? I hear all the propaganda that we are a serious organization. I have major doubts and I give them 24 hours to make a final […]
full_text: Full disclosure: I had to re-write my article that I was writing during the game. Here’s how the original article started: Are we the Miami Dolphins or the Mediocre Dolphins? I hear all the propaganda that we are a serious organization. I have major doubts and I give them 24 hours to make a final decision about how serious they ACTUALLY are. Right now, the mediocre Phins are a 2/3rds team. THE DOLPHINS HAVE CONCEDED NOT WINNING THE SPECIAL TEAMS EVERY SINGLE GAME! I repeat. THE DOLPHINS HAVE CONCEDED TO NOT WINNING THE SPECIAL TEAMS EVERY SINGLE GAME! We cannot go through the next 3-5 years of a rebuild holding our breath EVERY SINGLE TIME we kick a field goal. We cannot through the next 3-5 years giving the opponent starting field position at their own 40. We cannot go through the next 3-5 years giving up the most pathetic fake punt conversion ever. That’s how it started: You all know that the we got ONE special teams win that led to the three points. And they kicked a kickoff that did not land in the zone. Update to my article : I am giving them 48 hours to revamp the special teams….we all know that won’t happen. Here is the new article: We lived and did die with Malik Malik was obviously off Sunday I don’t know if many of you have pulled a groin, but IT IS HUMBLING. Analogous to a rib injury: if you laugh, cough or pass gas, or hit a speed bump, it is SUPER PAINFUL and then it occupies your subconscious whether you admit it or not. “Maybe I will drive around that speed bump, maybe I will wait until 2 minutes longer to use the toilet and when I do, I will hold my breath” NOT MAKING EXCUSES for Malik, however, I will refer you to my column “How to solve a problem like Malik!” and throwing off your front foot is CRITICAL for the pass to get where it needs to go. He is not a natural QB BUT we don’t have the personnel YET to “hide” Malik. I could bore you with examples but we went to the Super Bowl with David Woodley and if not for a missed tackle by Don McNeal (I still love you, Alabama man) we would’ve won that Super Bowl. Woodley had his moments but wasn’t that good. Marino was drafted and then we had the opposite problem: a SB caliber QB with inferior talent around him. Think Malik is bad? Did you see Carson Wentz last night? Oooof! You all know that we have been there! Cleo Lemon, John Beck, Daunte Culpepper….I have to stop or I will pluck out my own eyebrows. Let’s not forget Malik hit a deep shot, just beautiful, but HELL no, holding. Negated. The refs really affected the game. But I will admit some of the holding calls were good calls. But Detroit’s oline doesn’t hold at all? Hmmmm. Our line was OK against a ferocious D-line. I saw pieces of good things on offense. We just need to upgrade the trenches on both sides. Again, we are moving in the right direction. Ollie was effective and decent. If you want to criticize the Phins’ run game, go back to the 1990 NY Giants with Ottis Anderson, from the “U” and Forest Hill High School in West Palm Beach. 3.5 yards per carry and won the Super Bowl! It is moving in the right direction. Ollie “kept his mouth shut today and soldiered” on (Warriors’ film reference—did you know that groundbreaking film was a modern day telling of the Odyssey. But where we are not with our run game is the mantra I discussed earlier—can you get 2 yards when the other team KNOWS it is coming. We RARELY did that under McDaniel. I can remember many “gotta have it” short runs blown up in the BACKFIELD. We did get some Achane “bullet train” runs and those made me scream out loud. I see us wanting to be physical, again we need more “big uglies” (Keith Jackson reference, remember him?) up front. Sorry for the stream of consciousness. OBSERVATIONS: 1)I LOVE IT WHEN THE PHINSIDER’S READERS RESPOND! Please keep responding! I love all the Latin jokes. I did snort a couple of times. The differing perspectives make this whole endeavor so much fun. If we actually owned the Phins we could put our money where our mouth is. Ha. 2) Don’t forget these “coaches” make hundreds of thousands/millions per year along with the GM! So withering criticism comes with the job. 3)PLAYMAKERS MAKE PLAYS! Chop is playmaking but I am afraid he is doing a contract push and once he gets paid, he will revert to Chump. 4)If Trent Green says the word “Layer” one more time, I will set his voodoo doll on fire. That man opened his kindergarten Thesaurus and found a new word. I almost started a game of “Hi, Bob” but I can’t get drunk on RC Cola. GO PHINS

On Wednesday, the team made a move to replace their defensive lineman. Miami signed Keith Cooper Jr. off of the Carolina Panthers’ practice […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Keith Cooper Jr. #97 of the Miami Dolphins leaves the field after warmups against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins announced yesterday that veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler would miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a biceps tear he suffered against the Detroit Lions last Sunday. On Wednesday, the team made a move to replace their defensive lineman. Miami signed Keith Cooper Jr. off of the Carolina Panthers’ practice squad. The move immediately places Cooper on Miami’s 53-man roster. Here’s what Miami’s official website had to say about Cooper. “Cooper Jr. has appeared in four career games with Cleveland (2025) and Miami (2026), recording one tackle. He first joined the Dolphins on Jan. 9, 2026, and spent the first three weeks of the season on Miami’s active roster. Cooper Jr. entered the NFL as an undrafted college free agent with Detroit in 2025 and spent time on the practice squad with the Lions and the Browns. He finished his collegiate career at Houston (2024), where he started 12 games and recorded 46 tackles (25 solo), 3.5 sacks, 8.5 tackles for loss, two passes defensed and one fumble recovery. He transferred to Houston from Tulane following the 2023 season after appearing in 39 career games with 15 starts and recording 73 tackles (37 solo), 10.5 sacks, 16 tackles for loss, five passes defensed and one forced fumble in three seasons (2021-23) with the Green Wave.”

Hockenson* TE Wrist/Chest DNP Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins* DT Ankle DNP Jauan Jennings* WR Calf DNP Kyler Murray QB Hamstring DNP Kyle Van Noy OLB Calf DNP Jay Ward S Knee LP Carson Wentz QB Ankle LP Theo Jackson* S Quad FP Green Bay Packers Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Aaron Banks* LG Knee/Hip LP Chris Brooks RB Ankle LP Javon Bullard* S Ankle/Knee DNP Zaire Franklin* LB Shin DNP Travis Glover OT Knee LP Ty’Ron Hopper LB Illness LP Josh Jacobs* RB Finger DNP Bo Melton WR Concussion FP Skyy Moore WR Ankle LP Micah Parsons* (PUP) OLB Knee/Illness LP Sean Rhyan* C Ankle DNP Trey Smack* K Right Calf LP Lukas Van Ness* OLB Back DNP Josh Whyle TE Concussion DNP Savion Williams WR Groin LP Kevin Zeitler* RG Ankle LP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, Blake Cashman is the most significant player on the list as he is in concussion protocol. It is not typical for players to clear the concussion protocol and not miss at least one game, and this being a short week makes if probably even less likely. We’ll see how he progresses but it’s reasonable at this point to expect that Cashman will miss the Packers game. Cashman was the only player Kevin O’Connell pointed out in his press conference on Wednesday, meaning he was the one most at risk of not playing on Sunday, although Kyler Murray isn’t likely to be active for Sunday’s game either. We’ll see how the others progress tomorrow and Friday- obviously not good to have so many with estimated DNP statuses but that may change beginning tomorrow. For the Packers, Josh Jacobs broke his finger and is scheduled to have surgery on it this week so he is unlikely to play on Sunday. He is expected to miss at least a couple weeks. Micah Parsons has had his 3-week window open to return from the PUP list, but I suspect the plan has always been for him to return after the Packers bye-week, which follows Sunday’s game. He was also suffering from an illness on Wednesday. But I don’t see that he’s been ramping up much yet where he would play on Sunday, although he is expected to participate in some 11-on-11 activities in practice this week. The Packers interior offensive line starters are all on the injury list. Aaron Banks has been on the injury list pretty much the whole season for the Packers and hasn’t played much, so difficult to tell whether he’ll play on Sunday or not. He has a new hip injury. Center Sean Rhyan being a DNP is notable and not a good sign for his availability on Sunday having missed the last two games with the same ankle injury. Kevin Zeitler’s ankle seems more like something he can play through at this point. He was just inserted into the starting offensive line last week after spending several weeks ramping up after being acquired. Defensively, outside of Parsons, Lukas Van Ness, Javon Bullard, and Zaire Franklin are players to watch. Both are starters that had DNP statuses on Wednesday. Franklin has missed the last three games so his not practicing isn’t a good sign for Sunday availability although Packers head coach Matt LaFleur expressed some optimism about him being able to practice later this week. He also didn’t completely close the door on Rhyan being available on Sunday. Van Ness’ injury is new, so unclear how severe it is at this point. Javon Bullard had to come out of the game a few times last week due to injury so unclear if his injuries will keep him out or not. Lastly, Packers kicker Trey Smack is dealing with a calf injury on his kicking leg, so another player to watch later this week. We’ll have updates tomorrow and Friday with injury designations. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Minnesota Vikings News and Links: Only Way To Go Is Up!
summary: The Vikings got a QB that they feel can at least give them a competent offense. Kirk Cousins has done that before. Now the focus will shift to the offensive line and will forever be on the play calling. KOC gets a lot of hate here and elsewhere because the offense has struggled this year. […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 9: Defensive Coordinator Brian Flores of the Minnesota Vikings smiles prior to an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Vikings got a QB that they feel can at least give them a competent offense. Kirk Cousins has done that before. Now the focus will shift to the offensive line and will forever be on the play calling. KOC gets a lot of hate here and elsewhere because the offense has struggled this year. It also was not good when his starting QBs got injured. When he did have his starting QB they won 13 and 14 games. KOC has a 65% winning percentage while having to deal with 9 different starting QBs mainly because of injury and in Cousins case, unable to reach a contract extension. That is outstanding coaching. Here is a list of teams with 7 different starting QBs since 2022 and their winning pct … Team | Starting QBs | Win % Cleveland Browns | 10 | .403 New York Giants | 10 | .355 Las Vegas Raiders | 10 | .325 New York Jets | 10 | .312 Indianapolis Colts | 9 | .403 Minnesota Vikings | 8 | .645 Arizona Cardinals | 8 | .286 San Francisco 49ers | 7 | .658 Los Angeles Rams | 7 | .545 Miami Dolphins | 7 | .474 Washington Commanders | 7 | .408 Tennessee Titans | 7 | .263 The fire KOC herd mentality masses have gone completely mental. But heh, some dweeb gave him the QB Whisperer moniker and the herd just accepted it as their reality even though he never claimed to be that at all. I have said before that I doubted the Wilfs would let him go due to his 36-45M in pay they would still owe. But another commenter pointed out to me that if another team hired him then the offset language that is common in coaches contracts would absolve them from much of that money (if not all). I imagine that there will be teams lining up to try and hire him. Right now, the herd mentality says KOC is on the hot seat and if the team does not win a playoff game then the Wilfs should fire him. The majority of media types and fans share this mindset. Cool. Let’s say the Wilf’s do fire him and another team signs him. The media will praise the other team for hiring a coach with a 65% winning record who has to navigate 9 different starting QBs and the, they will blast the Vikings for giving up on him. That is my prediction. Now that I have shared the above nonsense with you, there is one caveat to replacing KOC and that is Brian Flores. Flores has his unit playing as the top defense in the NFL right now and hopefully it stays there but if not, it should finish top 5 at the least. You got a coach who has his side of the ball playing great and another coach who has his side of the ball floundering due to poor QB play, too complicated an offense (doubtful), etc. The Wilfs very well could decide to keep Flores. In that case, maybe a trade could be had whereby another team asks about KOC. Other teams can read tea leaves too. Some could say why not wait for him to be let go but then there is a chance for a bidding war. Maybe another team wants first dibs? The question I have is that this offensive ineffectiveness could be hurting any trade value. Let’s say the Commanders want to get rid of Dan Quinn. Would the be willing to trade for KOC? What could the Vikings ask for? What about the Cowboys, Colts, Chargers, or Jets? I would be happy with two 2nd round picks for KOC. Then, the Wilfs can promote Flores. There is all this talk about what team will hire Flores as head coach with the lawsuit going on. Well, one team has hired him to be DC and gave him a nice bump in pay this offseason. I doubt the Wilfs care about any backlash for promoting him to head coach. The team that could hire Flores as head coach is the Vikings. KOC would have to agree to get traded but being able to coach Daniels may be appealing. Let’s go with the Commandos giving up two 2nd round picks for KOC. Moving on to the stinking Pukers. It is going to be a tough game as the Packer seem to have found their groove offensively as they are averaging 28.0 points and 371.0 total yards per game over their last four contests. Their rushing attack is bad though. Over their last four games7, the Pukers have averaged 78.0 rushing yards per game and 3.03 yards per carry (312 rushing yards on 103 attempts). In the first game, Love threw for 387 yards and two touchdowns, with Christian Watson catching six passes for 147 yards and Matthew Golden adding six catches for 95 yards. The lack of a running game and the critical turnovers doomed them. Also, the 12 penalties for their obvious cheating did them no favors as well. We cannot expect the zebras to be friendly this week. Expect a lot of cheating. Love does get explosive plays against the Vikings but the relentless volume of pressures eventually wears them down. Let’s hope that happens again. The key for me is the offense maintain some long drives to keep the ball out of their hands and to give the defense rest. The defense was on the field for 42:32 against the Bills. They were on the field 20:49 vs the Dolphins and 20:23 vs the Saints and nobody was handing out tissues to them after those games. Before the Bills game the defense was averaging 28:29 per game on the field. The Bills game bumped it up to 30:15 per game. The defense should be fine. Minnesota Vikings News and Links Kirk Cousins trade grades: Vikings hope to salvage offense; Raiders get ‘A,’ turn to Fernando Mendoza https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/kirk-cousins-trade-grades-vikings-raiders-fernando-mendoza/ Kevin O’Connell and the Minnesota Vikings are making one last-ditch attempt to save their offense, reuniting with Kirk Cousins and sending their 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders in return. Minnesota Vikings: B- That the Vikings are even in this situation is worthy of an “F.” Ever since Cousins left, they have failed to find a suitable replacement: Sam Darnold was excellent in 2024, but the Vikings let him go in favor of J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy played poorly and was hurt several times last year, as the Vikings rode a quarterback carousel. Minnesota traded McCarthy, who had been demoted to third-string behind Murray and Wentz, to the Giants early this season. Murray — always a curious-at-best fit for this offense — clearly wasn’t cutting it, and Wentz was never going to, either. Cousins has been good this year — not great, but good. He looks far better than what he had been in Atlanta, where it was clear his mobility hadn’t returned post-Achilles tear. He’s still never going to win with his athleticism, but his negative play rate is down to 6.7%, on pace for a career best, and he is only being sacked on 9.8% of his dropbacks, also on pace for a career best. How much of that praise belongs to Klint Kubiak is up for debate, but it’s clear Cousins has regained some of his spryness. He doesn’t have to be Michael Vick, but he can’t be a statue. Really, though, this all comes down to fit. Murray never fit. Cousins, hypothetically, does. Obviously, there is proof of concept here given his past in Minnesota. He attacks the middle of the field and delivers on intermediate throws. Plus, he is comfortable off play action. These are crucial parts of O’Connell’s scheme. Cousins, if nothing else, should do a much, much better job keeping the offense on schedule. Given the circumstances, this grade can only be so high, and given the solution, it cannot get that much higher. Cousins is not a star. His arm strength is not what it once was, and for all the good things he did in Las Vegas, he is coming off a three-interception game. We’ll see how he holds up, physically, over the rigors of an 18-game regular season (he will not get a bye) plus expected postseason. His accuracy is a bit down from his best years, though it’s still a clear major improvement over Murray and Wentz, who at times seemed unable to hit water if they fell off a boat. full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - JANUARY 15: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings reacts after losing to the New York Giants in the NFC Wild Card playoff game at U.S. Bank Stadium on January 15, 2023 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images This is certainly not an article I expected to write at the start of the season. However, the Vikings’ trade for Kirk Cousins makes all the sense in the world. The Las Vegas Raiders appear ready to see what they have in former No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, while the Minnesota Vikings have somehow scraped together a 6-2 record behind a dominant defense, excellent special teams, and one of the worst offenses in football. The Vikings aren’t going to suddenly become an offensive juggernaut because of this move, but Cousins gives them something they haven’t had all season: competency at quarterback. The running game has struggled, in part because opposing defenses haven’t respected the passing attack. Minnesota ranks second-to-last in the NFL at just 160.8 passing yards per game. Meanwhile, Cousins is averaging more than 260 passing yards and two touchdowns per game, though he is also averaging more than one turnover. The Raiders’ four wins have come against the Dolphins, Chargers, Saints, and Jets. They played the Chiefs and Bills tough, but were blown out by the Rams, 49ers, and Patriots. The numbers suggest Cousins can still function as a capable NFL starter, even if he’s no longer the player he was at his peak. None of this guarantees success. The pessimist in me remembers the Randy Moss reunion and a long history of veteran acquisitions that failed to meet expectations. Midseason additions rarely transform teams into Super Bowl contenders. That said, it’s absolutely the right move to make. This defense deserves better than what it has received from the offense through the first half of the season.. I’m not ready to declare them Super Bowl contenders just yet, but they win on Sunday, I might be. Nothing would be more Minnesota than to win the Super Bowl with an enigma of a quarterback like Kirk Cousins.

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 13: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18) hauls in a pass for a 39-yard touchdown reception as Green Bay Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (2) defends during the second quarter of a NFL game between the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers on September 13, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis MN. (Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The second installment of the “Border Battle” for the 2026 NFL season is upon us, as the Minnesota Vikings make their annual trip to Lambeau Field this week to face off with the Green Bay Packers. These two teams faced off to start the regular season at U.S. Bank Stadium in a game that saw the Packers jump out to a big lead early and remain on top by a score of 22-10 with around five minutes left in the third quarter. Then, the Vikings’ defense took over, forcing several Packer turnovers and sparking the purple to 29 unanswered points over the final 20 minutes of regulation time to emerge with a 39-22 victory to get their season off to a 1-0 start. The Vikings won their first six games of the season and were the last undefeated team in the NFL, but have lost their last two games because of a lack of offense. Both the Detroit Lions and the Buffalo Bills were able to take advantage of the inability of the Minnesota offense to sustain drives and stay on the field, eventually wearing down the NFL’s best defense and sending the Vikings to two consecutive losses. To that end, the Vikings acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders at the trade deadline in the hopes of making those sorts of issues a thing of the past. The Packers, after getting off to a 1-2 start to the season, have won five of their last six games and are coming off of a big 45-27 victory over the New England Patriots in Foxborough in Week 9. The game saw Jordan Love throw three touchdown passes and the Green Bay defense force Drake May into three interceptions as the game may not have even been as close as the 18-point margin would make it seem. The Packers come into this game with a record of 6-3. . .a mark that, somehow, puts them in last place in the NFC North, which is once again the best division in the NFL. Kickoff for this week’s game is slated for noon Central Time, and the game will be broadcast on the FOX family of networks around the country. We will be putting everything relating to this week’s game in this stream for you, so keep checking back for all the latest. title: Mack Hollins happy with Patriots’ response after post-game challenge
summary: The New England Patriots were, unsurprisingly, not happy with the performance they put forward last Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. No player verbalized that more clearly than wide receiver Mack Hollins, who put a challenge to his teammates. “If you’re not ready to come to work Tuesday and Wednesday and get on that plane […]
full_text: The New England Patriots were, unsurprisingly, not happy with the performance they put forward last Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. No player verbalized that more clearly than wide receiver Mack Hollins, who put a challenge to his teammates. “If you’re not ready to come to work Tuesday and Wednesday and get on that plane and work all this week, you’re probably not meant for this team,” he said. “If there are guys on this team that are OK with that, I’m sure there are 31 other teams they can go to and maybe they can live like that. But we’re trying to get stuff done about this week.” So, with the smoke having settled on the 45-27 defeat, how does Hollins feel about the state of the Patriots? It appears better. Talking to the media on Wednesday, before the team’s flight to Germany for its upcoming international game with the Detroit Lions, he added further context to his prior comments and along the way praised the team’s response to its fourth loss of the season. “I think it’s good,” the 33-year-old said. “We’re excited for another opportunity, and I think the guys are focused on the ‘one week at a time’ mentality, which is a good thing. You’re trying to reach too far ahead or too far behind you, it’s hard to know where your feet are.” Hollins was not the only member of the organization to highlight the Patriots’ work ethic and mental toughness this week. Head coach Mike Vrabel did as well, effectively echoing what the wideout said on Sunday. And even with some time having passed, Hollins stood by every word he said. “If you come after that game and said, ‘We did enough, it’s not my fault,’ you’re not able to look in the mirror and say, ‘I can get better.’ It’s more of that than guys aren’t working or guys aren’t doing things,” he explained. “If you get this result and you’re OK with it, and you’re like, ‘I don’t need to come to practice next week and come to work, and I’d rather be somewhere where I can just relax and not do anything,’ this isn’t the place for you. I always stand by that, because I don’t want to play with guys that are like that. I don’t think we have guys like that, because, like we’ve said, we all we are, we all we need. The guys that are here, they come to play. Is the result always want we want? Hell, no. But do you continue to push that and get better? Yes.”

full_text: The New England Patriots defense played one of its worst games in recent memory, allowing the Green Bay Packers to hang 45 points on them while seemingly moving the ball through the air at will. Needless to say, things are not going to get any easier this week. The Detroit Lions are one of the most explosive offensive teams in the league in their own right, and will present another serious challenge to a reeling unit. Adding to the difficulty, for both teams, is that the game will take play overseas: the Patriots and Lions will face off in Munich, Germany, as part of the NFL’s International Series. Let’s find out what the Patriots can expect. Lions key stats Playing in what is currently the best division in football, the Lions are entering Week 10 off of four straight victories and as the fifth playoff seed in the NFC . Their statistics are a reflection of their success, especially on the offensive side of the ball. The unit has the second-best scoring rate in the league (50.0%) and the fourth-best turnover rate (6.1%) while also ranking 10th in both net yards per pass and yards per carry. Needless to say, the Patriots need to show some significant improvement compared to last week — particularly against the pass — in order to play a competitive game against the Lions. Luckily for the Patriots, Detroit’s defense has not been on the same level. No team has given up more passing yards (2,087) or passing touchdowns (18), which bodes well for New England’s ability to put pressure on the unit. In addition, the Lions have taken the ball away only eight time, six of those through interceptions. Lions 2026 season Coming off an underwhelming 9-8 campaign, the Lions started their season in uninspiring fashion. Since Week 5, however, they have played some very good and especially winning football. Week 1: 31-30 OT win vs. New Orleans Saints (1-0) Week 2: 41-31 loss at Buffalo Bills (1-1) Week 3: 31-24 win vs. New York Jets (2-1) Week 4: 32-26 loss at Carolina Panthers (2-2) Week 5: 45-21 win at Arizona Cardinals (3-2) Week 6: Bye Week 7: 20-17 win vs. Green Bay Packers (4-2) Week 8: 19-15 win vs. Minnesota Vikings (5-2) Week 9: 19-9 win at Miami Dolphins (6-2) Detroit started with a one-point overtime win against the Saints that was decided by a missed two-point try, followed by a loss to the Bills that was more lopsided than the final score would indicate. The team bounced back with a one-score victory against the lowly Jets and a loss to the Panthers. The Lions did build some momentum heading into their Week 6 bye and have maintained it ever since, including through quality wins over the Packers and the the then-undefeated Vikings in Weeks 7 and 8. Their most recent game was a defensive win over the Dolphins; Detroit didn’t showcase its offensive firepower but still did enough to secure a 10-point victory. While not a particular rushing threat — he has scored one touchdown on the ground — Goff has been as effective at putting pressure on opposing quarterbacks as any QB in the league. One reason for that is his supporting cast, led by NFL scrimmage yards leader Jahymr Gibbs and volume receiving target Amon-Ra St. Brown. The former has carried the ball a league-high 177 times for 847 yards and nine touchdowns, averaging 4.8 yards per carry; Gibbs also has hauled in 34 passes for 285 yards and two more scores. No player has touched the ball more, gained more yards, or scored more touchdowns this year so far. St. Brown, meanwhile, is ranked first on the team in targets (84), receptions (61), receiving yards (657) and tying fellow wideout Jameson Williams with five receiving touchdowns. Williams (28/468/5) is the Lions’ primary outside receiver, a role also played by second-year man Isaac TeSlaa (11/206/0). Joining them among the starting skill position players is tight end Sam LaPorta (35/399/3). Of course, an offense only can be as good as its offensive line allows it to be. And the Lions’ has been very good, despite undergoing some personnel changes. Still, the Lions’ rushing success and Jared Goff ranking seventh in the league in pressure rate (31.8%) speaks for itself. Speaking of pressure, the Lions defensive line has been able to generate it on a regular basis. They are ranked third in sacks (27) and seventh in pressure rate (25.7%) so far this season. With Jack Campbell on injured reserve, Barnes will be the clear No. 1 option at the position and joined in the starting lineup by veteran rotational option Malcolm Rodriguez. title: What Reggie Gilliam’s return designation means for the Patriots
summary: For the first time in five weeks, the New England Patriots had a traditional fullback at practice on Wednesday. Reggie Gilliam, who was initially placed on injured reserve due to knee and ankle injuries in early October, made his comeback during his team’s final session before its trip to Germany for the upcoming Week 10 […]
full_text: For the first time in five weeks, the New England Patriots had a traditional fullback at practice on Wednesday. Reggie Gilliam, who was initially placed on injured reserve due to knee and ankle injuries in early October, made his comeback during his team’s final session before its trip to Germany for the upcoming Week 10 meeting with the Detroit Lions. This means he is now officially designated to return from IR. Let’s check out how this impacts the Patriots for the time being. Clock starts ticking We will get into the actual on-field impact of a potential Gilliam return to the 53-man roster once/if he is activated. For now, at least, the window for such a follow-up move has been opened. This means that, at least theoretically, Gilliam could be back on the game day roster as soon as this Sunday against the Lions. He will join the rest of the team on the flight to Germany, so there is an option New England could activate him in time for the game. They don’t have to, however: the team has 21 days to make that call before the return window will close again. If not activated at that point, Gilliam would revert back to injured reserve to end his season. Obviously, with return designations limited — more on that in a second — the expectation is is that the 29-year-old will eventually return to the 53-man roster when all is said and done. Two guys, one spot Following Monday’s release of tight end Tanner Arkin — a move that might hint at a potential Gilliam activation given that the rookie served as a stand-in fullback over the last few weeks — the Patriots have 52 of the 53 spots on their active roster occupied. This means that they could easily activate Gilliam without having to make a follow-up move. There is only one problem: he is not the only player currently in the 21-day window. Interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten, who was the next man up after starting right guard Mike Onwenu fractured his ankle in September, returned to practice last week. He too is a candidate to be activated, especially given the current state of New England’s interior offensive line. Fact is, in order to bring both of them back, somebody will have to be removed from the active roster. There are several options, but one of them can effectively be ruled out: a player getting cut. With the Patriots taking their entire healthy roster to Germany, one of the 52 players getting handed his walking papers seems like a highly unlikely outcome. What is more likely is that only one of them will be brought back this week, or that the additional spot for a second activation will be created by moving another player to an injury list. There are multiple candidates such as the three non-participants during Wednesday’s practice — RB TreVeyon Henderson, OL Ben Brown, CB Carlton Davis — or offensive lineman Walter Rouse, who currently finds himself in concussion protocol. Another returnee The NFL allows every team to bring up to eight players back from injured reserve during the regular season. With Gilliam now getting designated as such a return player, the Patriots have used up five of those already. They previously designated wide receivers A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins as well as offensive linemen Marcus Bryan and the aforementioned Greg Van Roten for activation. All but Van Roten currently reside on the 53-man roster, with the O-lineman in the 21-day window alongside Gilliam. This also means that only three spots are left for the six eligible players currently remaining on injured reserve: WR Romeo Doubs, RG Mike Onwenu, LG Alijah Vera-Tucker, ED Quintayvious Hutchins, LB Khalil Jacobs, and S Dell Pettus. Doubs and Vera-Tucker appear to be the frontrunners to be brought back from that group both considering their injuries and importance to the roster as a whole. By the way, whether or not Gilliam (or Van Roten, for that matter) is actually activated to the 53-man roster is immaterial to the designation. He counts against those eight available return spots regardless.

full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 11: Tanner Arkin #84 of the New England Patriots runs against the Las Vegas Raiders following an NFL football game at Gillette Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images After 48 hours away, Tanner Arkin has made his way back to the New England Patriots. The organization officially signed the rookie tight end to the practice squad on Wednesday. He cleared waivers the afternoon prior. Arkin, 23, had been let go from the 53-man roster on the heels of last weekend’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium. The 6-foot-4, 262-pound blocking tight end now takes the open spot on the 17-man practice squad after the recent release of outside linebacker Jose Ramirez. Arriving in Foxborough as part of the 2026 undrafted class , Arkin outlasted the NFL’s cutdown deadline heading out of training camp. The former transfer from Colorado State to Illinois went on to appear in five games, including back-to-back starts, before finding himself on the league’s transaction wire. He played 60 snaps on offense and 41 snaps on special teams while also seeing time at fullback in the absence of incumbent Reggie Gilliam, who has since been designated to return from injured reserve. The Patriots move further into the fall with captain Hunter Henry, No. 95 overall pick Eli Raridon and August waiver claim Cameron Latu on the active tight end depth chart. On the practice squad, Arkin joins September signing Tanner Conner at the position. Mike Vrabel’s 5-4 team will face Dan Campbell’s 6-2 Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday as part of the NFL international series. Kickoff at Munich’s Allianz Arena is set for 9:30 a.m. ET.

summary: After missing the past five games, New England Patriots fullback Reggie Gilliam has been designated to return from injured reserve. Head coach Mike Vrabel made the announcement during his Wednesday press conference before the team travels to Germany to face the Detroit Lions. Gilliam, 29, went on injured reserve at the start of October due […]
full_text: September 20, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots fullback Reggie Gilliam (44) warms up before a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After missing the past five games, New England Patriots fullback Reggie Gilliam has been designated to return from injured reserve. Head coach Mike Vrabel made the announcement during his Wednesday press conference before the team travels to Germany to face the Detroit Lions. Gilliam, 29, went on injured reserve at the start of October due to knee and ankle injuries . He now has a 21-day practice window to work his way back to the 53-man roster. NFL clubs can designate a maximum of eight players for return from injured reserve per season. The 6-foot-1, 255-pound lead blocker marks the fifth to already get the call in Foxborough, following wide receivers A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins, offensive tackle Marcus Bryant and guard Greg Van Roten, who was back at practice as a limited participant last week. For now, the 5-4 Patriots carry an open spot on the active roster as well as the practice squad as the 6-2 Lions await. “We’ll probably get to 53,” Vrabel said of where things stand ahead of the NFL international series. “I mean, Greg has return to play. Reggie Gilliam will be back practicing, so that’ll be good. We’ll have to see where that goes. Wednesday is the first practice of the week and it’ll be important for us to see how those guys do.” Since arriving at Gillette Stadium on a three-year contract in March, Gilliam has played 58 snaps on offense and 39 snaps on special teams. Through four appearances elsewhere in the AFC East, he’s twice been in the starting lineup. The former Buffalo Bill stands 98 games, including 13 starts, into an NFL run that began as an undrafted free agent out of Toledo in 2020. His career includes 153 yards and two touchdowns from scrimmage across 25 combined carries and catches. Sunday’s kickoff at FC Bayern Munich Stadium is set for 9:30 a.m. ET. The bye week will follow.

title: Tom Brady offers high praise for Drake Maye despite rough Patriots loss
summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye did not play his best game Sunday with Tom Brady back at Gillette Stadium. With Brady calling the game from the broadcast both, Maye threw three interceptions in the Patriots’ 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Despite the rough outing, the former Patriots quarterback remains impressed by what […]
full_text: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye did not play his best game Sunday with Tom Brady back at Gillette Stadium. With Brady calling the game from the broadcast both, Maye threw three interceptions in the Patriots’ 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Despite the rough outing, the former Patriots quarterback remains impressed by what he has seen from Maye throughout his young career. “Been absolutely terrific,” Brady said on the Fox broadcast. “To come in here in his first year, it was a totally different offense and it didn’t really showcase what his abilities were. Then he got Josh McDaniels in his second year who is really teaching him the cerebral part of the game. He’s orchestrating the line. He’s orchestrating the protections and the run games. Over the last two years I see the maturity. I see the willingness to know when he can change a play and when he can’t. And just his overall expectation for himself all the time.” After a rookie season in which Maye started just 12 games, the quarterback took a significant Year 2 leap when paired with offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels. Maye went on to break Brady’s single-season franchise record with a 72% completion rate while throwing for 4,394 yards and 31 touchdowns. He finished second in MVP voting and led the Patriots to the Super Bowl. His third season has featured more ups and downs. Following a slower start, Maye had operated as one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks over the five weeks leading into Sunday’s matchup with Green Bay. While his overall performance has been less consistent this season, Brady has continued to notice his growth within the offense he spent much of his career in. “When Josh would normally just bring in the game plan, he would just kind of go, ‘Hey, this is what we’re running.’ Now Drake Maye is like, ‘No, no, no, how about we put this guy in this spot and this guy in this spot?’” Brady said. “There’s much more ownership from Drake Maye. That’s the cerebral part of the game, when you have this type of quarterback that thinks his way through the game, you’re going to see a progression over time of that play continue to get better and better and better. “I know today has been a rough game obviously with the interceptions, but he’s had a hell of a young career.”

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Lions ahead of Week 10
summary: The coaching staffs range from Terrell Williams and Todd Downing to Mike Kafka and Dan Skipper. But the ties between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions do not end on the sidelines or in the booth. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, eight players in the fold for the trip […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 20: Erick Hunter #49 of the New England Patriots runs onto the field prior to the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Gillette Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The coaching staffs range from Terrell Williams and Todd Downing to Mike Kafka and Dan Skipper. But the ties between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions do not end on the sidelines or in the booth. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, eight players in the fold for the trip to Germany have been members of both locker rooms during their NFL careers. Here’s a glance through the list of ex-Patriots and ex-Lions ahead of Sunday’s 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff at FC Bayern Munich Stadium. DETROIT Joshua Dobbs, quarterback — One March after signing, the Patriots released Dobbs with one year left on his contract. The veteran backup checked into four games during his lone season working alongside starter, captain, Pro Bowler and All-Pro Drake Maye. He completed 7-of-10 passes for 65 yards with no touchdowns nor interceptions. Entering the NFL in the fourth round of the 2017 draft at No. 135 overall by way of the Tennessee Volunteers, Dobbs logged previous stops with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Jacksonville Jaguars, Cleveland Browns, Tennessee Titans, Arizona Cardinals, Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers. The 31-year-old was previously in Detroit, too, and returned during training camp following the retirement of Teddy Bridgewater. The journey has brought 28 games, including 15 starts, while completing 62.8 percent of his passes for 3,346 yards with 17 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. An additional 515 yards and eight scores have been logged as a rusher. DeAndre Carter, wide receiver — A former FCS All-American out of Sacramento State, Carter made stops with the Baltimore Ravens and Oakland Raiders before signing to head coach Bill Belichick’s practice squad as an undrafted rookie in December 2015. He would be released, re-signed and retained on a futures contract at Gillette Stadium en route to catching a touchdown the following preseason. The 33-year-old has since toured double-digit teams around the league and went from the practice squad to the 53-man roster of the Lions in October. Through 114 career games, he stands with 1,336 receiving yards, 99 rushing yards and six touchdowns on offense. A seventh TD arrived on special teams, where Carter’s run includes 1,523 yards on punt returns and 3,468 yards on kickoff returns. K.J. Britt, linebacker — The Lions turned to the Patriots’ practice squad to poach Britt at the start of November. The 27-year-old linebacker now resides on the 53-man roster in Detroit after making the initial cut in Foxborough only to be released as a vested veteran and called upon as a standard elevation. Signed to a one-year pact last offseason, Britt’s career includes 78 games and 16 starts. Selected in the fifth round of the 2021 NFL draft at No. 176 overall, the Auburn product spent his rookie pact with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and finished atop the Miami Dolphins with 76.9 percent of the workload on special teams in 2025. He stands with 162 tackles, half a sack, four stops for loss and three passes defensed through 994 snaps on defense and 1,315 snaps on special teams. Myles Bryant, safety — After four seasons with the Patriots, Bryant’s stay reached its end in 2024 as he agreed to terms with the Houston Texans. A brief stop in the AFC North followed before the 28-year-old defensive back moved on to the NFC South as part of Detroit’s practice squad in October. Originally arrived in Foxborough as an undrafted rookie out of Washington in 2020, Bryant went on to appear in 55 games for the Patriots, including 17 starts, while recording 200 tackles, two sacks, three forced fumbles, one fumble recovery and four interceptions. He now finds himself 77 games into his run in the league while seeing 2,514 snaps on defense and 515 snaps in the kicking game. NEW ENGLAND Cory Durden, defensive tackle — Durden has been in New England’s starting lineup for all nine games this fall. The nose tackle stands with 22 tackles, the initial 1.5 sacks of his NFL career, as well as a new best with five quarterback hits. He began 2025 on the practice squad in Foxborough before quickly earning a promotion to the 53-man roster, appearing in every game on the way to Super Bowl LX. Entering the league as an undrafted free agent by way of Florida State and North Carolina State in 2023, Durden spent his rookie training camp with the Lions before being waived at the cutdown deadline. Stints with the Los Angeles Rams and New York Giants were also part of his path. The 27-year-old had checked into eight games to notch 13 tackles before becoming a Patriot. Erick Hunter, linebacker — An undrafted rookie out of Morgan State, Hunter signed his first NFL contract with the Lions in the spring. The stay ended at the league’s 53-man reduction in August. After clearing waivers, the 23-year-old made his way to the active roster of the Patriots. Now eight appearances into his stay at Gillette Stadium, Hunter has played 14 downs on defense while cutting his teeth with 132 downs on special teams. The 6-foot-4, 224-pound linebacker has stepped in as an oversized gunner downing punts and sits with 13 combined tackles, including one for loss. As far as the Patriots’ kicking game goes, he currently sits tied for the team lead in stops while ranking sixth in terms of snaps played. Carlton Davis III, cornerback — Davis’ Patriots tenure has featured 22 starts in the regular season, plus 96 tackles, including four for loss, and a dozen passes defensed. The 29-year-old cornerback arrived in Foxborough on a three-year deal as an unrestricted free agent in 2025 and has been limited to five appearances this campaign due to injury. Originally entering the NFL in the second round of the 2018 class at No. 63 overall, the Auburn product earned a Super Bowl LV ring while a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The run ended via trade as Davis headed to Detroit along with a pair of sixth-rounders in exchange for a third-rounder that became wide receiver Jalen McMillan. Davis started 13 contests during his lone year as a Lion, tallying 56 tackles, two interceptions, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. Kindle Vildor, cornerback — The 28-year-old Vildor signed with New England in March and began September on the practice squad after being released as a vested veteran. He went from serving as a standard elevation to earning a 53-man roster spot in October, yet has since returned to the 17-man group. Vildor stands with seven tackles, one stop for loss, one pass deflection and one forced fumble across a handful of appearances for the Patriots. Originally entering the league with the Chicago Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall, the Georgia Southern product spent time with five other organizations before landing in the AFC East. Count the Lions among them from 2024 into 2025. Through 85 career games, including 27 starts, the corner has had a hand in 147 tackles, one sack, two forced fumbles and two interceptions across 2,158 snaps on defense and 605 snaps in the kicking game.

title: Have the Saints finally cleaned up their discipline issues?
summary: The New Orleans Saints have spent much of the season making life harder on themselves with costly penalties. Whether it’s been extending opposing drives, putting the offense behind the chains or simply failing to execute when it matters most, discipline has been a consistent concern. However, Sunday’s win over the Cleveland Browns gave fans a […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Chris Olave #12 of the New Orleans Saints reacts during the fourth quarter of a game against the Cleveland Browns at Caesars Superdome on November 08, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints have spent much of the season making life harder on themselves with costly penalties. Whether it’s been extending opposing drives, putting the offense behind the chains or simply failing to execute when it matters most, discipline has been a consistent concern. However, Sunday’s win over the Cleveland Browns gave fans a reason to believe things might finally be moving in the right direction. The Saints finished the day with just four penalties for 25 yards, a big improvement from what we’ve seen throughout the first half of the season. The Saints have struggled to avoid those self-inflicted setbacks, making Sunday’s performance a refreshing change. Coming out of the bye week, there was an opportunity for Kellen Moore, his coaching staff and the players to address some of the issues that have held them back. Still, it would be an overreaction to say the Saints have officially solved their problems. One game, regardless of how encouraging it was, doesn’t take back the mistakes that have continued to show up throughout the first half of the season. Consistency is key in the NFL, and it’s beyond time for Kellen Moore and New Orleans to prove they can maintain this level of discipline moving forward. The encouraging part is that the Saints showed they are capable of playing a much cleaner game. It’s too early to say the issue fixed, but it is certainly fair to believe the bye week helped to some degree. Now the challenge is making Sunday’s discipline the expectation rather than the exception.
author: Nic Jennings

full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 08: Alvin Kamara #41 of the New Orleans Saints runs with the ball against the Cleveland Browns during overtime of an NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on November 8, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another win for the New Orleans Saints, but until the end of the game, it was a bad performance from the offense. This may keep the Saints from jumping higher in the power rankings. NFL.com – 23 (+5) “I’m asking Saints fans to stick with me through this. This ranking, which is still below the team New Orleans just defeated , is not me simply being a hater. I am taking into account the surrounding circumstances of the game, the ugliness of it (until the final few minutes of regulation and overtime) and the larger picture. This was a win the Saints desperately needed, a triumph in which they finally ran the ball with some emphasis, but it’s not going to vault them up into the top half of the rankings. They’ll need more than one of these for that to happen.“ Fox Sports – 23 (+3) “The Saints really needed that win over Cleveland coming out of their bye week, no matter how squeaky it was. They’ve now beaten the Browns and Giants — think of them as two mid-majors — over their last three games. And while the Saints haven’t looked great, they’ve got a golden opportunity to take a measure of control in the NFC South when they play the Panthers in New Orleans on Sunday. In a division where eight wins will likely be enough, every division game matters.“ Bleacher Report – 23 (+5) “The New Orleans Saints came out of their bye with a more aggressive mindset. New Orleans’ defense generated pressure on nearly 48 percent of the Cleveland Browns’ dropbacks Sunday, according to NFL Next Gen Stats (h/t Daniel Oyefusi ). The Saints blitzed 45 percent of the time. Some of this approach is due to facing Shedeur Sanders after the quarterback made certain remarks during the practice week. But New Orleans also failed to close during multiple games this season. In fact, Cleveland nearly made a comeback during this latest outing. However, the Saints will be far better off by remaining aggressive to try and dictate terms after three one-score losses through the first eight games. — Sobleski ” CBS Sports – 23 (+3) “They beat the Browns on Sunday to get their third victory, which ties them for first place. They face a big one this week with Carolina. Can you believe that?” Sports Illustrated – 23 (+3) “I do love that some Saints fans, amid the internet’s seedy underbelly, are taking Harold Fannin’s rumbling touchdown from Sunday as evidence of a choreographed phony and not—as they should—that the Saints just can’t tackle.”

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need as the Giants get set to take on their NFC East rivals Washington Commanders tonight. NFL midseason surprises: 6 teams and players nobody saw coming | SB Nation New York Giants. It is not like things were expected to be much better in […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need as the Giants get set to take on their NFC East rivals Washington Commanders tonight. NFL midseason surprises: 6 teams and players nobody saw coming | SB Nation New York Giants. It is not like things were expected to be much better in New York. Again, looking back at our preseason ranking of all 32 teams, we had the New York Giants in the second-lowest tier, the “Works in Progress” group. But if the NFC playoffs began right now, the Giants would be at home during Wild Card Weekend as the winners of the NFC East, thanks to their 5-2-1 record. That is surprising enough, but when you consider that New York lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart early in the year due to an injury, and running back Cam Skattebo has been iced out — he was inactive for New York’s Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles — the Giants are doing this without two players we all expected to be cornerstones of their offense. Things will get tougher for New York over the second half of the season. The Giants have games against Jacksonville, San Francisco, and Seattle on the docket, and the Week 17 meeting with the Dallas Cowboys could decide the division. Still, these Giants are one of the biggest surprises in the league at the midway point. Nabers: Divisional games mean more Malik Nabers on the importance of this divisional matchup pic.twitter.com/FMrX7QnJFK — GiantsTV (@GiantsTV) November 10, 2026 Game Preview: Nothing worthwhile comes easy for first-place Giants | Giants.com Until they can start winning by wider margins, they will do whatever it takes. “The bottom line is finding a way to win,” Harbaugh said. “It’s all or nothing basically from that perspective. You can win by a bunch, you can win by 40, and it’s still just one, 1-0. But you’d rather win by 40. There’s no doubt about it. Really, [it’s] just chasing that, playing better in a way that makes it really tough for your opponent to even stay close if you’re good enough to do that. So, we would like to get to that place.” The bright lights are calling Cam Skattebo again. So are the Giants | The Record Cam Skattebo walked to the center of the New York Giants’ locker room, leaned against the ping-pong table and greeted the small group of reporters converging on his space. “What up?” Skattebo yelped. A lot’s been up with the Giants: trade talk for Jonathan Taylor, which ended with a whimper when the NFL deadline passed roughly 40 minutes after Skattebo’s post-practice interview. As Giants don’t land Jonathan Taylor, offensive concerns remain: ‘We’re not there yet’ | NJ.com In the end, the Giants didn’t add a weapon — like running back Jonathan Taylor — at Tuesday’s trade deadline. So what now for their offense, as it tries to find stability with replacement quarterback J.J. McCarthy, amid the push for a shocking NFC East title? “We’re still finding our way,” said wide receiver Darnell Mooney of the Giants’ offense. “What we need to continue to do is find our offense, find our identity. We’re still looking for it. We’re still looking for what we are great at. I don’t think anything has been great [enough] to be like: ‘Oh, we have enough.’ NFL Wide Receiver Rankings: Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains No. 1 | PFF 7. Malik Nabers, New York Giants (up 1). Nabers is coming off his second-lowest-graded game of the season but moves up one spot with Mike Evans dropping out due to time missed. Being held to 43 yards against the Philadelphia Eagles broke a streak of four straight games with at least 100 receiving yards. NFL midseason All-Rookie Team: Arvell Reese, David Bailey pacing 2026 draft picks | The Athletic Linebacker. First team: Arvell Reese, New York Giants; Jacob Rodriguez, Miami Dolphins. Reese terrorized the Eagles this past Sunday, to the tune of 12 tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble on a sack that took just 2.29 seconds — the fastest sack in the NFL since Week 7 of last season, according to NextGenStats. Reese was my top-ranked player in the 2026 draft, and he hasn’t disappointed. His main appeal as a prospect was his versatility, which is also why he is one of the favorites for Defensive Rookie of the Year. He is the only NFL player (not just among rookies) with 65-plus tackles, eight-plus tackles for loss and at least one interception. Add in his forced fumble from Sunday and 4.5 sacks, and Reese has made an impact for the NFC East-leading Giants. Interior offensive line. First team: Vega Ioane, Baltimore Ravens; Austin Barber, Cleveland Browns; Francis Mauigoa, New York Giants. I had higher hopes for Mauigoa, a top-10 pick, but he has been good enough at right guard. Daniel Jeremiah on Arvell Reese "It's the stuff that he's doing against the run that's blowing me away." Arvell Reese is checking all the boxes EARLY in his NFL career #giants pic.twitter.com/GWeVbZx2j8 — Move The Sticks Podcast (@MTSPodOmaha) November 11, 2026 The gamble these Giants took in doing nothing at the trade deadline | New York Post Sure, there was a sense of letdown as the NFL trade deadline came and went Tuesday and the Giants did not exactly jump into the deep end of the pool. The lack of action was not for a lack of trying. The Giants engaged in “a lot of conversations,” according to a source, but were wary about overpaying for players and eventually stood pat. Questions on 2026 NFL trade deadline deals: Does Kirk Cousins lift the Vikings? | ESPN.com Which teams will look back and regret not doing more? I wonder how much the Ravens and Chargers mostly deciding to hold onto their veterans mattered here, given that Harbaugh has shown an affinity for adding players from those organizations (and front offices) he knows best since joining the Giants. It’s also true that New York will get Cam Skattebo back from his hamstring injury sooner than later, but the Giants are relying heavily on a player who was a healthy scratch for them earlier in the year in Devin Singletary. They’re one injury away from Greg Desrosiers Jr. stepping in as their primary running back. Like the Rams, the Giants are probably going to look toward veteran free agency as a place to add depth. It wouldn’t be a shock to see them bring in someone like Taven Bryan for a tryout at defensive tackle. Backs like Antonio Gibson and D’Ernest Johnson are still available in free agency. Given that they’re in position to win the NFC East for the first time since 2011, though, I’m a little surprised that the Giants didn’t make at least one move for a rotational player on offense or defense. Report: Giants called Falcons about a potential Bijan Robinson trade | Pro Football Talk The Giants didn’t make any big deals at the trade deadline, but they tried to make a very big one. The Giants called the Falcons to see whether running back Bijan Robinson was available in a trade, according to Jordan Raanan of ESPN. That would have been a blockbuster, but it’s unsurprising that the teams didn’t make a deal. The Falcons made a big investment in Robinson this offseason, signing him to a three-year, $66.8 million contract extension, and from all accounts they view him as one of the most important pieces of their franchise.
