title: 2026 NFL midseason report: Questions, stats for all 32 teams entering second half
summary: The 2026 NFL season has hit the midway point. Here's what to watch in the second half, key QB stats and fantasy nuggets for all 32 teams.
full_text:
Nine weeks of the 2026 NFL season have passed. Some teams are riding high, while others are grasping for wins.

 Much of what we believed we knew when it all began in September has been validated -- but lots of surprises, blockbuster trades and injuries have changed the course of our early-season predictions. 

 AFC South-leading Jacksonville went all-in on the defensive side with a trio of trades before the deadline this week, while John Harbaugh has the NFC East-leading New York Giants believing they hired the right man. No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza has yet to take the reins in Las Vegas but will this week after another big trade ; there's not a single rookie who has stood out enough so far to say that the race for ROY isn't wide open. The NFC North remains the strongest division halfway through the season, while both Super Bowl participants have looked shaky of late. Of note, neither Seattle (11) nor New England (16) was ranked in the FPI top 10 at this point last season.

 With that in mind, ESPN's 32 NFL team reporters took part in a midseason reset. Here, they lay out what they've learned through the first nine games and frame what's to come over the final nine weeks and beyond. Teams are ranked below by where each stands in ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI) rankings, and each club's current odds to win the division are also included as well as Eric Moody's non-QB fantasy football nuggets.

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 

 

 

 
 
 San Francisco 49ers 
 FPI rank:  1 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  99.3% 
 Chances to win their division:  94.6%

 First-half storyline: The 49ers have jumped to a 7-1 start despite more injuries to key players, including to DE Nick Bosa (calf) and WR Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis). But the Niners have again overcome those issues to find themselves in the driver's seat for the NFC's No. 1 seed with wins against three of the last four teams in the 2025 playoffs.

 
 QB stat to know: Brock Purdy leads the NFL with a QBR of 82.5 and is firmly in the mix for the NFL's Most Valuable Player award. Perhaps more important given the other injury issues is that Purdy has started and finished all eight games, providing stability at the game's most important position.

 

 
 Second-half storyline: Despite the hot start, the 49ers believe they can be better. Some of that will depend on health, but San Francisco has five starters in their first or second seasons -- and even more youngsters in key roles. If those players continue to develop, it could push the Niners to another level. -- Nick Wagoner 

 Fantasy nugget: Brock Purdy started the season averaging 27.0 fantasy PPG in the first three games. Since then, he has scored 18.1 fantasy PPG and has topped 20 points just once. He has the fourth-toughest remaining QB schedule, with games against the Vikings, Seahawks, Rams and Chiefs still on tap. It may be worth putting him on the trade block this week. -- Moody 

 

 

 
 Buffalo Bills 
 FPI rank: 2 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  99.8% 
 Chances to win their division:  96.3%

 First-half storyline: Historic offense, problematic defense: The Josh Allen -Joe Brady partnership is a huge argument for continuity, with the Bills scoring at rates comparable to those of the best offenses in NFL history. But coordinator Jim Leonhard's defense, especially the secondary, is leaky and still figuring out communication issues far too late in the season.

 
 QB stat to know: Allen has maintained a league-leading and career-best yards per attempt average (8.6) despite an injury that kept his best deep threat (WR DJ Moore ) out of the lineup for the better part of four games. Even if it's not Brady's primary emphasis, the 2026 Bills are more explosive than they were even in Allen's best years.

 
 Second-half storyline: The Thanksgiving to Christmas gauntlet: From Thanksgiving Day through Christmas Day, the Bills will play five consecutive games against contenders: Kansas City, at New England, at Green Bay, Chicago, at Denver. It's the toughest stretch of the season at the most important point of the season, and should decide whether the Bills hold on as AFC Super Bowl favorites. -- Nick Suss 

 Fantasy nugget: DJ Moore has a 26% target share, 41% air yard share and 14.3 fantasy PPG in his four full games. That is high-end WR2 production, but he will be tested to maintain it, as he has the toughest remaining fantasy schedule for WRs. -- Moody 

 

 

 
 Cincinnati Bengals 
 FPI rank:  3 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  98.6% 
 Chances to win their division:  79.5%

 First-half storyline: Joe Burrow has officially found his groove, and the offense has never been better. The Bengals are third in points per drive (2.82), first in third-down conversion percentage (53.6%) and in fewest number of drives without a first down (18.3%). The engine that is built to lead the team is doing exactly that.

 
 QB stat to know: Burrow has been otherworldly at stretching the field vertically, which is as much a credit to Burrow as it is to his star receivers -- Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . On throws of 15 air yards or more, Burrow has a 99.3 QBR and a whopping 18.1% completion percentage over expectation, per ESPN Research.

 
 Second-half storyline: Can the offense continue its torrid pace? The offense has masked the defensive inconsistencies that have popped up in various moments. Third downs and allowing big rushing plays have been issues. But if the Bengals can keep forcing turnovers and keep their defensive red zone efficiency high (currently fifth), that might be enough. -- Ben Baby 

 Fantasy nugget: The Bengals have arguably the best passing attack in the NFL at the moment. Joe Burrow is the fantasy QB2, while Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase are both top-five WRs. That will be tested as the Bengals have the seventh-toughest remaining fantasy schedule for QBs and third-toughest for WRs. Meanwhile, struggling Chase Brown has the third- best fantasy RB schedule. -- Moody 

 

 
 Jacksonville Jaguars 
 FPI rank:  4 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  98.8% 
 Chances to win their division:  93.4%

 First-half storyline: The Jaguars are beating teams at a historic pace. They have four victories by 23 or more points, which is the most in a single season in franchise history. They're also the fifth team since 1999 with four victories by 23 or more points in the first eight games of the season -- three of the previous four teams that did that reached the Super Bowl, per ESPN Research.

 
 QB stat to know: Trevor Lawrence has the NFL's lowest off-target percentage at 9.2%, which is by far the best percentage of his career (15% in 2025 was his previous best). Coach Liam Coen has praised Lawrence's footwork, which was the first thing he worked to fix in the spring before his first season as coach in Jacksonville in 2025, as a reason for his improved accuracy.

 
 Second-half storyline: The Jaguars must keep the pass rush from being a liability. They are seventh in pressure rate but have only 16 sacks -- just four ahead of last-place Miami. Edge rushers Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker only have a combined five sacks. That's not going to be good enough against Caleb Williams , Aaron Rodgers , C.J. Stroud and Dak Prescott , who are all left on their schedule. -- Mike DiRocco 

 

 Fantasy nugget: Bhayshul Tuten is 15th among RBs in fantasy PPG and is third in the NFL in forced missed tackles rate. Tuten leads the Jags in goal-line carries and has scored three of their four goal-line TDs. In fact, he and Kenneth Walker III are the only RBs in the NFL with at least three rushing and receiving touchdowns this season.  -- Moody 

 

 

 
 Denver Broncos 
 FPI rank:  5 
 Chances to make the playoffs:  96.6% 
 Chances to win their division:  57.0%

 First-half storyline: Despite some…

title: NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Kirk Cousins, Josh Downs, Ryan Neuzil
summary: Was getting Kirk Cousins a home run for the Vikings? Did the Chiefs make a smart move to pick up Josh Downs?
full_text:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals from the 2026 trade deadline , which passed Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.

 When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

 Here are our evaluations for all 17 deals, including three Jaguars trades from Monday, three quarterback moves for teams in need and multiple deals involving at least one first-round pick.

 Editor's note: The Broncos-Chargers trade for linebacker Daiyan Henley was rescinded early Thursday , so the grade for that trade has been removed. 

 

 
 Jump to a trade: 
 Neuzil/Vorhees |  Downs | Hooker 
 Cousins  |  Allen  |  Davis 
 Godchaux  |  Cisco  |  Bates  |  Brissett 
 Simmons  |  Buckner  |  Nelson  |  Harrison 
 Jurgens  |  Porter | McCarthy 

 
 

 

 Falcons trade C Neuzil to Ravens for G Vorhees 
 Ravens get: C Ryan Neuzil 
 Falcons get: G Andrew Vorhees , 2028 sixth-round pick

 Falcons grade: C- 
 Ravens grade: B+

 The Ravens traded for their second center of this deadline season, with Neuzil heading to Baltimore for Vorhees and a late-round pick. It is a surprising and, at first glance, somewhat confusing deal.

 Neuzil is a solid center who ranks in the 57th and 50th percentile in pass block win rate and run block win rate at the position, respectively. He is in the last year of his contract.

 It's a little hard to know each team's plan. Cam Jurgens has been struggling since the Ravens acquired him a little over a month ago. Is Neuzil coming in to start over him? Is one of them moving to guard? Or is this just a pure value play?

 The Falcons have so much cap space in 2027 that they are likely to be very active in free agency and therefore unlikely to receive compensatory picks for players lost. Did the Falcons know they weren't going to bring back Neuzil and dealt him to avoid losing him for nothing? That's possible, though I would have thought they would have managed more of a return. But maybe that's what attracted the Ravens -- they saw this as a value play that could net them a profit in terms of compensatory picks with upside that Neuzil could help them now and in the future.

 I don't mind that for Baltimore, especially since the Jurgens deal already is looking like a mistake. But it's a tougher sell for the Falcons. I would much rather try to re-sign Neuzil to a long-term deal (perhaps they did). If they were going to trade Neuzil, was this really the best they could get? And though the Falcons are hardly contenders, this certainly won't help quarterback Michael Penix Jr . down the stretch.

 

 Backup Corey Levin will presumably start going forward. Vorhees figures to be a depth guard for the Falcons as he was for the Ravens. -- Walder 

 

 

 Colts trade WR Downs to Chiefs 
 Chiefs get: WR Josh Downs , 2027 seventh-round pick 
 Colts get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick

 Chiefs grade: B+ 
 Colts grade: B+

 Downs is free! The slot receiver is out of Indianapolis and now has a chance to be a major part of the Chiefs' offense down the stretch and, perhaps, during a playoff run.

 Downs has earned 354 receiving yards on 33 receptions this season (1.2 yards per route run) but has recorded 1.7 yards per route run over the course of his career. But as any fantasy football die-hard will tell you, Downs has much more potential than that.

 

 Over his four seasons, Downs has a 68 open score in ESPN's receiver scores , which evaluate a receiver's ability to get open on all routes -- not only the ones when he is targeted. And that 68 score means Downs is well above average. Though this has hardly been a guarantee for past Chiefs receivers, it is possible that playing with Patrick Mahomes will unlock a higher level of production from Downs.

 Kansas City is back to being a contender -- the Chiefs entered Tuesday with a 96% chance to reach the playoffs and a 7% chance to win the Super Bowl -- but their offense hasn't felt as if it has reached its maximum potential. The Chiefs rank only eighth in EPA per dropback but have been able to outperform that because of the rushing success of  Kenneth Walker III .

 Rashee Rice (35%) and Xavier Worthy (20%) spend time in the slot, but I expect those numbers will drop with Downs, who aligned in the slot 51% of the time in Indianapolis this season, now on the team. Over his career, Rice's numbers have been slightly worse in the slot (2.3 yards per route run) compared with when he's lined up outside or elsewhere (2.8).

 The cost here is similar to what the Seahawks gave up last year for Rashid Shaheed who, like Downs, was in a contract year. Perhaps the Chiefs will re-sign Downs as the Seahawks did with Shaheed but if not, they should be in line for a likely compensatory pick given that Kansas City does not have much cap room for in 2027. Given the Chiefs' need to augment the offense and status as a true contender, I think this is a worthwhile addition.

 

 As for the Colts, while I wouldn't have been opposed to them signing Downs to a long-term deal given his age (25) and talent, dealing him is quite logical. They are in the midst of a teardown, and if Downs left via free agency, they would not recoup this much value in a compensatory pick -- if they even got one. -- Walder 

 

 

 Titans trade S Hooker to Bills 
 Bills get: S Amani Hooker , 2027 fifth-round pick 
 Titans get: 2027 second-round pick

 Bills grade: C+ 
 Titans grade: A-

 As the Bills push for a title run, safety was an obvious place for an upgrade. I thought the answer might be Jessie Bates III , but the Jaguars -- arguably Buffalo's biggest threat in the AFC -- traded for the former Falcons safety  Monday.

 After the team released C.J. Gardner-Johnson last week, Damar Hamlin was left playing next to Cole Bishop , with Geno Stone as the third safety. In Hooker, the Titans upgrade from Hamlin and pick up a player who has been having an impactful season in Tennessee.

 

 Hooker has recorded five interceptions and six passes defensed this season with the Titans, good enough to have the sixth-best EPA allowed on targets among safeties. All current metrics on safeties are quite noisy, but some of the others are not as strong: 1.0 yards per coverage snap this season and last, and positive EPA allowed in 2025.

 The Bills will be getting him on a value contract, as they will be on the hook for the rest of Hooker's roughly $8.9 million in salary and per game roster bonuses this year, and then will be slated to pay him a non-guaranteed $10.3 million in 2027 and $13.5 million in 2028, per OverTheCap.com . That's less than Hooker would make on the open market, I believe, though not free.

 

 So Hooker is an upgrade at a position of need for a Super Bowl-contending team and will save them a few million dollars per year relative to the market. But is that worth a second-round pick? It strikes me as rich. Hooker is a good player but not a star -- he has never been a Pro Bowl selection or All-Pro and only snuck into Jeremy Fowler's NFL evaluator survey of top safeties in the "also receiving votes" category. As a result, the compensation here is a bit steep. -- Walder 

 

 

 Raiders trade QB Cousins to Vikings 
 Vikings get: QB Kirk Cousins 
 Raiders get: 2027 third-round pick

 Vikings grade: A 
 Raiders grade: B+

 The Vikings were in the unusual position of being Super Bowl contenders who desperately needed a quarterback. And Tuesday was essentially the last day they could get one.

 Kyler Murray is hurt and clearly not a fit in Kevin O'Connell's offense. Murray has struggled this season and currently ranks 27th in QBR…

title: NFL Week 10 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips, post-trade deadline news
summary: No deals for Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones or Brian Thomas Jr.? Vikings seeking QB answers with their Kirk Cousins trade? Here's the latest intel.
full_text:
It's Week 10 of the  2026 NFL season , and the trade deadline is officially behind us. As the dust settles on all the moves, insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 For the past month, there has been plenty of trade speculation on Jonathan Taylor , Daniel Jones and Brian Thomas Jr ., among others. But none of those players ended up switching teams. Was there ever any momentum? Why did those three big names stay put? One player who did get traded was Kirk Cousins , and there were plenty of dominoes to fall there. What now for the Raiders, who will turn to Fernando Mendoza ? And does this deal fix the Vikings' offense amid their push to the top of the NFC North?

 Jeremy and Dan share what they're hearing, answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 10.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 No Taylor, Jones or BTJ deals? 
 Cousins trade fallout for both teams? 
 Fantasy advice  | More notes, intel 

 
 

 Jonathan Taylor , Daniel Jones and Brian Thomas Jr . were arguably the buzziest names before the deadline but didn't move. Why not? 
 Graziano: In Taylor's case, it's because the "buzz" never lined up with the Colts' desire to trade him . Remember, Quenton Nelson , DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen were all in the final year of their contracts. Taylor is not. He's 27 years old and signed for two more years. They didn't have to trade him. He can be part of the solution next year and beyond. So they held firm on their price, asking for a first-round pick or some package of picks that would be reasonably equivalent to that. And no team emerged that was willing to give them that.

 The important thing to remember about Taylor is that the Colts never had an interest in moving on from him to just clear salary or be rid of the player. They like him. He's the only one of their prominent veterans who were extension-eligible last summer and actually got an extension. ( Alec Pierce and Jones were free agents, remember.) So while there were talks, I don't get the sense the Colts were ever eager or close to trading Taylor.

 

 Fowler: The buzz around Taylor persisted because of interest from other teams, the franchise's teardown tone set by the Nelson/Buckner trades and the sheer mileage on the player (1,712 carries). But he's a boon for any Indy coaching staff in 2027. He's also the team's best player. While Josh Downs clearly wanted out , Taylor wasn't as dug in (though I'm sure he would have welcomed the chance to play for a contender). My sense in talking to teams is that Indy wanted at least a first-round equivalent in any package, and interested teams couldn't get there. I believe Denver gave it a run this week but wasn't comfortable with the return Indianapolis was seeking.

 As for Jones, he was likely Minnesota's backup option to Cousins. It's worth noting that the Colts' coaching staff just doesn't seem eager to play Anthony Richardson Sr . and is much more comfortable with Jones despite his struggles. So I believe that's a factor in all of this.

 Graziano: Jones, who turns 30 next May, will be a decision for the incoming GM and (possibly) next head coach to make in the offseason. He's scheduled to earn $38 million in 2027. None of that is guaranteed at the moment -- $10.51 million of it becomes fully guaranteed if he's still on the roster on the fifth day of the 2027 league year. If Jones finishes the season playing well, and the team can legitimately talk itself into the idea that he'll be better next year further removed from his Achilles injury , that price could make him an attractive option. If not, Indianapolis can cut him without too much pain. It would take on $35.2 million in dead money cap charges in 2027, but that's not as intimidating a number as it used to be.

 Fowler:  Thomas, meanwhile, garnered significant interest, but in the end the Jaguars, a true contender, didn't want to subtract . They only wanted to add. And they value Thomas, though his numbers don't reflect that. He has speed that demands defensive attention.

 Graziano: Thomas doesn't appear to be an important player for the Jaguars anymore when you check the box score, but look around the league. The Rams are almost out of receivers . The 49ers have been scrambling to fill those spots all season. Injuries happen, and if something should happen to Jakobi Meyers or Parker Washington , the Jaguars believe Thomas could help them if he suddenly got thrust into a higher-volume role. The Jaguars are very clearly thinking about getting the top seed in the AFC and winning the Super Bowl. Maintaining quality depth at premium positions is important.

 

 Fowler: What's tough about Thomas' situation is he has only one reception in the past four games, and my sense is the player would have welcomed a fresh start had a trade happened. But that's a lot of talent on which to give up. Thomas was, quite easily, the most gifted athlete on the field when I visited Jaguars training camp. So while Taylor staying in Indy was a matter of the Colts' high demands, I don't think that was the case with Thomas. The Jaguars could have gotten a quality pick for him. They just didn't seem interested in moving him, even though he could have helped recoup some of the lost capital from Monday's flurry of trades .

 But Jacksonville should probably try to find a way to get Thomas involved more. It will need him in January.

 

 
 What now for the Vikings and Raiders after Kirk Cousins was traded to Minnesota? 
 Fowler: Cousins is comfort food for Minnesota. He's predictable. And more importantly, he's predictable in Kevin O'Connell's offense. He removes at least some unknown variables that could derail a promising season. Kyler Murray hadn't proved to be a fit in this specific scheme (which could have been detected back in, say, March ), and Carson Wentz was just bad. In fact, had Wentz simply played passable football Monday night , I'm not so sure Minnesota would have stretched draft capital to get quarterback help. Murray would have been back from injury eventually and perhaps Minnesota could have adjusted to his skill set.

 But Monday night was dire, so it's time to salvage the season with a quarterback who knows the system and played well in Las Vegas. Cousins is essentially a half-season option with a chance to re-sign. His $10 million roster bonus in 2027 is guaranteed. He has a two-year, $80 million extension that kicks in on the fifth day of the new league year, effectively serving as a poison pill. The Vikings most likely won't pay that, but they can either pay him $10 million to walk away or repackage it in a new deal.

 What the Vikings do at backup quarterback will be fascinating. Either Murray or Wentz can serve as QB2. There's also the option to release one or place one on injured reserve. (Murray already has an injury, and Wentz appeared to hurt his throwing hand Monday night.) Either way, QB1 is solidified, at least for a half-season. And Minnesota didn't have to give up a pick in the top two rounds to make it happen.

 Graziano: I agree with you and honestly don't believe that the Vikings wanted to trade for a quarterback. They believed Murray would play better than he did in Week 8 in Detroit and obviously didn't know he'd get injured in that game. And Wentz played considerably worse Monday than anyone in the Vikings' building thought he would. So they spent the early hours of Tuesday morning examining the landscape and what was possible, looking at options that included Cousins, Daniel Jones and Geno Smith .

 From what I have been told, the Raiders weren't looking to trade Cousins, who has played well for them and allowed them to hold off on playing  Fernando Mendoza  as long as possible. The Vikings had checked in on Cousins last week to get a sense of what it might cost if they decided to go down that road, but they didn't get the sense that Cousins…

title: NFL survivor power rankings: Why this is the week to use the Rams or the Bills
summary: ESPN NFL survivor pool strategy, predictions and ranking the top seven options for Week 10.
full_text:
Week 9 was the quietest week of the Survivor season after eight weeks of mostly chaos. For the first time in two years, only one underdog won outright, the Green Bay Packers upsetting the New England Patriots on the road. Over 97% of entries advanced last week, by far the most this season.

 Still, only 1.9% of ESPN Survivor entries from the start of the season remain alive as we are officially past the halfway mark of the season.

 Week 10 is a particularly interesting week, as each of the five biggest moneyline favorites all play on the road. Three are favored by more than a touchdown, including the Buffalo Bills , who are currently the heavy chalk at 40% selected. 

 Despite being one of the Super Bowl favorites, the Bills are still 68% available in ESPN Survivor. At this stage of the season, check your individual groups, as that number will vary widely, but the Bills have not had many obvious spots to use them until now.

 The Jacksonville Jaguars are the biggest favorites of the week, but they are just 38% available on ESPN and even lower in some other major contests (37% on Splash, 25% on Circa). But just like we said last week, there will still be plenty more spots to use Jacksonville, including each of the next two weeks (at New York Giants , vs. Tennessee Titans ).

 While the Bills and Jaguars are the two elite teams on the menu this week, there are a lot of other intriguing options if you can stomach them. Despite losing Puka Nacua , the Los Angeles Rams are now up to 9.5-point favorites on the road against the Arizona Cardinals , who will be starting rookie Carson Beck with a receiving corps that already dealt Marvin Harrison Jr . and lost both Kendrick Bourne and Michael Wilson for the season. Of course, the Cardinals upset the Rams as 13.5-point underdogs in Week 6, which knocked out 35% of the field at the time.

 The Seattle Seahawks are up to 6.5-point favorites on the road against the Las Vegas Raiders . That line moved 3.5 points after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins , though the Seahawks are expected to start Drew Lock for a second straight week. The Houston Texans are going to come in very low-selected on the road against the Cleveland Browns , but if you still have them available, there are plenty of better spots, so while they are a fine pick, I lean towards saving them.

 

 If your goal is to try to get different, the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers are both on the road, putting their opponents in play. Jacoby Brissett and the Baltimore Ravens host the winless Chargers, while the lowly Indianapolis Colts host the Dolphins. There are enough strong options where the risk probably isn't worth it at this point, but it will put you in strong position if you can get by with either one.

 Based on the current ESPN selections, the Rams are the obvious choice. They are bigger favorites than the Bills with less future value at a fraction of the ownership. However, in sharp contests, I expect their selection percentages to flip with the Rams being the heavy chalk. In that case, I would prefer the Bills.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Future value based on Mike Clay's cheat sheet .  

 1. Los Angeles Rams (at Arizona Cardinals ) 
 

 Out of the three biggest favorites this week, the Rams have the least future value. So at 13% ownership on ESPN as of Wednesday morning, they would be a slam dunk pick. They host the Dallas Cowboys in Week 15, and they visit the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 17, but their other games are against the Green Bay Packers , Kansas City Chiefs , San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks (twice). Yes, it's scary to take the Rams without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , but the Cardinals are even more banged up and nowhere near the team that upset the Rams in Week 6.

 
 Chance to win: 87% (ESPN Analytics), 96% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Rams -9.5 (-425 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Cowboys (Week 15) 
 Availability: 63% 
 ESPN Selection: 13% 
 
 2. Buffalo Bills (at New York Jets ) 
 

 At 40% picked, it is hard not to justify saving the Bills. Next week, the Bills are 16.5-point favorites over the Dolphins on the lookahead line, the largest point spread all season. However, there are several other strong choices next week, and taking the Bills now allows you to get off that chalk next week. The Bills would be my top pick in most sharp contests for that reason, but if you want to save them and take them next week, it's hard to blame you.

 
 Chance to win: 83% (ESPN Analytics), 90% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Bills -8.5 (-485 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Dolphins (Week 11), at Dolphins (Week 17), vs. Jets (Week 18) 
 Availability: 68% 
 ESPN Selection: 40% 
 

 3. Seattle Seahawks (at Las Vegas Raiders ) 

 Last week, the Seahawks were very similar to the Rams as a big favorite with low ESPN selection that I expected to rise in sharper contests. However, once Sam Darnold was ruled out, the line moved against Seattle, keeping their selection relatively low. Surprisingly, the Seahawks are still 68% available on ESPN, so at 7% picked, they are a strong choice right now. They have some future value, but with over 50% of the field likely to still have them, this is a chance to get them as a reasonable favorite before the other players consolidate on them later.

 
 Chance to win: 74% (ESPN Analytics), 72% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Seahawks -6.5 (-285 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Giants (Week 14), at Eagles (Week 15) 
 Availability: 68% 
 ESPN Selection: 7% 
 

 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (at Tennessee Titans ) 

 

 The Jaguars are the biggest favorites on the board this week, so 19% selection isn't too bad. However, they are available to only 38% of entries, meaning half of them are using them this week. With an elite remaining schedule (five games with at least 70% win probability according to Mike Clay and ESPN Analytics' models) they will continue to be a better play each week as long as Trevor Lawrence remains healthy. Still, it's hard to dock them too much as the only double-digit favorites in Week 10. They would rank higher on this list in groups with very few people remaining, but if you are chasing the grand prize trying to last all 18 weeks, I would keep saving them.

 
 Chance to win: 84% (ESPN Analytics), 96% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Jaguars -10.5 (-600 moneyline) 
 Notable games: at Giants (Week 11), vs. Titans (Week 12), vs. Steelers (Week 14), vs. Commanders (Week 17), at Colts (Week 18) 
 Availability: 38% 
 ESPN Selection: 19% 
 

 5. Baltimore Ravens (vs Los Angeles Chargers ) 

 To me, taking the Ravens this week comes down to whether or not you think Lamar Jackson returns. If Jackson comes back, Week 14 (vs. Buccaneers), Week 16 (vs. Cleveland Browns ) and Week 18 (vs. Pittsburgh Steelers ) are all potential weeks to use the Ravens. If not, then the Ravens become a viable pick as a 4.5-point favorite with very little future value.

 
 Chance to win: 46% (ESPN Analytics), 70% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Ravens -4.5 (-218 moneyline) 
 Notable games: None 
 Availability: 50% 
 ESPN Selection: 3% 
 

 6. Houston Texans (at Cleveland Browns ) 

 

 Both ESPN Analytics and Mike Clay's models like the Texans more than the betting market this week. And similar to the Seahawks, the Texans are a reasonable favorite available to over two-thirds of entries at minimal ownership. However, Houston has many more usable spots than Seattle does, and most of those spots will have higher projected win probability. I lean towards saving them.

 
 Chance to win: 76% (ESPN Analytics), 67% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Texans -4.5 (-225 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Colts (Week 11), vs. Ravens (Week 12), at Eagles (Week 16), vs. Titans (Week 18) 
 Availability: 69% 
 ESPN Selection: 2%

 A 2-7 team as a 3.5-point favorite tells you what the market thinks of Kyle McCord and the Dolphins. The Colts have an easy remaining schedule, but they are also a bad football team, so it…

title: 2026 NFL midseason award rankings: MVP picks, top rookies, OPOY, DPOY, coaches
summary: Joe Burrow for MVP? Arvell Reese as the DROY? Hardware for Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Will Anderson Jr.? We ranked the top contenders to win eight NFL awards through Week 9.
full_text:
It's midseason awards time. I'm here to hand out my ballot for the first half of the 2026 NFL season . And in a year that has felt dominated by parity and very few players or teams separating from the pack, it wasn't easy to pick favorites. There are multiple legitimate contenders to win every single award through nine weeks, running all the way from Most Valuable Player (where I counted six players who had a legitimate argument) to Comeback Player of the Year (where three future Hall of Famers came back from season-ending injuries and immediately looked like their old selves).

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 As always, these are my picks for who I feel should win each of these awards after the first half of the season as opposed to predictions for who the voters are likely to actually select by the end of the year. I place a priority on availability, so players who have sat out more than a game or so because of injury will find it difficult to compete with players who have answered the call each and every weekend. And naturally, I'm using healthy amounts of data and what I've seen watching All-22 film every week to inform my choices here.

 Let's begin with the rookies before wrapping with my MVP rankings and my midseason All-Pro team.

 

 
 Jump to an award: 
 DROY | OROY |  Coach of the Year 
 Comeback Player of the Year 
 Protector of the Year 
 DPOY | OPOY | MVP  | All-Pro roster 

 
 

 Defensive Rookie of the Year 
 My top pick five weeks ago : Arvell Reese 

 After the offense-heavy draft classes in 2024 and 2025, this has been a very fun crop of defensive rookies, driven by the players at the very top. There were no sure things, but we're seeing a lot of players who had questions about their fit in a defense or as every-down options thrive. The 49ers and Chiefs first-year defenders in particular have been exciting to watch, although Mansoor Delane 's shoulder injury has kept the top-drafted cornerback in the class from getting on the field often enough to compete for this award, while defensive tackle  Gracen Halton sustained a season-ending broken ankle for the 49ers.

 I was left with five contenders for three spots. Jacob Rodriguez has been ever present at linebacker for the Dolphins and has been a very good run defender while wearing the green dot for Miami as a rookie. The Bengals were able to isolate Rodriguez in coverage for a couple of touchdowns earlier this season , but he has generally had the athleticism to compete there against running backs and tight ends.

 

 And though  Brandon Cisse 's season got off to a tough start against Justin Jefferson , the Packers cornerback has improved. He has been surprisingly impactful along the line of scrimmage, creating problems as a blitzer and making quick reads and sure tackles on screens. He has been one of the biggest reasons why the Packers -- whose outside cornerbacks struggled last season -- have been able to withstand the absence of Micah Parsons .

 

 3. Sonny Styles , LB, Washington Commanders 
 Of course, I have to start any conversation about Styles by mentioning what might have been one of the single most impressive highlights I saw from any player in the first half of the season -- when he  obliterated   Saquon Barkley in pass protection. It hasn't been an isolated moment for the Commanders linebacker, either, as we're repeatedly seeing his physicality and athleticism impact blockers and draw eyes in pass protection.

 He has also been a quick study in coverage over the middle of the field, showing a real comfort with understanding route distributions and passing receivers off to avoid creating the voids that offenses try to exploit. It has been a frustrating season for the Commanders, but Styles looks as if he's going to be an essential part of the defense moving forward.

 

 2. David Bailey , Edge, New York Jets 
 Bailey is long and athletic, and we saw those traits last week , when it very briefly appeared that he had injured Patrick Mahomes . Bailey terrorized Chiefs tackle Jaylon Moore for two strip sacks in a four-play span, and he's tied with Fred Warner for a league-leading five strip sacks so far this season.

 Bailey has 7.5 sacks overall, 12 quarterback hits and 10 tackles for loss. Some of those numbers are a little inflated; Bailey got his first career sack in the opener against the Titans on a play on which he didn't touch Cam Ward as the quarterback ran out of bounds, then another as Jordan Love slid in front of the rookie edge rusher. But don't let that mask his impact on a down-by-down basis. Bailey is second among all players with a 20.6% pressure rate and 20th in quick pressure rate at 5.7%. Teams haven't doubled Bailey very often, but that's going to change in the second half. He's already one of the league's most unstoppable pass rushers.

 

 1. Arvell Reese , LB/Edge, New York Giants 
 Picking between Bailey and Reese is unfair. I leaned Reese if only because he has been two impactful players in one this season. As an off-ball linebacker, Reese has been all over the place for a Giants team that has been better against the run this season, even after trading  Dexter Lawrence II . Reese has made tackles on 15.3% of his snaps, the eighth-highest rate in the league. He has given up an  81.3 passer rating in coverage , a very credible number for a veteran linebacker, let alone a rookie just getting his feet wet at this level.

 And then there's Reese's side quest as a devastating force on blitzes. Despite rushing the quarterback only about 11 times per game, Reese already has 4.5 sacks and 14 pressures. His 10.2% quick pressure rate would be the second-best mark in the NFL if he qualified. And the average Reese pressure comes after 2.44 seconds, the fifth fastest among players with 10 pressures or more.

 

 The Giants are already building pass-rush packages around Reese, like when they isolated him  against Eagles guard  Landon Dickerson last week , with one of the league's highest-paid interior linemen struggling to even slow down Reese on one of his three sacks. Philly decided to leave Reese completely unblocked for another. Reese was also the best player on the field earlier this season in a  win over the Cardinals , making the difference in swinging a close game New York's way.

 Reese vs. Bailey is going to be a conversation in bars around New York and New Jersey for a long time.

 

 

 Offensive Rookie of the Year 
 My top pick five weeks ago : Denzel Boston 

 All you need to know about the offensive side, meanwhile, is that Fernando Mendoza instantly became the betting favorite to take home this hardware after the Kirk Cousins trade Tuesday afternoon. There are plenty of rookies who have flashed with a nice week or two, but very few have sustained a significant level of play over the first half. As a result, my feelings here head in a somewhat surprising direction at the top.

 

 3. Carnell Tate , WR, Tennessee Titans 
 Sitting out last week's game against the Bengals (and the high-scoring 43-36 result that ensued) probably hurt Tate's chances of climbing to the top of the award ballot at midseason, but after a slow start, the Ohio State product is settling in as the focal point of the Titans' passing game. He leads all rookies in averaging 2.2 yards per route run, which is right in line what Justin Jefferson (2.2) and Tetairoa McMillan (2.1) are averaging this season. And though Tate has only one touchdown, Cam Ward has missed him at least two other scores.

 

 2. Denzel Boston , WR, Cleveland Browns 
 Boston leads all rookies with 507 receiving yards, which owes in part to the fact that he has run 301 routes, the seventh most of any player in the NFL. Boston has been the big-play provider for the Browns, with his three catches of 50 or more yards tied with Christian Watson of the Packers for the most in the league. His 55-yard touchdown against the Bucs was the best of the bunch, with Boston breaking three tackles in two…

title: Questions on 2026 NFL trade deadline deals: Does Kirk Cousins lift the Vikings?
summary: Let's make sense of Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, Josh Downs to the Chiefs, the Jaguars getting aggressive, a wild Bengals comp-pick mixup and four teams' deadline silence.
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone. For all the big names rumored to be in the mix Tuesday afternoon, the most significant trade of the day involved Titans safety Amani Hooker , who was dealt to the Bills with a fifth-round pick for a second-round selection. The Vikings reunited with quarterback  Kirk Cousins for a third-round selection, but the biggest moves ended up taking place Monday, when the Jaguars sent out a first-round pick and two second-round selections to land Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III .

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 What we saw over the past 24 hours left me with more questions than answers. So, I set out to try to answer those questions.

 I'll get to the Cousins deal, a trade that was ruined by the internet and the teams that missed an opportunity to make a deal, but I have to start this in Florida, where a Jags regime that has been very happy to bet on themselves doubled down.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Did the Jaguars give up too much? 
 Can Cousins elevate the Vikings enough? 
 What happened with the Bengals? 
 What does Downs mean for the Chiefs? 
 Why weren't there more trades? 
 Which teams missed out? 

 
 

 

 Did the Jaguars give up too much to address two injuries on their roster? 
 The most fascinating team at the deadline did its work Monday with a series of stunning trades. The impetus for those moves, seemingly, goes back to a pair of relatively under-the-radar injuries  in the Week 8 win over the Colts . During that game, defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton tore his quadriceps muscle, and safety Eric Murray injured his elbow. Both are expected to sit out the rest of the season.

 Hamilton and Murray aren't bad players -- Hamilton was having his best season as a pro -- but they're not the sort of load-bearing, cornerstone contributors who would lead a front office to panic that the defense will collapse without them. It was surprising, then, that the Jaguars decided to fill those holes by sacrificing a significant portion of their high-end draft capital over the next three years.

 

 First, general manager James Gladstone & Co. addressed safety by trading 2027 second- and 2028 fifth-round picks  to the Falcons for veteran  Jessie Bates III , whose contract expires at the end of the season. Trading a 2028 sixth-round pick to the Saints for Davon Godchaux seemed logical in terms of adding a rotational defensive tackle, but the Jaguars went over the top Monday evening, sending 2027 first- and 2029 second-round picks to the Eagles for defensive tackle  Jordan Davis . Suddenly, the Jags look as if they're all-in, and it's to fill holes that didn't really seem as if they were huge liabilities.

 Let's start by talking about the players. It's easy to understand why Jacksonville would be excited. Bates is a leader and a playmaker on the back end, where his instincts and experience help get him into throwing lanes and in position to break up passes. He hasn't missed a start since leaving for Atlanta in 2023, which helps mitigate some of the concerns about his advancing age (turns 30 in February).

 The league is generally very anxious about targeting safeties with significant contracts as they hit 30 given the ground they must cover while playing as a single-high or two-deep free safety. I'm not concerned about that with Bates at the moment. He has covered an average of 16.7 yards per play so far this season, per NFL Next Gen Stats, in line with what he did in 2023 (16.8), 2024 (17.0) and 2025 (16.7), when the Falcons aligned him near the line of scrimmage more often than they had in past years.

 I'm not sure there's evidence that his ability to reach top speeds has fallen dramatically. According to Next Gen Stats, he has topped 19 mph three times through nine weeks, which is in line with his averages through the first half of the season in each of the three previous years with the Falcons. One measure I use as an estimate is a player's average 90th percentile maximum speed, which tries to measure the speed each player is likely to get to on the vast majority of their snaps. Bates' 2026 figure there (15.6 mph) is higher than it was in any of his previous seasons with Atlanta.

 Godchaux is a reasonable nose tackle, but he now projects to be in a backup role behind Davis, who was added to be an essential player for the Jaguars up front. The Eagles moved up ahead of the Ravens in 2022 to take Davis with the 13th pick in the draft, forcing Baltimore to "settle" for safety  Kyle Hamilton with the 14th selection. The expectation was that Davis would have a floor as an excellent run stopper, while his high-end athleticism raised hopes that he would develop into a significant pass-rushing threat on the interior with more experience and NFL coaching.

 That hasn't really come together. Despite playing next to Fletcher Cox, Jalen Carter  and Milton Williams at different times during his run in Philadelphia, Davis hasn't been able to create steady pass pressure. Davis has 9.5 sacks and 15 knockdowns over 4½ years as a pro. And those really haven't typically been a direct product of Davis creating opportunities, such as last week's sack against the Giants , where Davis twisted with Carter and the latter came free, only for  J.J. McCarthy  to duck under Carter and into the arms of Davis.

 

 Since entering the starting lineup for good in 2023, Davis has generated pressures on 5.6% of his pass-rush snaps and 1.2% of his quick pressures. Among defensive tackles with 700 pass-rush opportunities or more over that time frame, Davis ranks 63rd out of 71 qualifiers in pressure rate and 60th in quick pressure rate. Godchaux, for what it's worth, ranks 71st in both categories.

 Davis is a good two-down nose tackle. I'm assuming the Jags think he still has another gear to hit. For one, they can follow in the footsteps of what the Eagles did when they got A.J. Brown and simply play him more often. Davis hasn't sat out a regular-season start since the start of 2023, but with the Eagles rotating Davis alongside Moro Ojomo , Williams and others over the years, he has played about only 48% of Philly's defensive snaps in that span, dropping just below 25% on third downs.

 Getting Davis on the field on third downs will simply get him in the lineup against pass plays more often, which would give him more opportunities to get after the quarterback. The Jaguars also might greenlight Davis to be more aggressive getting into the backfield with opportunities to one-gap as opposed to playing the gap-and-a-half style that DC Vic Fangio employs in Philly with his defensive tackles. I'd be surprised if Davis became a great pass rusher after not showing it for four-plus years, but I wouldn't be shocked if his pass-rush production improved with the move to Jacksonville.

 That's the good news. The prices the Jags paid to get those guys? That's the bad news. These were trades in which the guys on the other side of the phone had to ask twice to make sure that the rounds they were hearing were correct. The Eagles just signed Davis to a contract extension in March and paid him an $18.8 million bonus in the process; I suspect they asked  LeBron James  if they could borrow his helicopter to get Davis to the airport before the Jaguars changed their mind.

 Bates is a pure half-season player since his contract expires at the end of the season. The Jaguars could re-sign him, of course, but they could also have gone after him (or a replacement) in free agency next offseason, and signing him would be locking the team in for what are likely to be Bates' decline years. As my colleague Seth Walder noted , the Jags are far more likely to recoup a compensatory pick for Bates than the Falcons, but I'm at least a little skeptical that it'll be a significant selection. The last time a safety on the wrong side of 30 even qualified for anything higher than a sixth-round compensatory pick was 2019.

 Let's say Bates breaks that mold and lands the Jaguars a fifth-round…

title: Why protected picks aren't common in NFL trades
summary: It's common for NBA teams to protect picks they trade, but things are different in the NFL. Here's why.
full_text:
When the Indianapolis Colts traded a package that included two first-round picks to the New York Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner at last season's NFL trade deadline, they likely envisioned the 2027 selection would be one of modest value.

 Perhaps a mid-first-round choice. Or, with any luck, it would be a late-first-round selection if the Colts finished with a strong record in 2026.

 Now, with the 2-7 Colts on track to have one of the NFL's worst records, the Jets could be in line to receive one of the 2027 draft's top picks via the second of the two first-rounders they received from Indy.

 But what if the Colts could have made the deal with a caveat?

 After all, NBA teams do it routinely. They trade top picks with so-called protections, meaning the draft pick is not conveyed to the other team if it falls into a particular range, say, the top five or top 10.

 But in the NFL, it's practically unheard of. Why is that?

 The reasons, league officials said, are mostly related to the contrasting rules governing how many years in advance draft picks may be traded. Also at play are the differences in how draft picks are valued in football versus basketball.

 These kinds of provisions are not prohibited in the NFL. They're just rarely broached in trade discussions.

 But protected picks did come up recently in a very notable trade.

 Protected draft picks were discussed during trade talks between the Los Angeles Rams and Cleveland Browns in negotiations that produced this year's Myles Garrett trade, according to a league source. But, as is usually the case, the inclusion of protected picks did not come to fruition.

 This is usually the outcome when these conversations occur, sources said, because the mechanics are just too difficult to figure out. In the NBA, draft picks may be exchanged up to seven years into the future. But in the NFL, picks may be traded just three years down the line.

 "It's just really hard to pull off," one NFL executive said.

 

 In the NBA, protecting picks in trades can have massive impact. Take the 2020 trade that sent forward Al Horford and other assets from the Philadelphia 76ers to the Oklahoma City Thunder . Included in the deal was a first-round pick that was top-six protected in 2025.

 Midway through the 2024-25 season, it appeared as if the Thunder -- in a season when they won a championship -- would receive a likely lottery pick in the deal. But that was before the 76ers went 4-24 after the All-Star break, allowing them to wind up with the No. 3 pick, which they used on  VJ Edgecombe .

 He's now a full-time starter for Philadelphia and was averaging 13.2 points entering Tuesday night. Meanwhile, the Thunder ended up with the eventual 17th pick in the 2026 draft, which was traded away in a draft-night deal. The whole saga took six years to come to its conclusion.

 Further complicating the use of protected picks in the NFL is the difference in the value of draft selections. Applying NBA draft logic to the NFL draft just doesn't work, one league executive said. Even a late-first-round selection in the NFL is seen as quite valuable, whereas a late-first-round NBA selection is often a developmental player.

 "In the NBA, the top six picks are the first round, the next six picks are the second round and so forth," according to an NFL executive. "In the NFL, pick 20 is still pretty valuable, so the acquiring team isn't as mad about receiving it."

 One NFL executive added that NFL teams are more active in the trade market today. That means teams can usually find a trade partner without having to settle for a deal that includes protected picks.

 

 But that doesn't mean NFL teams don't use other creative provisions in trades. In fact, the Garrett trade is a prime example of a deal that includes some quirky language. Conditional trades have been used for years by NFL teams, and the Rams and Browns included a provision in their deal that reportedly states that the 2029 third-round choice owed by the Rams will become a first-round choice if the Rams trade Garrett to one of the Browns' AFC North foes.

 That sort of condition is hardly the first of its kind.

 In 2008, the deal that sent quarterback Brett Favre from the Green Bay Packers to the Jets included a condition that the Jets would owe the Packers three first-round picks if Favre were traded from New York to one of the Packers' NFC North rivals. Favre famously retired after one season in New York and was released from his contract by the Jets, allowing him to ultimately come out of retirement to join the Minnesota Vikings as a free agent.

 More conventional trade conditions are used all the time, such as those tied to a player's snap counts. The second-round choice the Colts traded to the Philadelphia Eagles for quarterback Carson Wentz in 2021 upgraded to a first-round selection because Wentz played at least 75% of the Colts' offensive snaps that season.

 But this time around, it's pretty clear cut for the Colts. They will be handing over their 2027 first-round choice to the Jets -- likely a much higher pick than they ever imagined.

title: Cowboys rave about Quinnen Williams a year after trade deadline deal
summary: Voted a captain by his teammates, Williams is making a difference in Dallas on and off the field.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- In his past few meetings with the media, Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams has come up with a couple of phrases for when he does not want to address a certain subject or does not know enough about one to comment.

 One common refrain has been: "I've got to think about that."

 Another has been: "I'm going to keep that to myself."

 Recently, he said he was not playing in a dominant manner, that he needed to fine-tune some things.

 

 "I know exactly how it's supposed to look, how it's supposed to feel when it gets there," Williams said. "Right now, I can just focus on getting better, the things I did wrong, the things I need to do better and keep going in the right direction. When that game comes, when that game hits, I can build off that with momentum."

 What exactly is missing?

 "I'm going to keep that to myself," he said.

 Whatever is missing might be the most minute details that only he and a limited number of players in his stratosphere can understand. Williams called his 2022 season with the New York Jets his standard: He had 12 sacks, 12 tackles for loss, 28 quarterback pressures, four pass breakups, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery.

 Through nine games this season, Williams leads the Cowboys in sacks (five), tackles for loss (14) and forced fumbles (two). He is second in quarterback hurries (29).

 "If there's a better interior defensive lineman than him in the league, I haven't been around one in a long time," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "He's just dominated the way he can change the game."

 

 He has recorded at least two tackles for loss in each of his past four games. Only linebacker  DeMarcus Ware (five) has a longer streak by a Cowboy since TFLs began being tracked in 1999. His 14 TFLs are the most by a Cowboys defensive tackle in the first nine games of a season. Only Ware had more (18 in 2011).

 He had three TFLs in last week's 27-23 win against the Indianapolis Colts . His biggest came on the Colts' second-to-last drive, when Indianapolis could have run down the clock to make the Cowboys' comeback more difficult, as he stopped  Jonathan Taylor for a 1-yard loss.

 Earlier in the fourth quarter, Williams stopped Taylor for a 2-yard loss and forced a fumble that linebacker Shemar James recovered.

 "I told him during the game, in the midst of the fire, 'I love playing by you,'" James said. "He's the guy that makes plays. He's the guy that's vocal, that runs his room, controls his room. And ultimately he's just a great leader and a great player."

 It has been a little more than a calendar year since the Cowboys acquired Williams from the Jets for a 2026 second-round pick and 2027 first-rounder. In 16 games with Dallas, he has been credited with 56 tackles, 6.5 sacks, 62 quarterback hurries, two forced fumbles, two pass breakups and an interception.

 

 "I think he's fully within that flow really since Week 3," defensive coordinator Christian Parker said recently. "And he wasn't playing bad the first two weeks, just wasn't the dynamic impact that we all know he's capable of.

 "I think that he's just been comfortable with himself, No. 1, and comfortable with the people around him. And he knows just to cut it loose and go play and we'll make the corrections. I tell him all the time, 'Your mistakes belong to me,' so as long as you play fast and aggressive, we can fix everything else."

 Kenny Clark , Williams' defensive tackle runningmate the past 16 games, is a three-time Pro Bowler himself and knows what it is supposed to look like.

 "Just his ability to play fast," Clark said. "Actually, I was watching the film, he's just dominant. He's just dominant in there. He does a great job of finishing, whether it's him getting TFLs or getting tackles on the running backs or finishing his rushes, getting sacks and stuff like that. He does a great job of finishing. He's a complete player. It's not much that he can't do."

 Off the field, Williams' voice has become one of the most important in the locker room. Before the Cowboys' win against the Philadelphia Eagles , Williams gave a pregame talk. He was not interested in divulging what he said or why he said it.

 "I'm going to keep that to myself," he said.

 He was voted a captain by his teammates, along with Clark, quarterback  Dak Prescott and kicker  Brandon Aubrey . He is on the player council that reports to Schottenheimer when issues arise. During the struggles of the Cowboys' defense, he has repeatedly mentioned there are more things he can do, taking accountability for the group.

 

 Inside The Star, the Cowboys' practice facility, his locker is next to Prescott's.

 "There's a guy who loves this game, loves his teammates," Prescott said. "I'm fortunate to be a locker over from him to have conversations throughout the week about leadership and how to get his side going versus our side going and what we need to do for the team.

 "One of my favorite teammates all time and super thankful for that guy, for the way that he's wired. He plays this game the right way. He loves this game the right way, and it shows. It shows every time. Every snap that he plays, he puts it out there."

 After he signed his three-year, $105 million extension in training camp, Williams spoke about his desire to make the playoffs for the first time in his career and win a Super Bowl. At 4-5, the Cowboys are still in the NFC East race , but that might be their only path to the postseason.

 If the Cowboys are to truly contend, they need Williams to continue to chase his standard.

 Williams said he is heading in "the right direction on what I want to do, what I want to be, who I want to be, how I want to affect the game. I got to continue to execute, continue to do the things I know I can do to help this defense turn around and help this team win football games."

title: Big plays by Broncos defense in late-game situations keying Denver's 7-2 start
summary: The offense has gotten a lot of the credit for the Broncos' late-game heroics, but the defense's knack for big plays is just as important.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Since the start of the 2024 NFL season, no defense has created more sacks than the  Denver Broncos  (157, 32 more than the next-best team), scored more defensive touchdowns (seven) or been better in the red zone (46.4% touchdown percentage allowed). But the numbers aren't quite as dominant through nine weeks of the 2026 season, as opponents have moved at a quicker pace and attacked more on first down to keep the Broncos from revving up their pass rush.

 Still, the Broncos' defense might have carved out a new category of excellence this season.

 During the first half of the 2026 season, this Denver defense has made the plays in the biggest moments, helping the 7-2 Broncos win six one-score games and become the NFL's premier team in crunch time.

 

 "If you look at the sideline [in those moments], everybody knows it's time to make a play," Broncos edge rusher Nik Bonitto said. "... But I feel like we all think we have more work to do and we can be so much better because we don't step back in those times, we want to be there."

 Bonitto's strip-sack and fumble recovery at the end of Sunday's win over the Carolina Panthers  -- the Broncos' fifth straight victory as they enter their bye week -- was the latest instance of Denver's defense shutting the door on its opponents. That work, in concert with quarterback Bo Nix 's late-game offensive heroics, have the Broncos in first place in the AFC West and in prime position to be the AFC's No. 1 seed for a second straight season.

 Here's a look at some of the big moments that the Broncos' defense has mustered so far in 2026.

 

 

 Week 2 vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars ( 20-13 win ) 
 The Broncos trailed the Jaguars 13-6 with 1:40 left in the third quarter, with Jacksonville facing a third-and-6 from midfield. Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence tried to hit wide receiver Parker Washington up the left sideline, but Denver cornerback Riley Moss snatched the ball away at the Broncos' 33-yard line.

 The Broncos scored on the next possession to tie the game 13-13 and went on to win by a touchdown.

 "You could see it in our eyes," said Moss, who had dropped a potential pick-six earlier in the game. "... To be honest with you, it just felt good to come down with one."

 
 

 Week 3 vs. Los Angeles Rams ( 30-26 win ) 
 The Broncos trailed 19-16 with 5:01 left in the game and the Rams were driving, facing a third-and-6 from the Denver 38-yard-line. Under pressure from edge rusher Que Robinson , Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford tried to get the ball quickly to running back Kyren Williams . Broncos' All-Pro safety Talanoa Hufanga undercut the route and took the interception 66 yards for a touchdown to put Denver ahead 23-19.

 After the teams exchanged touchdowns, with Denver going ahead on a Nix 1-yard run with 47 seconds left, Hufanga intercepted Stafford a second time. This pick came in the Broncos end zone on the last play of the game to preserve a victory on a night in which the team erased a 16-point, third-quarter deficit.

 

 "I really just came out there and felt like it was just a kids' game ... in a high school game, and it felt like a super real feeling," said Hufanga, who also had a sack against the Rams.

 
 

 Week 5 at Los Angeles Chargers ( 23-17 win ) 
 This was more about the total body of work. Down 17-10 to start the fourth quarter, the Broncos held the Chargers to 19 net yards on their last five possessions.

 On the Chargers' first four possessions of the fourth quarter, the Broncos' defense forced a punt, turned L.A. over on downs by snuffing out a fourth-and-1 Justin Herbert quarterback sneak, recovered a fumble on Zach Allen 's strip-sack and had an interception via safety Brandon Jones . Cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian called game on the fifth possession with a fourth-down sack of Herbert at the Broncos' 46 as time expired.

 
 

 Week 6 vs. Seattle Seahawks ( 17-14 win in OT ) 
 The Seahawks were six plays into their drive to open overtime and had a third-and-7 at their own 28-yard line. Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold tried to push the ball up the left sideline to wide receiver Rashid Shaheed , but McMillian, in a zone look, flashed in front of the receiver and notched the interception to give the Broncos the ball at the Seahawks' 43.

 "He kind of just threw the ball up in the hole shot," McMillian said. "He thought he had the hole shot."

 

 Denver went only 8 yards on the next three plays, but that was plenty for kicker Wil Lutz , who kicked a 53-yard field goal for the walk-off win.

 
 

 Week 8 vs. Kansas City Chiefs ( 28-24 win ) 
 The Broncos packed a game's worth of clutch plays into the final three minutes of the fourth quarter. The Chiefs, who beat the Broncos in Week 1, led 24-21 and had a third-and-2 at the Denver 30 with 2:44 to play. But linebacker Alex Singleton sacked Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes for a 6-yard loss, forcing Kansas City kicker Harrison Butker into a 54-yard field goal attempt that he missed.

 The Broncos scored two plays later to take the lead, but the Chiefs pushed themselves into a first-and-goal from the Broncos' 4-yard line with 35 seconds left. But two run stuffs -- from cornerback Pat Surtain II and safety JL Skinner -- sandwiched around a Mahomes incompletion forced by Robinson, put the Chiefs in a fourth-and-goal from the Denver 1.

 A false start nullified a game-winning touchdown and knocked the Chiefs back to the 6-yard line for another fourth-and-goal. Defensive tackle Malcolm Roach then sealed Denver's comeback win with a sack of Mahomes as the clock hit zeros.

 

 "I think sometimes, we might be more comfortable down there than in the open field," Singleton said about being backed up in a goal-to-go situation. "... Crazy at that sounds, it might be true."

 
 

 Week 9 at Carolina Panthers ( 26-21 win ) 
 Before Bonitto's heroics, the Panthers led 14-13 with a first-and-goal at the Broncos' 1-yard line with 1:35 left in the third quarter. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young tried to squeeze a pass to tight end Tommy Tremble in the back left corner of the end zone. Linebacker Justin Strnad broke up the pass as he and Tremble crashed to the ground. The ball bounced off Tremble's right forearm as he hit the ground, with Broncos safety Devon Key snatching the ball mere inches from the turf for an interception. (Denver successfully challenged the play , which was initially ruled incomplete.)

 

 Denver scored two touchdowns to seemingly take control of the game, but the Panthers responded with a touchdown of their own and were driving when Bonitto became the latest Broncos defender to be a late hero.

 "We never flinch when those situations are upon us," Key said. "... I wouldn't say it's luck."

 The Broncos have defied percentages over the past season and a half, winning 22 of 28 games -- including 16 straight one-score regular-season games. They choose to think of it as the intersection between preparation, coordinator Vance Joseph's knack for the right calls at the right time and an unwavering willingness to be at their best in those moments.

 "It's just fighting, competing," Singleton said. "... I don't know why anybody expects anything different."

title: Does Packers' Christian Watson + Matthew Golden = 3,000 yards?
summary: Watson and Golden are on pace to join a rare club of WR pairs who combined for 3,000 yards.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- No one is more relieved about the emergence of receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden than the Green Bay Packers ' custodial department.

 They no longer have to worry about cleaning up after a potential disgorgement.

 Those in charge of keeping Lambeau Field neat and tidy have been on call for the better part of the past two years -- ever since coach Matt LaFleur grew tired of being asked whether they'll ever find a No. 1 receiver again and quipped: "I want to vomit every time I hear 'number one wide receiver' to be honest with you."

 Halfway through this season, there is little question that the Packers have a WR1(a) and WR2(b) pair with Watson and Golden, who have transformed Green Bay's offense into one of the most explosive in the league despite the absence of any semblance of a running game.

 Through nine games, Watson and Golden rank third and fourth, respectively, in the NFL in receiving yards. If they keep this up, they will write themselves into the record books as one of the most productive receiving tandems in NFL history.

 Watson's 879 yards receiving puts him on pace for 1,660 yards. Golden's 783 calculates to 1,479 yards over the 17-game regular season. Combined, that's 3,139 yards.

 There have been only four pairs of teammates who combined for 3,000 receiving yards in a single season, according to Elias Sports Bureau. The most was a 3,174-yard season by the Lions duo of Brett Perriman (1,488 yards) and Herman Moore (1,686 yards) in 1995, and that was in a 16-game season.

 And there has never been a team with a pair of 1,500-yard receivers.

 

 The Packers went from not having a reliable No. 1 receiver since Davante Adams ' departure after the 2021 season, which was the last time they had a 1,000-yard receiver, to seemingly having two of them.

 "The numbers they're putting up, the plays they're making, yeah, I feel like we've got two number ones for sure," Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said this week. "But again, we don't look at it that way. We look at it as you got two great players, how can we just get them the ball, and it's a great problem to have."

 It's exactly what LaFleur and general manager Brian Gutekunst envisioned when they streamlined their receiver room in the offseason. After they let Romeo Doubs leave in free agency and traded Dontayvion Wicks , they acknowledged it was more challenging than they thought to keep so many receivers happy last season.

 

 Sunday's win over the New England Patriots validated their thinking. With Jordan Love pinpointing deep ball after deep ball, Watson and Golden had massive -- and nearly perfect -- performances. Between the two of them, they caught 17 of 18 targets. The only missed connection was a sideline pass that was just off the outstretched hand of Watson, which would've added another 35 yards or so to his total. Even without it, he caught seven passes for 174 yards and a touchdown. Golden caught all 10 passes thrown his way for 164 yards and a touchdown.

 "Christian and M.G., I mean, I looked at their stat line after the game, it was just crazy," Love said. "It's crazy to see that, and I think they're balling right now. So we just got to keep finding ways to get them the rock."

 For Golden, it's been a 180 from his rookie season last year, when he was targeted only 44 times and caught 29 passes for 361 yards without a touchdown in 14 games despite becoming the first receiver the Packers drafted in the first round since 2002. He topped those numbers by Week 5 this season. The only thing holding him back is a league-high eight drops this season, but after one of them Sunday, Love went right back to him on the next play and he caught a touchdown.

 " We talk about it all the time, we feed off each other," Golden said. "Whenever he gets going, I get going, it goes back and forth. I think when we're on the same side of the ball, it makes it even better. You gotta pick one. I know me and him, we talked about it all offseason -- we were gonna come in, do this thing and take off with it. It's just about continuing to keep going and keep winning games."

 

 Watson agreed that it's contagious.

 "However many yards he had in the first quarter, 120 or whatever it was, it only helps me, gets my energy going," said Watson of Golden, who actually had 150 yards in the first half on Sunday. "Obviously, it puts less stress on me as an individual actually out there on the field. It's definitely contagious. We're feeding off each other's energy all game. If he's making plays, I know there's plays for me to make. Obviously 10 [Love] is at the helm of it all."

 It's why running back Josh Jacobs used the same three words in separate answers to describe what Love, Watson and Golden did against the Patriots and throughout the season.

 "Oh my goodness," Jacobs said.

 It has the Packers ranked No. 2 in the NFL in passing yards per game (279.7) and Love at the top of the passing yards category with 2,618. Love also ranks third in touchdown passes (19) against only six interceptions.

 The only worry, if there is one, is that an injury to either Watson or Golden could derail an offense so dependent on that twosome. They already lost slot receiver Jayden Reed to a season-ending neck injury in Week 2.

 Which is why LaFleur put the kibosh on the double-back-flip touchdown celebration that Watson and Golden broke out on Sunday.

 "I did not see it live," LaFleur said. "I was told about it, and I said, 'Don't ever do that again, please.'"

title: Jacksonville Jaguars' Foyesade Oluokun leads the way again in Africa's Week 9 NFL exploits
summary: Foyesade Oluokun - a seasoned linebacker of Nigerian heritage - had yet another superb week in Week 9, starring for the Jacksonville Jaguars as they beat the Baltimore Ravens to go 6-2 for the NFL season.
full_text:
Foyesade Oluokun - a seasoned linebacker of Nigerian heritage - had yet another superb week in Week 9, starring for the Jacksonville Jaguars as they beat the Baltimore Ravens to go 6-2 for the NFL season.

 He continues to stand out among Africa's stars in the NFL, and there were several other stars with Nigerian ties across who also had strong performances this week - particularly defensively. Additionally, Zimbabwe's Nate Landman made big plays in the LA Rams' win over the Washington Commanders.

 Africa Player of the Week: Foyesade Oluokun (Jacksonville Jaguars) 
 

 Oluokun picks up Africa Player of the Week honors for a second successive week after making seven tackles - six of them solo - and a sack in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens.

 Oluokun sacked Joe Fagano early in the second quarter, resulting in a two-yard loss for the Ravens on third down. The Jags already led 10-3 by then, but the Ravens were looking to get a drive going to enable them to nullify that advantage, and Oluokun knocked the wind out of their sails.

 As usual, however, Oluokun's contribution throughout the win was not built on having the flashiest moments, but rather ruthless consistency and efficiency.

 The first-generation Nigerian-American has now made two sacks and two interceptions this season. He is one of only two players in the entire league to have recorded both multiple sacks and multiple interceptions - with the other being the Carolina Panthers' Devin Lloyd.

 Africa Moment of the Week: Nick Emmanwori (Seattle Seahawks) 

 Emmanwori - a safety who is reportedly the youngest of five brothers born to Nigerian parents and raised the country's flag after winning the Super Bowl last season - stopped a touchdown in the 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

 

 With just over four and a half minutes left in the fourth quarter, he forced Trey McBride to spill the ball at a crucial moment - keeping the 14-point lead intact.

 By defending Gardner Minshew's pass to McBride on fourth down, Emmanwori allowed the Seahawks to start again from their own one-yard line, and they saw out the game from there.

 That one-on-one wins Moment of the Week because it was not only a moment of instinctive brilliance from Emmanwori, but also a potentially crucial one in determining which way the game went.

 The Seahawks are now 5-4 for the season and despite not being as consistent as last season, they remain in contention.

 Honorable mentions 

 Among other stars of traceable Nigerian descent: Malik Mustapha made an impressive interception for the San Francisco 49ers in their 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Tyler Onyedim forced a fumble for the Denver Broncos in their 26-21 win over the Carolina Panthers, and Rome Odunze scored his first touchdown of the season as the Chicago Bears beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 27-24.

 Emmett Johnson, who has family roots in Liberia, scored a touchdown for the Kansas City Chiefs in a 35-12 win over the New York Jets.

 There were players with African ties who made big plays in week 9 but ultimately ended up losing. For one, Austin Ajiake (ties to Nigeria) forced a fumble for the Indianapolis Colts in their 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

 His compatriot, Josh Uche, made some big plays for the Miami Dolphins in a 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions with a sack and a pass defended. Another, Ifeatu Melifonwu, had a pass defended and a fumble reception in the Buccaneers' loss to the Bears.

 Africa-born Player Watch 

 Nate Landman - a linebacker born in Harare, Zimbabwe - was the standout African-born player in week 9. He picked up his third forced fumble of the season and is now joint-fifth in the NFL in that department, also notching up a second pass defended for 2026.

 Landman had brilliant moments throughout the game, but was not as consistent as Oluokun. While they both ended with seven tackles, Oluokun had six solo and Landman only three.

 Most importantly for Landman, however, his Rams picked up a second successive win - beating the Washington Commanders 20-13.
